claim: Testimony discourse on D&C 110, the Kirtland appearance, personal revelation, and family union; no claim on any regress/progression axis.

John W. Taylor states that what makes men as God is presiding over their own posterity 'in their turn, as our Father is now presiding over His,' with the continuation of lives given them forever — an explicit parallel between the Father's parenthood and the exalted saints' future parenthood.
quote: When the children of God understand true wealth and that which will make them as God, they will find it in presiding over their posterity in their turn, as our Father is now presiding over His, and in the fact that they have wives and children, their posterity increasing and multiplying, and the principle of the continuation of lives committed unto them for ever and ever

claim: Temple/vicarious work, tithing, and sealing; celestial exaltation mentioned only as generic reward, no axis content.
Employment, poverty, tithing, and the law of the celestial kingdom as an economic law; no axis content.
Tithing, debt, retrenchment, and missionary preparation; 'sure of eternal lives' is a bare closing formula.
Franklin D. Richards notes in passing that Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob 'have become Gods' — bare theosis, no regress, new spirit children, or divine progression.
quote: The three great patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, started with a small beginning, and revelation tells us that they have become Gods, and the promise was given to them that their seed should be as numerous as the sands upon the seashore.

claim: Lorenzo Snow grounds human deification in literal divine heredity (the infant-inherits-its-father's-capacities analogy, 'a portion of Himself'), but asserts nothing about God's own Father, God's progression, or new spirit children.
quote: There is a spiritual organism within this tabernacle, and that spiritual organism has a divinity in itself, though perhaps in an infantile state; but it has within itself the capability of improving and advancing, as the infant that receives sustenance from its mother

claim: Despite the supplied title, Lorenzo Snow speaks only of human self-improvement toward perfection, the United Order, and Jackson County; theosis appears only as generic 'be perfect even as God the Father is perfect.'
quote: It is our duty to try to be perfect, and it is our duty to improve each day, and look upon our course last week and do things better this week; do things better today than we did them yesterday, and go on and on from one degree of righteousness to another

claim: Zion, unity, and Lehi's land-of-promise prophecy; no axis content.
Testimony, the Holy Spirit, priesthood succession by revelation, and tithing; no axis content.
Francis M. Lyman says the Saints are to 'come up as He came up' and become heirs of all the Father possesses — generic theosis/joint-heirship, no regress or divine progression.
quote: we also are the sons of God, the junior brethren and the sisters of our Lord Jesus Christ, and He designs that we should come up as He came up, and accomplish what He has accomplished

claim: Joseph F. Smith on Church organization, home-building, land, and cooperative economics; no axis content.

Church President Lorenzo Snow asserts a Heavenly Mother as revealed fact ('we have a mother in the other life as well'), joined to sealed wives and children continuing and increasing in the next life.
quote: We are the offspring of God, He is our Father, and we have a mother in the other life as well—These women that are sealed to us for time and eternity will, with our children be ours in the other life, going on in honor and glory—The Lord has revealed this to us, and we know it is so

claim: Lorenzo Snow urges advancing 'toward the perfections of the Almighty' and being perfect as the Father is — generic theosis only.
quote: It certainly is possible to advance ourselves toward the perfections of the Almighty to a very considerable extent, to say the least

claim: George Q. Cannon puts the Father inside the grace-for-grace chain of reception — the Saints receive the fulness as Jesus received it, 'and Jesus received it as the Father received it' — and insists the promised equality with God is real power and dominion, not title.
quote: The Latter-day Saints are promised, if they are faithful, that they shall receive the fullness, as Jesus received it: and Jesus received it as the Father received it.

speaker: George Q. Cannon
claim: Cannon says faithful couples will inherit God's power of procreation in eternity, the power by which worlds are peopled.

Francis M. Lyman places God, Christ, and exalted humans on one ladder of principles — the same principles 'have made Him and His Son so great' and have made His posterity great — implying God's greatness is the product of principles rather than intrinsic. One clause only, no elaboration.
quote: We desire to become more acquainted with God, and with the principles that have made Him and His Son so great, and that have made so many of His posterity great men and women.

claim: Marriner W. Merrill on the Church's growth, young people marrying and colonizing, and following priesthood counsel; no axis content.
Franklin D. Richards on resurrection, marriage, and posterity in this life; 'become like Him' is generic theosis and the posterity language is earthly seed, not new spirit children.
quote: We have to come to the Father by the Lord Jesus Christ; and by His principles and instructions, to become like Him.

claim: Lorenzo Snow on two temptations (fear of opinion, withholding tithing) and the Holy Ghost as personal guide; no axis content.
Rudger Clawson on Saul, strict obedience, and tithing; no axis content.

Joseph F. Smith affirms premortal divine sonship and being 'begotten in the similitude of Christ,' but the point is resurrection and likeness to Christ, not spirit-birth mechanism or new spirit children.
quote: We are begotten in the similitude of Christ himself. We dwelt with the Father and with the Son In the beginning, as the sons and daughters of God, and at the time appointed we came to this earth to take uoon ourselves tabernacles

claim: John Henry Smith on softened public hostility and the pioneer monument; no axis content.
Lorenzo Snow on submitting the will to the Father and progressing into the life to come; generic only.
quote: In this way we shall progress and gain an experience that will be useful to us, not only in this life, but in the life to come.

claim: Lorenzo Snow rehearses the Jackson County persecutions and preaches tithing with financial tables; no axis content.

George Q. Cannon on law-governed progression through the degrees of glory, with the divine-seed formula ('the elements of Deity in their inchoate state') and God described as being in an 'exalted condition' — suggestive but never asserting God's own progression, a Father of God, or new spirit children.
quote: We have within us the elements of Deity in their inchoate state, to be developed as time passes on and as we obey the laws of God

claim: Reed Smoot's brief acceptance remarks on his call to the apostleship; no axis content.
John W. Taylor on the gifts of the Spirit (Moroni 10, 1 Cor 12) and continuing revelation; 'saved and exalted in His kingdom' is closing formula only.
Matthias F. Cowley on America, the Constitution, and Saints' civic duty; no axis content.
Heber J. Grant ties exaltation to possessing sealed wives and children in the next world — eternal family in the generic sense, with no new spirit children or mechanism.
quote: we shall be worthy to go back into the presence of our Father, and be worthy not only to receive exaltation ourselves, but also to receive our wives and our children that have been sealed unto us that we shall possess them

claim: Lorenzo Snow on personal testimony, sacrifice, and the resurrected exalted body with wives and children; the one notable touch is that the Father 'educated' Christ through trials, but nothing is claimed about God's own status.
quote: I believe that his Father had educated him, had passed him through scenes that were of a very serious character, of great trials, and he knew just what he could depend upon from the facts that were illustrated and shown by his experience

claim: John W. Taylor on sealing authority and patriarchal blessings; no axis content.
Horace S. Ensign's departing testimony before the Japan mission; no axis content.
J. Golden Kimball on spiritual gifts not being confined to office and on persevering effort; no axis content.
Anthon H. Lund on humility, class feeling, and true greatness; 'we look forward to exaltation' is generic.
Francis M. Lyman on living by the Spirit and on being developed 'to become like our Father'; generic theosis only.
quote: we come here to be developed, to be enlarged, and to become like our Father, following the example set by the Son of God

claim: Charles W. Penrose defines 'eternal lives' as everlasting increase in which exalted couples' posterity is multiplied worlds without end, and says they will pattern after the Eternal Father's works, sharing in creating worlds and extending God's dominion through space forever — the full forward chain, ten years before his measured Oct 1911 statement.
quote: only those who attain to the celestial glory, and the power and dominion and exaltation, and the gift of everlasting increase, wherein their posterity will be multiplied worlds without end, have the real gift of eternal life.

claim: Joseph F. Smith on tithing, the book of the law of the Lord, and personal testimony; no axis content.

Church President Lorenzo Snow states that the infant Jesus did not know he was the Son of God or that he had created the earth, and that his divine identity and prior glory were revealed to him progressively as he grew — a divine being passing through ignorance and gaining knowledge; he also affirms endless human increase in wisdom, power, and dominion worlds without end.
quote: When Jesus lay in the manger, a helpless infant, He knew not that He was the Son of God, and that formerly He created the earth. When the edict of Herod was issued, He knew nothing of it; He had not power to save Himself; and His father and mother had to take Him and fly into Egypt to preserve Him from the effects of that edict. Well, He grew up to manhood, and during His progress it was revealed unto Him who He was, and for what purpose He was in the world.

claim: John W. Taylor on continuing revelation and the gathering; no axis content.

At Lorenzo Snow's funeral conference John W. Taylor affirms God's own ongoing progression in the classic never-catch-up form — when you reach the position the Father occupies today, He will be that much further ahead — while recounting Snow's revelation that men may attain the perfection the Eternal Father possesses.
quote: It is true, however, that when you reach the position He occupies today, He will be that much further ahead of you, and it will still be said to you, "Be ye perfect, even as your Father in heaven is perfect."

claim: Anthon H. Lund on the perfect organization of the priesthood (Eph. 4); no axis content.
Joseph F. Smith on reorganizing the First Presidency and the offices of the priesthood; no axis content.
Joseph E. Robinson's California mission report; no axis content.
Hyrum M. Smith on God exalting His people and teaching children; 'exalt' used in the sense of raising up the Church, no axis content.
Joseph F. Smith on conduct, the golden rule, and rearing children; theosis appears only as being 'exalted to the right hand of the Father, to sit upon thrones and have dominion and power.'
quote: He designs that we shall accomplish our mission, to become conformed to the likeness and image of Jesus Christ, that, like Him, we may be without sin unto salvation, like Him we may be filled with pure intelligence, and like Him we may be exalted to the right hand of the Father, to sit upon thrones and have dominion and power in the sphere in which we shall be called to act.

claim: John Henry Smith reports on eastern missions and public sentiment; no axis content.

Hyrum M. Smith places the Saints in 'eternal and infinite progression' whose terminus is possessing all power, glory, and knowledge exactly as the Father now possesses it, and separately explains God's omniscience naturalistically by analogy to the Church's reporting hierarchy — presupposing the Father's knowledge is already complete.
quote: All things will be given to us— all power, all glory, all knowledge, even as our Father in heaven possesses it — in due time, as we are capable of receiving them.

claim: Abraham O. Woodruff on every member being a missionary, forgiveness by leaders, and gathering; no axis content.
Brigham Young Jr. on Zion's growth and the surety of the work; no axis content.
Stake report on the Uintah Stake; no axis content.
Mission report on the Sandwich Islands; no axis content.
Samoan mission report; no axis content.
Joseph F. Smith on priesthood councils and Church finances/buildings; no axis content.
Reed Smoot on colonization, religious education, and family prayer; no axis content.
Charles W. Penrose on guarding the tongue and missionary work continuing in the spirit world; no axis content.

Joseph F. Smith affirms only bare theosis and generic divine sonship — God's will is to exalt men and make them heirs of God — with no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: We believe that God's will is to exalt men; that the liberty that comes through obedience to the Gospel of Jesus Christ is the greatest measure of liberty that can come to man.

claim: Clawson invokes God's unchangeableness only as boilerplate grounding for the unchangeableness of gospel law, with no engagement of God's nature, past, or progression.
quote: This great law of faith is unchangeable. Why? Because God is unchangeable, and it belongs to the everlasting Gospel.

claim: A Sunday School statistical report whose only axis contact is a closing bare-theosis line about gaining an exaltation in the Father's kingdom.
quote: I know that it is true, and that if we, as Latter-day Saints and Sunday school workers will live up to its precepts, we shall gain an exaltation in our Father's kingdom.

claim: Sunday School talk on teaching children; the only axis contact is a formulaic closing wish to be exalted in the celestial kingdom.
quote: And, finally, may we be redeemed, saved and exalted with the sanctified in the celestial kingdom of our Father, is my humble prayer for us all, in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: George Albert Smith asserts generic divine offspring/image language against evolution but specifies no mechanism, Heavenly Mother, or chain.
quote: No matter if scientists and great men of the world shall proclaim that we have evolved from the lower order of animals, the witness of the Spirit to you, my brethren and sisters, is that you are the offspring of the Lord, that the spirits which inhabit your bodies are immortal, and that in due time, if you are faithful, you will go back to the presence of that God who gave you life.

claim: A missionary report from Scandinavia whose only axis contact is the generic statement that gospel principles are calculated to exalt mankind.
quote: We say that the principles of the gospel are true, and are calculated to exalt mankind, to bless the people, and to bring salvation to the human family, if they will obey it.

claim: Report on the Bureau of Information and Temple Block symbolism; touches exaltation only as a generic goal of obedience, with no claim about God's nature or origin.
quote: Those are signs indicating our abode .here and how we have come to fill our probation upon this earth and perfect ourselves that we may regain an exaltation in the presence of our God, "And how?" by obeying the laws that God has revealed.

claim: Survey of the Church's growth, missions, and temple work; the only axis contact is generic welding-link/sealing language with no claim about God's nature, origin, or progression.
quote: the uniting together of the past with the present, of the fathers with the children, is one of the most stupendous facts connected with this great work of the Lord in the last days.

claim: Robinson argues for the corporeal personality of God against pantheism, affirming generic spirit-fatherhood, divine sonship of Christ in the flesh, and bare theosis, but asserts no divine ancestry, no divine progression, and no spirit-offspring mechanism.
quote: It seems to me that if men would study these things as they are written, and not spiritualize them, they could not help but admit the fact that we are in the image of our Father; that as He is the father of our spirits He is also the Father of Jesus, the Christ.

claim: Sermon on peculiarity and forgiveness closing with generic eternal-family assurance and a stock 'saved and exalted' phrase; no specific claim on any axis.
quote: The assurance that our relationship here as parents and children, as husbands and wives will continue in heaven, and that this is but the beginning of a great and glorious kingdom that our Father has destined we shall inherit on the other side, fills us with hope and joy.

claim: Whitney asserts a premortal existence and foreordination of Israel and of prophets, but only in generic 'children of God before Abraham was born' terms with no ancestry, mechanism, Heavenly Mother, or progression content.
quote: What is the significance of sending into the world a chosen race of spirits, called upon earth the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but known to us to have been the children of God before Abraham was born?

claim: Nibley invokes universal divine fatherhood and human brotherhood as a social-equality argument, with no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or spirit birth.
quote: We are — as the children of the world are — children of God.

claim: Richards uses only bare salvation/exaltation language plus a passing remark that the Savior reached perfection by the gospel plan; no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: It is the plan by which our Savior lived, by which He reached perfection, through which He ascended to the Father, and is now enjoying the glories of His kingdom.

claim: George Albert Smith expounds D&C 93 to affirm that a member of the Godhead progressed — the Son did not receive a fulness at once but grew grace for grace. Conflation risk: this is the Son's completed mortal progression, not the Father's ongoing progression; it is one of the two standard proof-texts of the D debate.
quote: We find in the same section the information that the Savior did not receive a fulness at once, but grace was given Him for grace.

claim: Teasdale speaks only generically of attaining the highest degree of glory and of the sons and daughters of God, with no claim about God's nature, ancestry, or eternal increase.
quote: They attained the highest honor which man can secure in this life, for they had been true and faithful to God, and finally laid down their lives for their testimony, and hence was insured to them eternal life and happiness, even the highest degree of glory possible for man to attain.

claim: The official 1907 Address to the World states man's divine sonship, premortal spirit existence, endless progression, and eternal marriage only in generic public-facing terms; it softens the Church's political and polygamy positions but says nothing specific about divine ancestry, God's own progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: We hold that man is verily the child of God, formed in His image, endowed with divine attributes, and possessing power to rise from the gross desires of earth to the ennobling aspirations of heaven.

claim: Richards treats exaltation only as the generic reward of gospel obedience, with no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: There is no way to exaltation except by yielding obedience to the principles which are taught by the Latter-day Saints, revealed in this last dispensation through the prophet Joseph Smith, the same principles, in the same order, as they were taught by Jesus Himself, having the same saving power.

claim: Bare theosis ("become like unto Him") plus a stock scriptural immutability epithet for the Father, with no doctrinal development on any axis.
quote: I invoke the favor and protecting care, the mercy, forgiveness and loving kindness of the Father of light, in whom there is no variableness nor shadow of turning, upon all the Latter-day Saints, and upon all the honest in heart and upright in all the world.

claim: George Albert Smith uses generic pre-existence and becoming-like-God language in a Word of Wisdom sermon without any specific axis claim.
quote: I look upon the Word of Wisdom as kind advice of our Father in heaven, who desires to see His children become more like Him.

claim: Joseph F. Smith's opening address uses 'exaltation in the kingdom of God' and 'children of our Father' only as generic salvation language in a sermon on unity, individual repentance, and vicarious work for the unrepentant dead.
quote: Men can only be saved and exalted in the kingdom of God in righteousness, therefore we must repent of our sins, and walk in the light as Christ is in the light, that His blood may cleanse us from all sins, and that we may have fellowship with God and receive of His glory and exaltation.

claim: Hyrum M. Smith defends God's corporeal personality and man's creation in God's image, and insists no revealed doctrine has ever been receded from, but makes no claim on divine ancestry, divine progression, or spirit birth.
quote: Thus they could truthfully testify to others that God lives, and that we are His children, created in His image.

claim: Hart argues we must know God's attributes and that God and Christ are tangible resurrected personages, but makes no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring; exaltation appears only as a bare term.
quote: we have learned through that principle that God is a tangible being, as is also His Son, that He lives and that He hears and answers the petitions of His children

speaker: Heber C. Iverson
claim: Heber C. Iverson explicitly teaches that the hymn's doctrine is that Latter-day Saints have a Mother in Heaven and mothers of their spirits.
Counsel on preaching peaceably and on the breadth of God's work; touches exaltation only as a generic future law and says nothing specific about divine ancestry, progression, or spirit birth.
quote: but also, by the promulgation of other great and important laws pertaining to man's exaltation and glory.

claim: A stake report whose only axis contact is the generic sealed-family point that parents cannot enjoy exaltation without their children — no generative exaltation, ancestry, or progression claim.
quote: I was impressed sometime ago by a thought that was expressed by the Prophet Joseph Smith, that we cannot be perfect without our children; we cannot enjoy exaltation in the kingdom of God without our children.

claim: Whitney quotes Joseph Smith that God 'found Himself in the midst of spirits and glory' and was preeminent 'because He was more intelligent,' then instituted the laws by which the rest might advance like Himself — grounding God's godhood in comparative intelligence among co-eternal spirits rather than in absolute, uncaused deity.
quote: In the beginning, God, finding Himself in the midst of spirits and glory, because He was more intelligent, saw proper to institute laws whereby the rest might advance like Himself.

claim: Mission report; only generic references to going "on unto perfection" and to a hoped-for resurrection and exaltation, with no content on ancestry, divine progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: Such a man will be entitled to the resurrection and exaltation which you and I are all seeking for.

claim: A mission report whose only axis contact is generic exaltation-as-goal language and a generic hope to come to know the Father as He knows us.
quote: He holds out His hand with charity towards us, and will save us if we will, as Brother Pratt has told us this afternoon, work for our salvation, work for our exaltation.

claim: Mission report on personal accountability and the spirit world; the only axis contact is a stock benedictory request to be exalted in God's kingdom.
quote: Brethren and sisters, may God bless you in His mercy, comfort you in your homes in the future have His hand ever extended to bless the Saints, save our children, and keep us for ever and ever in His holy keeping, and save and exalt us in His kingdom, I ask it in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: California mission report; the only axis contact is generic joint-heirship with Christ and a passing reference to premortal existence.
quote: Jesus is the Christ, the begotten son of the Father, and our elder brother with whom we are joint heirs to all the powers and prerogatives of our Father's kingdom,if we but keep the faith.

claim: George Albert Smith invokes 'great exaltation' and 'sons of God' generically in a Word of Wisdom and temperance sermon.
quote: Can we expect to be able to keep a higher law, and be able to attain great exaltation, if we fail to keep this simple requirement?

claim: Joseph F. Smith uses only generic salvation-and-exaltation language plus a stock James 1:17 epithet for the Father's constancy; no assertion about divine ancestry, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: There is no hope of everlasting life but through obedience to the law that has been affixed by the Father of Life, "with whom there is no variableness, neither shadow of turning;" and there is no other way by which we may obtain that light and exaltation.

claim: Sermon on gratitude and service to God; closes with a stock promise of salvation and exaltation and makes no specific claim on any axis.
quote: The Lord has done His part by us ; let us see to it that we do our part, that we may be entitled to salvation and exaltation in His presence that is promised to the faithful, I ask it through Jesus Christ.

claim: Bennion mentions only bare exaltation in God's kingdom as the reward of obedience; no divine-ancestry, progression, spirit-offspring, or mechanism content.
quote: By the principles which God, the eternal Father, has established, you and I may gain an exaltation in His kingdom, where He and His Son dwell.

claim: Roberts expounds the D&C 3 immutability text at length, but applies it entirely to institutional and personal honesty (the post-Manifesto controversy), not to God's nature, progression, or ancestry.
quote: neither doth He vary from that which He hath said; therefore His paths are straight, and His course is one eternal round.

claim: Whitney refers in passing to God having made and peopled, redeemed, and glorified millions of earths; no ancestry, progression, or spirit-birth claim, but the plurality-of-worlds motif travels with the cluster (adjudicator raised from PASSING to keep it findable).
quote: the all-wise Being who made this earth — and who had made millions of earths like it, and had peopled them, redeemed them, and glorified them.

claim: Callis asserts that God's own work is unending and — with an explicit disclaimer that he does not mean to be sacrilegious — that this ongoing work is what accounts for God's greatness, then extends progression under law to immortal beings.
quote: What! The Lord God at work? Yes — and I believe that it is this work in which He is engaged that accounts for His greatness, and I do not mean to be sacrilegious in saying that.

claim: Ivins mentions exaltation only as returning to the Father's presence through faith plus works, with no claim about God's nature, ancestry, or eternal increase.
quote: While we believe that these first doctrines of the Church are fundamental and indispensable, we do not regard them as sufficient to assure exaltation to the presence of our Father in heaven, but that they must be accompanied by works; that we must do the will of the Father, keep the commandments which He has given us, in order that we may be brought back into His presence.

claim: Brimhall assumes premortal intelligences/spirits as the Father's children and credits the Father with sacrifice and labor for them, but asserts nothing about divine ancestry, progression, staging, or eternal increase.
quote: He could not comprehend that the work of his Father had been one of sacrifice, one of toil, one of labor, mental and physical, for the good of the spirits there.

claim: Administrative conference report (statistics, tithing, amusements, the end of plural marriage); the only axis contact is the stock phrase about being saved or exalted in the kingdom of God.
quote: No other name, under heaven, is given, but that of Jesus Christ, by which you can be saved or exalted in the Kingdom of God.

claim: Penrose teaches that sealed couples resurrect as sexed beings whose posterity has no end, that those not so sealed 'are not numbered among the Gods,' and closes by grounding human spirit and body in divinely established 'laws of generation' that had no beginning and will have no end — a beginningless generative order that reaches backward past the Father, though he does not name a grandfather explicitly (conflation risk: the beginninglessness attaches to the laws, not stated of a chain of begetters).
quote: I know that He lives, that he is our Father, the Father of our spirits ; that our spirits are, in form, like unto Him, and our bodies have been made to conform to the spirit, under the laws of generation that God has established, to which there was no beginning, and of which there shall be no end.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith's Sabbath sermon uses 'exaltation in His kingdom' only as a bare reward-term; nothing on divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: They are not given merely to please the Lord, but to make us better men and women, and worthy of salvation and exaltation in His kingdom.

claim: Penrose's closing testimony asserts literal bodily paternity of Christ ('in the body as well as in the Spirit') and closes with the stock D&C 132 thrones-and-dominions formula, but both are unargued testimony boilerplate with no mechanism, no Mother, no chain, and no new spirit children (downgraded from SUBSTANTIVE by the adjudicator for consistency with the Robinson 1905 literal-paternity call).
quote: I bear testimony to this congregation, as I have had the privilege of doing many times in years that are past, that God, the Maker of the universe, is our Father, the Father of our spirits ; that Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified on Mount Calvary, is His Son, in the body as well as in the Spirit, and that He is our Savior.

claim: Rich preaches theosis with some color — exalted men will know and control the elements as Christ did and be made like unto God, kings and priests — but asserts nothing about divine ancestry, God's own progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: Faith will take immortal men into the presence of God; not only that, but will make them like unto God, exalt them as kings and priests in the celestial kingdom of our heavenly Father.

claim: Joseph F. Smith argues from procreative necessity to divine embodiment: a spirit could not have begotten a physical Christ, therefore the Father is bodily 'the exact resemblance' of the Son. Conflation risk: the begetting in view is Christ's mortal conception, not premortal spirit birth; no regress, no Mother, no progression, no new spirit children.
quote: and, that God, the Father, is like His Son; that it would be inconsistent and impossible for a spirit to beget a man like Christ, and therefore the Father and the Son are the exact resemblance of each other.

claim: This is the known Penrose Oct 1911 discourse: resurrected husbands and wives come forth as parents of children with the gift of endless, perpetual increase in worlds without end, and Christ, having passed through these conditions, is now exalted exactly like the Father.
quote: though death may part them, yet in the resurrection they shall come forth to be husband and wife, to be parents of children, to have the gift of endless, perpetual increase, the beginning of their kingdom and their glory in worlds without end.

claim: Richards mentions salvation and exaltation generically and names the hymn 'O, my Father' only as a musical example, with no doctrinal content on any axis.
quote: my love of the truth and my appreciation of what the Lord has done for me and for you in providing a means of salvation and exaltation in His presence were greatly stimulated.

claim: Herrick uses 'exalt' only in the generic sense of gospel principles saving the individual; the talk is about exemplary living and missionary anecdotes.
quote: We have the principles which will exalt and save us if we will rightly live them.

claim: Salvation-for-the-dead address; exaltation and sealing of generations appear only as generic goals, with no claim about godhood, spirit offspring, or divine origins.
quote: So we cannot be saved and exalted in the kingdom of God unless we have .within our hearts the desire to do this work and perform it, so far as it is within our power on behalf of our dead.
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith

claim: Eternal-marriage and resurrection address: sealed couples keep their identity forever and the faithful gather an Abrahamic posterity, but the increase described is sealed mortal posterity, not new spirit children.
quote: In obedience to this work, in the Gospel of Jesus Christ, I shall gather around me my family, my children, my children's children until they become as numerous as the seed of Abraham, or as countless as the sands upon the sea shore.
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Decalogue/Constitution address; the only axis contact is the generic statement that God is the Father of our spirits.
quote: He is the Father of our spirits, the Father of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, who is our God ; and we shall not have any other before Him.
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: No axis content
speaker: Joseph E. Robinson

claim: No axis content
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith

claim: Temple-and-genealogy address; exaltation is named only as the destination secured by vicarious ordinances.
quote: He can impart to them authority and power without which they never can pass to their exaltation.
speaker: David H. Cannon

claim: No axis content
speaker: Joseph W. McMurrin

claim: Missionary-duty address that lists eternal progression among true doctrines but never says who progresses or how far.
quote: The gift of the Holy Ghost teaches me that not only is baptism and repentance and faith essential to salvation — and true — but it teaches me that the pre-existence of spirits, the resurrection from the dead, the doctrines of eternal judgment and the other glorious principles, including the doctrine of eternal progression, are true.
speaker: Charles A. Callis

claim: No axis content
speaker: Alonzo A. Hinckley

claim: No axis content
speaker: Frank Y. Taylor

claim: Richards states the Snow couplet from the pulpit and adds a mechanism: God became what He is by the practice of virtue and righteousness and by obedience unto law and authority, and man may become as He is on the same principle; he also calls the Saints God's literal spirit-born offspring who inherit His very attributes.
quote: We believe that as we are now God once was, and by the practice of virtue and righteousness, by obedience unto law and authority, He has become what He is, and as He is, man may become, on the same principle.
speaker: George F. Richards

claim: Brief closing testimony; exaltation appears only in the formulaic promise of a reward in the Father's kingdom.
quote: Through faithfulness we shall overcome all things and receive an exaltation in our Father's Kingdom.
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith

claim: Obedience/tithing/temple address; exaltation in the Father's presence is the generic petition of prayer, with no claim about godhood or offspring.
quote: When we kneel down at night, as I trust all who are Saints do, and pour out our hearts in gratitude to our Father, in whose image we are created, we ask him among other things to grant that we may be eternally exalted in His presence with a fulness of glory.
speaker: David H. Cannon

claim: States the couple-precondition of exaltation (neither man nor woman can be exalted alone) but asserts nothing about spirit offspring or divine origins.
quote: The house of the Lord is a house of order and not a house of confusion; and that means, that the man is not without the woman in the Lord, neither is the woman without the man in the Lord; and that no man can be saved and exalted in the kingdom of God without the woman, and no woman can reach perfection and exaltation in the kingdom of God, alone.
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Word of Wisdom and modesty address; exaltation and the unbreakable sealing covenant are affirmed in general terms only.
quote: Christ has opened up to the world, through faith and obedience, this hope of everlasting life and exaltation in His glorious kingdom.
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Stake-report testimony; bare theosis in the closing hope of exaltation.
quote: above all it has that saving power that will enable us to attain eternal life, if we are faithful unto the end.
speaker: John W. Ham

claim: Address on obeying Church leaders; exaltation and 'eternal life and progression' occur only as generic rewards.
quote: I know that Jesus is the Christ, that He did come into the world to redeem the world from sin, and that men through acceptance of the principles of the Gospel — those principles which were taught at the opening of our conference — will receive a reward and an exaltation in the kingdom of our God.
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith

claim: Whitney defines exaltation as salvation added upon, says embodiment makes souls capable of endless increase and everlasting progression, speaks of the work 'men or gods' engage in, and then lists explicit limits on God (He cannot create from nothing and cannot be in all places at once in His own person).
quote: And yet, through that transgression, and the consequent fall of man, God's purpose was accomplished, in the coming of a race of spirits to take upon themselves bodies, thus becoming souls, capable of endless increase and everlasting progression.
speaker: Orson F. Whitney

claim: Reads D&C 132 on the new and everlasting covenant, including the passage that those who reject it 'are not gods, but are angels of God,' but adds only generic exposition on eternal marriage.
quote: "For these angels did not abide my law, therefore they cannot be enlarged, but remain separately and singly, without exaltation, in their saved condition, to all eternity, and from henceforth are not gods, but are angels of God, for ever and ever."
speaker: Rudger Clawson

claim: Ballard says the law stands above the Father Himself — the Father could not abridge or void it, complied with it Himself, and 'through compliance with it became God' — an explicit claim that God attained Godhood by obedience to law rather than always having been God.
quote: He complied with it Himself, and through compliance with it became God.
speaker: Melvin J. Ballard

claim: Generic theosis in a closing doxology: we are made in God's image and placed here to become like the Only Begotten and inherit glory and exaltation; no increase, regress, or progression claim.
quote: since He has placed us here that we may become like unto His only begotten Son and to inherit the glory, exaltation and reward provided for God's own children
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Richards gives a mechanism for theosis - literal spirit birth transmits to us the very attributes and qualities of Deity 'which in our Father in heaven are pefect and make Him what He is,' making us 'gods in embryo' who will be like Him 'in very deed' - and in the same testimony describes the Father as a glorified being 'whose power has no limitations' (the D-denial pole).
quote: while we are now but gods in embryo, having been born of God, in His likeness, in His image, and having received from Him the attributes of Deity, through perfecting those attributes in time and in eternity we will be like Him in very deed, and be glorified with him in His kingdom
speaker: George F. Richards

claim: A single generic phrase about Church activity leading to salvation and the exaltation of the soul; the talk is about work, virtue, and the vitality of the Saints.
quote: for attainment of salvation and the exaltation of his soul
speaker: Heber Q. Hale

claim: Universal theosis stated generically as a ground for charity - every soul born into the world may eventually become divine in power and attributes; no spirit offspring, regress, or divine progression.
quote: We could not believe that every soul that has been born into the world may become eventually, through endeavor and the things accomplished, divine in his power and attributes
speaker: Richard W. Young

claim: Richards ties temple sealing to a specific postmortem outcome: a worthy husband and wife sealed for eternity keep that relationship beyond the grave and 'shall have eternal increase in the kingdom of God,' while all other unions will not be recognized; he closes by referring to the plan instituted 'by the Gods' (plural).
quote: those relationships maintained and recognized in the life beyond, and that they shall have eternal increase in the kingdom of God
speaker: George F. Richards

claim: Robinson asserts that in the eons to come the exalted will come into a fulness of divinity and 'build yet other mansions for our Father, thus adding to His glory' - an explicit claim that God's glory increases through His children's endless progression, alongside a perpetual family home.
quote: With Him and in His presence, in the eons of years yet to come, we shall come into a fulness of divinity, and build yet other mansions for our Father, thus adding to His glory as we add to the glory and perpetuity of our own homes and families.
speaker: Joseph E. Robinson

claim: Smoot states as the distinguishing LDS conception of God that the God we worship has passed through all the experience we are now passing through and is an exalted being - the King Follett past-mortality claim, with no backward chain of Fathers asserted (trap 1).
quote: the God whom we worship has passed through all the experience that we are now passing through. He is an exalted being, a personality
speaker: Reed Smoot

claim: A tithing and faithfulness sermon; exaltation appears only as the generic hope of being saved and exalted through Christ by obedience.
quote: we have hope in Christ and an assurance that we will be saved and exalted through Him, by keeping His laws and commandments
speaker: George F. Richards

claim: A creedal recital: the just exalted to thrones, powers, and principalities; the eternity of the marriage covenant; the family relation continuing in the life to come - all generic, with no eternal increase or spirit offspring asserted.
quote: I believe that the just will be exalted to thrones and powers and principalities in the kingdom of God
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith

claim: In his closing address Joseph F. Smith qualifies theosis by sphere: he does not expect anyone to become in mortality 'quite so perfect as God is perfect,' but says we may become as perfect in our sphere as God is in His higher and more exalted sphere - an explicit graded limiting of 'be ye perfect.'
quote: we may become as perfect in our sphere as God is perfect in His higher and more exalted sphere
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Temple marriage urged so couples may meet beyond the veil and continue their relationships; celestial versus terrestrial reward framing, but no increase, offspring, or divine-progression claim.
quote: so that when they go beyond they may meet their life's companions, and continue there the relationships that have been so dear to them in life
speaker: Henry H. Blood

claim: Closing benedictory promise of eternal life and continued progress throughout all eternity for the faithful - endless human progression stated generically, with no content about God's own progression.
quote: come home and enjoy eternal life and continued progress throughout all eternity
speaker: George A. Smith

claim: A report-and-exhortation address on peace, prayer, and following counsel; exaltation appears only as a closing generic promise of salvation and exaltation in the world to come.
quote: we will have great joy in time, and salvation and exaltation in the world to come
speaker: Francis M. Lyman

claim: Brief testimony; the only axis touch is the generic hope of reaching glory and exaltation in the Father's kingdom by following the leaders.
quote: we will be able to reach that glory and exaltation in our Father's kingdom for which we have started
speaker: Lars P. Overson

claim: Joseph F. Smith states the D-denial pole - God's power reaches all His creations, 'His knowledge comprehends them all ... and He knows all,' and He cannot be in two places as an individual - while also saying of the departed prophets 'They have advanced ; we are advancing' and hoping one day to know as God knows.
quote: His power extends to all His creations, and His knowledge comprehends them all, and He governs them all and He knows all
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Penrose says the Father 'was an exalted man who had passed through all things' Christ later passed through and calls this 'a repetition of the things that had been done from remote, eternal ages' for all the worlds God has created - a backward-recursive framing verging on C-infinite; the same discourse is an extended correction rejecting the Adam-God teaching and also denies that Christ was a resurrected being before mortality.
quote: He was an exalted man who had passed through all things that Jesus Christ, His Beloved Son, afterwards passed through. It was a repetition of the things that had been done from remote, eternal ages, the great plan of salvation for all the people of all the worlds that God has created.
speaker: Charles W. Penrose

claim: A sermon on selfishness, missionary duty, and prohibition; God is called the Father of our spirits who placed us here to gain an exaltation, but the exaltation language stays wholly generic.
quote: the testimony of the Father of our spirits, the God who created us and who has placed us here that we might gain an exaltation
speaker: George Albert Smith

claim: Defines immortality and eternal life and says the righteous may attain a fulness of the glory of God, but adds no specific claim about godhood, parenthood, or divine origins.
quote: The revelations of the Lord indicate to us the height, depth and grandeur of the glory of God to which the righteous may attain.
speaker: George F. Richards

claim: Testimony talk on knowing God lives through the Holy Spirit; exaltation appears only in the closing formula.
quote: That we may be saved and exalted with Him and His Son and the righteous who have fought the good fight and endured to the end, I humbly pray, in the name of Jesus Christ.
speaker: Joseph E. Cardon

claim: Prohibition and Word of Wisdom address; the only axis contact is the boilerplate closing wish for exaltation in the kingdom.
quote: May God help us to keep His commandments, to live the lives of Latter-day Saints, that we may be worthy of an exaltation in His Kingdom, is my prayer and desire, and I ask it in the name of Jesus.
speaker: Heber J. Grant

claim: Asserts that no man can be exalted alone (the couple-precondition of exaltation) and restates the Father's tangible body, but never asserts spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: the knowledge we now possess that a man cannot be exalted into the presence of God and the full enjoyment of his glory, alone.
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Administrative address on eliminating inactivity among the priesthood; exaltation appears once as a generic goal of labor.
quote: Do all that you can for it will take all that we can do to work out our salvation and exaltation in the kingdom of God.
speaker: Francis M. Lyman

claim: Missionary-work address; exaltation in the celestial kingdom is asserted generically as the reward for doing one's part.
quote: I know that we are identified with the Church that our heavenly Father has restored in this day and if we will do our part, we will gain exaltation in his celestial kingdom.
speaker: George Albert Smith

claim: No axis content
speaker: Walter P. Monson

claim: No axis content
speaker: Hyrum M. Smith

claim: Extended defense of a literal bodily resurrection, including that the Father has a body of flesh and bones; exaltation appears only in the closing hope.
quote: Then I know that we shall arise again, to be exalted and to sit in glory in the celestial kingdom of our God
speaker: Hyrum M. Smith

claim: No axis content
speaker: George A. Smith

claim: No axis content
speaker: Anthony W. Ivins

claim: No axis content
speaker: James E. Talmage

claim: Sabbath-habit and ward-teaching address closing with a generic promise of exaltation in the kingdom of God.
quote: If we continue to do this, we shall finally gain an exaltation in the kingdom of God.
speaker: Alma Merrill

claim: Affirms premortal existence and that the faithful receive exaltation, power, and principalities, and clarifies that D&C 132 is about the eternal order of marriage rather than only plural marriage, but asserts no spirit offspring, regress, or divine progression.
quote: I feel that the sphere beyond is the reward of eternal life to those who are faithful, exaltation, power, principalities and blessings and privileges beyond our power to understand.
speaker: Wm C. Parkinson

claim: Develops a 'dual parentage' doctrine in which God is the literal Father of the spirit and the mortal father the father of the body, and says obedience will exalt us, but makes no claim about new spirit children, God's own ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: the Father of my spirit and the father of my body having entered into a copartnership in this dual soul composed of the body and the spirit.
speaker: M. H. Smart

claim: Growth-of-the-Church and tithing address; glory and exaltation are named generically as what God has in store for his children.
quote: may prepare ourselves to go back and enjoy that glory and exaltation which he has in store for his children
speaker: Lars P. Oveson

claim: Signs-of-the-times and priesthood-attendance address; says the priesthood is the power by which men are exalted as heirs of the kingdom, without specifying what exaltation consists of.
quote: you can lift yourselves above the groveling events of this earth, and be exalted, heirs to the kingdom of God.
speaker: William T. Jack

claim: Conference-opening address on the truth of the work, past Church presidents, Sabbath, Word of Wisdom, and tithing; exaltation appears only as the generic end of God's plan for his obedient children.
quote: The Almighty, in the beginning, never devised a plan for the redemption of his childern that was not true, that was not efficacious, that would not be effectual in the accomplishment of his purpose to bring to pass the final exaltation into the kingdom and the enjoyment of his presence, of all his children who would obey his laws and keep his commandments.
speaker: Joseph F. Smith

claim: Generic priesthood-exaltation sermon: the faithful receive 'all that my Father hath' and 'glory and exaltation,' with no claim about God's nature, ancestry, or progression.
quote: If he advances no further than the office of an elder but is faithful in the magnifying of his calling, he will enter into his glory and exaltation and will receive the fulness of which the record speaks.

claim: Wartime comfort sermon on patriarchal blessings; the only axis contact is the bare phrase that the gospel is the plan of redemption and exaltation.
quote: I know that we have the gospel of Jesus Christ and that it is the true plan of human redemption and exaltation.

claim: Reporting a conversation with a Christian Scientist, Hart states flatly as the Latter-day Saint position that God is a material, exalted, immortal man who was once as we are, and that men may attain the heights he has attained.
quote: As Latter-day Saints — 'Mormons,' as we are known — we believe that God is a material being, an exalted, immortal man. He was once as we are, and it is possible for us to attain to the heights that he has now attained ; and we base our faith on the circumstance that transpired in the death, crucifixion, and resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

claim: Ballard quotes the Lorenzo Snow couplet and then explicitly narrows it — denying that it means all men will become what God is, and restricting 'becoming what God is' to those who gain celestial glory.
quote: I don't understand that the "Mormon" doctrine, announced by President Lorenzo Snow, and so often quoted by us : "As God is man may become, and as man is God once was," means that all men are going to become what God is, not by any manner of means.

claim: Sermon on sustaining leaders and on mortality as a probationary sphere leading to exaltation; exaltation language is entirely generic.
quote: I tell you that men and women are led up to exaltation by obedience to the laws and ordinances of the gospel.

claim: Wide-ranging counsel sermon (home production, salvation for the dead, teaching children); the only axis contact is generic — a personal God who is 'the Father of their spirits' and the aim to 'come up to the standard occupied by our Eternal Father.'
quote: The boundless universe is before us all to learn and to live and to come up to the standard occupied by our Eternal Father and to be fit for his society.

claim: Brief closing remarks on the parable of the rich fool; exaltation appears only as a summary phrase for the plan of salvation.
quote: I trust we are beyond and above this dreadful condition, and that we do know that our Redeemer lives, and that we have put on Christ, and have adopted his glorious plan of redemption and salvation and exaltation beyond the grave.

claim: Testimony of the restoration and of prophecy fulfilled; 'exaltation in the kingdom of God' is used only as a generic goal.
quote: I know, beyond any doubt whatever, that this is the work of God, that we are engaged in a work that will save and exalt us in the kingdom of our Father in heaven if we will do our part.

claim: Appeal to use Church auxiliary organizations to reach youth; 'the exaltation and the glory that we hope for' is the only axis contact and is entirely generic.
quote: The spiritual refreshing that we get from a consideration of these great truths cannot be effectual in bringing the exaltation and the glory that we hope for, unless we incorporate them into our lives.

claim: Sermon on worship, humility, and rearing children; touches theosis only through the generic Matthean call to be perfect as the Father is perfect and to make men 'Godlike.'
quote: All these things we aim to do that we may finally be perfect, even as our Father in heaven is perfect.

claim: Wartime address on justice, peace terms, and German restitution; no content on any axis.
quote: God hasten the day when Justice shall rule in the world and selfishness shall hide its head and stand subdued, for selfishness is always destructive of self, and the only hope of the great and goodly race, the German people, is that contrition of heart shall be given them, till they are willing to make restitution.

claim: Draws the salvation/exaltation distinction and preaches salvation for the dead, but says nothing specific about what exaltation consists of beyond returning to God's presence.
quote: But the plan of salvation holds out, through the gospel, a code of laws that can not only bring unto the children of men salvation, but will bring unto them exaltation, and bring them back into the presence of our Father, from whence we came.

claim: Prohibition endorsement plus a sermon on personal revelation; 'become like our Father in heaven' is a single generic clause.
quote: I bear witness to you that the Lord has again spoken from heaven, has revealed his gospel, organized his Church, and placed therein every blessing and gift that is necessary for us to develop and grow and become like our Father in heaven, even in the gospel within the Church.

claim: Grant's first remarks as President — a pledge of faithful service and a charge to exercise priesthood by persuasion; no axis content.
quote: With the help of the Lord that is exactly how I shall administer, to the best of my ability, the priesthood of God that has come to me.

claim: Tribute to past Presidents, quoting Joseph F. Smith's 1902 address on being conformed to Christ's likeness and exalted to thrones and dominions — thrones-and-dominions language without any claim about God's nature or origin.
quote: He designs that we shall accomplish our mission to become conformed to the likeness and image of Jesus Christ that like him we may be without sin unto salvation, and like him we may be filled with pure intelligence, and like him we may be exalted to the right hand of the Father to sit upon thrones and have dominions and power in the sphere in which we shall be called to act.

claim: Tribute to Joseph F. Smith plus a missionary charge; 'exalted' is used only of Christ's and Joseph Smith's present station, with no doctrinal claim.
quote: I know that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and is exalted at the right hand of his Father.

claim: Personal reminiscences of Joseph F. Smith's kindness and sensitivity to the Spirit; no axis content.
quote: I revere his memory. I revere him for many things.

claim: League of Nations, labor liberty, and the ensign of peace; exaltation appears once as a generic outcome of receiving the gospel.
quote: It is the cause of God and of humanity, his children, for it involves the happiness and salvation of many millions, and the exaltation of those among them who received the gospel in the flesh, or afterwards received it in its fulness, and prepared themselves thereby to associate with the good and the true and the best of mankind.

claim: Charge to parents and prospective missionaries; exaltation named only as the generic reward of a clean life.
quote: It will mean salvation and exaltation to any soul who will live that kind of a life, and endure.

claim: Post-war reflection favoring the League of Nations; closes with a generic triad of glory, exaltation, and eternal life.
quote: If the world would obey the gospel and adopt these principles and live by them it would mean peace to individuals, peace to the world, and would bring to men glory, exaltation and eternal life.

claim: Whitney reads Genesis 1:27 as teaching not only that God is in the form of man but that Latter-day Saints have a Mother in heaven as well as a Father, in whose image male and female are made.
quote: This is equivalent to saying that God is in the form of man, and that we have a Mother as well as a Father in heaven, in whose image or likeness we are, male and female.

claim: Recounts Book of Mormon baptism and sacrament narratives and the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood, closing with D&C 121; no axis content.
quote: I testify to you that Joseph Smith was and is a Prophet of God, that Jesus Christ is the Savior of the World, that his Church is on the earth today and that this people are led by a prophet of God.

claim: Systematic sermon on the gospel governing health, wealth, society, government, and happiness; exaltation appears once as a generic hereafter reward.
quote: It sets forth a rule of action for our conduct that leads us to happiness and joy in this life, as well as to exaltation in the life to come.

claim: Sermon on law, order, and the persistence of habits after death; refers in passing to a premortal council in which 'God called the gods together,' but makes no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or origin.
quote: It is true that in the beginning, while in the spirit world, there was a council held; and you remember that God called the gods together.

claim: Report on the California mission and the first principles taught by missionaries; no axis content.
quote: We are trying to bear record of the truth, but we are not building up men. We are in no way trying to exalt the names of men, but we are trying to advance and magnify the gospel of the Redeemer, which is the power of God unto salvation.

claim: Sermon on charity and refraining from judgment; exaltation and the D&C 121 'everlasting dominion' promise appear only as generic outcomes.
quote: But if we have in our hearts the love of God and the love of our fellow men, nothwithstanding our weaknesses, there is hope for us; we may be redeemed from sin and be brought to a knowledge of the truth; we may be exalted and brought back into the presence of our Father.

claim: Penrose, in the First Presidency, carefully qualifies the anthropomorphic God ('we do not say that God is a man; he is a perfected man'), affirms literal spirit begetting of all humanity, and — in the year the Lectures on Faith were dropped from the Doctrine and Covenants — publicly reframes Lecture Fifth's two-personage Godhead as superseded by the 1843 revelation.
quote: We do not say that God is a man; he is a perfected man; he is exalted above all mankind, and he is our Father. He begat us in our original being, as his sons and daughters, verily and literally and truly.

claim: Mission report arguing that preaching power comes from the Spirit and charity, not learning; no axis content ('exalted above measure' is Paul quoted on his thorn in the flesh).
quote: It is that love of God, which overshadows and transcends the love of everything else in the world whether it be personal glory and honor, wealth or fame.

claim: Sermon on unchanging fundamentals, the perfection of Church organization, and missionary duty; touches Christ's unique divine paternity and generic exaltation, but makes no claim about God's own origin or progression.
quote: So we accept him as the Only Begotten of the Father in the flesh, as explained by President Penrose, the only one who has dwelt in the flesh who had a Father who was immortal.

claim: Historical/testimonial address on Nauvoo, the westward migration, coming hard times, and 1 Nephi 14; 'exalted his work' is figurative and there is no axis content.
quote: He is just giving us today all we can stand. He will not give us more unless we will prove to him, that we will serve him no matter what may come.

claim: Philosophy-of-history address on the vindication of the Saints, the fate of nations, and the gathering of Judah; 'an exalted place in the world' is figurative and there is no axis content.
quote: A steadfast devotion to these same principles, along with industry, education, and true religion, are certain to lift a people to an exalted place in the world.

claim: Anti-cigarette campaign, thrift, sacrament attendance, and an engineer's 'Specifications for a Man'; no axis content.
quote: Let us, I pray, make our lives conform with these exalted specifications, and all the glorious principles of the perfect gospel of Jesus Christ.

claim: Priesthood sermon that makes eternal marriage a prerequisite for a woman's exaltation and glory, but stops short of any claim about heavenly parenthood, offspring, or God's own nature.
quote: Every woman in the Church, of mature age, and worthiness, who is ambitious to attain to exaltation and glory hereafter should be married, should be sealed to a man for time and all eternity.

claim: Defines eternal life as God's own kind of life and receiving 'all that the Father hath,' but frames it entirely as celestial glory attained by keeping commandments — no claim about God's origin, progression, or heavenly parenthood.
quote: No indeed, it means coming forth in the resurrection from the dead, crowned with immortality and eternal life, and in that term we mean an exalted life in the presence of God, for he is indeed the very Eternal One and eternal life means his life, to live with him forevermore, to receive from him, as has been promised, "all that the Father hath".

claim: Report on European missions plus a doctrinal core: God is a personal, embodied being in whose image we are made and by whom our spirits were begotten — all stated generically, with no claim about God's origin or progression.
quote: If you have received the witness that has come to me and know as I know that our heavenly Father has revealed himself to the children of men, that he is a personal God, that we are created in his image, that our spirits were begotten by him, that he has given us an opportunity to dwell upon the earth to receive a physical tabernacle, in order that we may be prepared to return into his presence and live eternally with him, I say, if you have received that assurance, then you have a foundation upon which you may build your faith.

claim: Eastern States mission report and testimony; salvation and exaltation named only as the generic result of living the gospel.
quote: We are being saved temporally just as fast as we live the laws pertaining to our temporal salvation ; and if we continue therein we shall earn our salvation and exaltation in God's kingdom.

claim: Sermon on the obligations attaching to every association from marriage to citizenship to the Church; exaltation appears only as the generic design of the gospel.
quote: It is the Church and kingdom of God ... formed under a supreme law, the perfect law of liberty, the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ, designed to exalt the children of God, to liberate them from the bondage of sin.

claim: The Presiding Bishop states flatly that no man, whatever his office, can be exalted without his wife — a strong marriage-required-for-exaltation claim, but with no mention of heavenly parenthood, offspring, or God's own nature.
quote: We lords of creation, that we never can attain to exaltation in the Kingdom of God, not one of us, without our wives. It does not matter whether he is a president of the Church or what office he holds, or how great his Priesthood or calling: "The man is not without the woman in the Lord," in the Church, in the Kingdom of God. He can't be redeemed or exalted in the presence of God without his wife.

claim: Overflow-meeting testimony on the growth and influence of the Church; exaltation and eternal life named once, generically. Notable only as a negative datum — Widtsoe, the author of A Rational Theology, says nothing here about God's progression.
quote: I know that in the light of the gospel, man may walk in happiness and in enjoyment throughout this life's journey, and ultimately, when we shall pass through the great veil, we may enjoy exaltation and eternal life throughout the endless ages.

claim: Temple-work sermon quoting D&C 76 on the fixity of the degrees of glory ('worlds without end'), but the language is quoted scripture applied to salvation for the dead, with no original claim about increase, parenthood, or God's nature.
quote: "And they shall be servants of the Most High, but where God and Christ dwell they cannot come, worlds without end." (Doctrine and Covenants 76: 112)

claim: BORDERLINE: Smith names as the doctrinal payload of the First Vision that 'our Father in heaven and his Son Jesus Christ are glorified men' — a flat anthropomorphic claim, but stated of God's present nature only, with no assertion that the Father was once mortal, has a Father, or continues to progress; classed REDUNDANT under the taxonomy's conflation traps, flagged here for adjudication.
quote: From that boy who, at fourteen years of age, beheld the Father and the Son, there came that wonderful message that our Father in heaven and his Son Jesus Christ are glorified men.

claim: Sermon on the home as the basic institution; grounds the hope of exaltation in family relationships and in taking one's posterity along hereafter, but says nothing about heavenly parenthood, new offspring, or God's nature.
quote: Attention has already been called to the fact that we base our very hope for exaltation and eternal life upon those relationships that lie at the basis of home. No man, whatever his accomplishments may be, can, in my judgment, be said to have achieved success in this life if, when he goes hence he may not take his posterity with him.

claim: Western States mission report defending the divinity and sonship of Christ against modernist critics; no axis content.
quote: We know that His is the only name given under heaven by and through which salvation can come to the children of men.

claim: Survey of the Bible urging its study; the only axis contact is the generic 'if we would be like him, we must become intelligent.'
quote: He will not condone ignorance, for "the glory of God is intelligence," and if we would be like him, we must become intelligent.

claim: Sermon on teaching by the Spirit, the world's need of the gospel, and charity toward other churches; refers generically to God's children 'created in His image, whose spirits were created by Him' and to working out an eternal exaltation.
quote: From that nucleus of six has developed a Church of hundreds of thousands of our Father's children, created in His image, whose spirits were created by Him, who have earned the right to come into the world to work out their eternal exaltation.

claim: Richards states as the Church's message to the world that the Father is a resurrected being with a body of flesh and bones — the word 'resurrected' applied to the Father presupposes His past mortality and death, going beyond ordinary anthropomorphism.
quote: For almost a century, we have been trying to convince the world that God has spoken from the heavens ; that He has revealed Himself and His Son, Jesus Christ, and that the Father is indeed a resurrected immortal and glorified being, having a body of flesh and bones, and spirit like His Son after His resurrection.

claim: Address on self-control, tithing, and moral integrity; touches the reframing axis only obliquely by describing the surrender of plural marriage as an act of law-abiding rather than a doctrinal revision, and says nothing about exaltation, parenthood, or God's nature.
quote: We resigned the practice of a principle that God had revealed, when we gave it up. What for? In order to obey the law of the land.

claim: Brief stake-president testimony on drawing near to the Lord in hard times; 'saved and exalted' is a single generic clause.
quote: We as a people will be saved and exalted just in proportion to our obedience to the laws and ordinances of the gospel as promulgated from time to time by the mouthpiece of God upon the earth, and his associates.

claim: Warning sermon from 1 Nephi 14 and Ether 2 on the Gentiles' conditional tenure of this land; affirms a literal tangible God whose child he is and that men may be exalted as Christ was, but entirely without claims about God's origin, progression, or heavenly parenthood.
quote: I know that I am created in the image of the Lord, my Maker; that I know that Jesus Christ came into the world, and was and is the Son of God, that He taught wisdom to men, whereby they may be, as He has again been, exalted into the celestial kingdom of our Father in heaven.

claim: Canadian Mission report on newspaper agitation and the perfection of Church organization; exaltation appears only in the closing formula.
quote: God help us to trust in Him, and hold fast to the iron rod, that through His mercy and His power, we shall receive salvation and exaltation in His kingdom.

claim: Sermon on humility as the source of priesthood power, built on D&C 121; 'everlasting dominion' and 'eternal life in His kingdom' are quoted or generic, with no axis claim.
quote: Whosoever will lose self in the Lord's great cause, consecrate every energy of his being, every sympathy ot his soul, to its up-building, and, that with an eye single to the glory of God, shall find eternal life in His kingdom.

claim: Sermon distinguishing broad-mindedness from heresy and defending orthodoxy; no axis content ('exalted principles' is adjectival, 'utmost progression' is about human understanding of truth).
quote: I am orthodox ; I am proud to be orthodox. I cannot conceive how one who is impregnated with the great mission of this work in the earth, and who is convinced of its truth and divinity, can be other than orthodox.

claim: Law-and-government sermon opening on Moses 1:39; glosses eternal life as 'exaltation with our heavenly Father' and calls the gospel 'the plan of the Gods,' but neither phrase carries a claim about divine ancestry, progression, or heavenly parenthood.
quote: The gospel is the plan of the Gods for the existence of this earth and of man upon it, of their fall, of their redemption, and of their glorification.

claim: Long survey of gospel dispensations from Genesis to the Restoration, framed as the contest between God and Satan; the only axis contact is the generic 'man is the offspring of Deity, created in the image of God.'
quote: One teaching that man is the offspring of Deity, created in the image of God, and placed upon the earth endowed with intelligence to discern between good and evil, between right and wrong.

claim: Sermon on obedience to law and the divine founding of America; quotes D&C 130:18-21 on intelligence rising with us and names celestial glory as the reward of the first principles, all generically.
quote: "And if a person gains more knowledge and intelligence in this life, through his diligence and obedience, than another, he will have so much the advantage in the world to come."

claim: Bare theosis in passing: obedience to gospel principles is elevating and may lead to exaltation in the life to come.
quote: Our people should learn to love the principles and requirements of the gospel, and should love to conform to them according to the spirit in which they are given for they are all elevating, even in this life, and through them, in their completeness, we may be exalted in the life to come.

claim: Church-and-state address; exaltation appears only as a generic term for the end of divine law.
quote: our obligation to the church, which represents divine law, given for the purpose of preparing men for future glory and exaltation in the kingdom of heaven ?

claim: Faith-and-works sermon; exaltation named as the reward of doing rather than hearing, with no content on its mechanism.
quote: it is the doing of the things which the Lord, through his gospel, has prescribed by which we may attain to glory and exaltation.

claim: Insists God is a personal, embodied being in whose image man is created, but makes no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or begetting spirit children after this life.
quote: Show me the man, regardless of who he is, who can prove from holy writ that God our eternal Father is without form) and without body, parts or passions.

claim: God creates innumerable worlds in order to people them with His sons and daughters, but the sermon stays on the worth of souls and generic exaltation, never asserting divine ancestry, God's own progression, or new spirit children begotten by exalted humans.
quote: The Father is creating worlds for the purpose of peopling them — placing upon them his sons and his daughters.

claim: Youth work, missions, and Scouting; no content on any axis (the only 'exalted' is 'exalted ambition' in sons and daughters).
quote: What we want is sons and daughters strong in the power to resist; sons and daughters with high ideals and exalted ambition, for these 'give joy and satisfaction which no amount of money can purchase.

claim: Conference opening report (temples, missions, Word of Wisdom); no axis content — 'exalted position' refers to the U.S. presidency.
quote: I am grateful that the high office he held until his death is now occupied by a man who I believe with all my heart is worthy of that exalted position.

claim: Bare theosis: following the Brethren yields salvation and exaltation in the Father's kingdom.
quote: if we will listen to their words that we will gain a salvation and exaltation in our Father's kingdom

claim: Argues species fixity against evolution and ties eternal marriage to priesthood authority carried into eternity, but the exaltation reference is generic and no claim is made about begetting spirit children or divine ancestry.
quote: I fancy we could not rise to glory and exaltation without the blessings imparted unto us in the temples of God .

claim: Mission report; exaltation named only as the reward of gospel obedience.
quote: only through obedience to the laws and ordinances of the gospel, as taught by the Latter-day Saints we can hope for an entrance into and an exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: Testimony of Christ and Joseph Smith; no axis content (the one 'exalted' is Acts 5:31 applied to Christ).
quote: Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Savior, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.

claim: Fundamentalism/modernism sermon; resurrection is said to lead on to exaltation and glory, but nothing specific on any axis.
quote: We go down into our graves, we expect to come up out of our graves, and take up these bodies purified, and go on to exaltation and glory.

claim: Temple sealing is required for a fulness of glory and exaltation, and those who attain that glory receive a continuation of the seeds forever — an eternal increase; Richards then presses the point pastorally, warning that refusing children forfeits an offered blessing.
quote: We are informed that such marriages as are performed in our temples are necessary for men and women to obtain a fulness of glory and exaltation in the celestial kingdom of our Father in Heaven; for those who attain to that glory are to have a continuation of the seeds, forever, an eternal increase.

claim: Testimony and pioneer reminiscence; no axis content ('exalted position' means the pulpit).
quote: In this exalted position, being honored to stand before this magnificent congregation, I hope to voice the sentiments of my heart in the testimony which I hope to bear to you today.

claim: Restoration testimony; exaltation named generically as what the restored keys and authority make possible.
quote: restored the gospel in all its purity, with all its power, keys, and authority -- all that is necessary for the salvation, and exaltation of all the children of men.

speaker: Rudger Clawson
claim: Rudger Clawson states that the premortal family included a mother in heaven alongside the Father and spirit children.
Aaronic Priesthood sermon; closes with a bare wish for exaltation with the Master.
quote: I pray, my brethren and sisters, that we may be found faithful and diligent to the end, that when the time shall come for us to be called by the Master we will be found worthy of an exaltation with him.

claim: Missionary-work testimony; exaltation named only as the eternal outcome of accepting the gospel.
quote: bring them not only salvation here in time, but salvation and exaltation in all eternity.

claim: Calls the priesthood 'in very deed a portion of Godhood' by which men most nearly approach God, but this is deification-by-participation language with no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: It is in very deed a portion of Godhood, and you men and boys who are privileged to possess it more nearly approach God in your Priesthood than in any other attribute or way.
