claim: Practical sermon on health, finances, and education as part of salvation; no axis content ('exalted' used of the listener's mood).
quote: And so when we return to our homes, exalted, refreshed, rested, ready to take up the battle of life again, — we shall encounter practical problems.

claim: Short testimony; bare theosis in the closing promise.
quote: if we will live up to our duties, brethren and sisters, there is no power can stay our progress, our advancement and our exaltation finally in the kingdom of our God.

claim: Courage-of-convictions sermon; exaltation is the named goal but is given no doctrinal content.
quote: I must reach that standard if I would be accounted worthy of an exaltation with him in our Father's kingdom.

claim: Apostasy-and-restoration narrative; priesthood restored for the redemption and exaltation of God's children, with no further specification.
quote: again revealed to the earth with the power of the holy Priesthood to officiate in these ordinances for the redemption and exaltation of God's children.

claim: Anti-Darwinian sermon asserting literal divine parentage of the human spirit — tracing human ancestry back to an 'eternal Sire' who gave us bodies premortally — but the chain runs only from man up to God, never past Him, and nothing is said about exalted humans begetting spirits.
quote: Is it not reasonable to believe that God foreordained prophets, as we read in Jeremiah, first chapter, and that we were in an ante-mortal state able to act and to perform works . under the direction of our eternal Father -- the Father of our spirits -- who gave us bodies in the beginning, and that our parentage goes back to that eternal Sire who governs and controls the destinies of men, according to their obedience to law?

claim: Whitney stages pre-mortal existence in tiers — 'lesser intelligences' who then 'became God's sons and daughters' and won the right to bodies and so to become souls 'capable of endless increase' — and calls the gospel 'the plan of eternal progression, designed by the wisdom of the Gods before the foundation of the world.'
quote: What Latter-day Saint can doubt that Adam was among "the noble and great," referred to in the Book of Abraham as "rulers," chosen before they were born into this world to play leading parts in the divine drama having as its purpose the uplift and promotion of "the lesser intelligences" who became God's sons and daughters -- the end designed by the all-wise, all-benevolent Creator from the beginning?

claim: Pre-existence and Abrahamic lineage sermon; spirits differed in the pre-mortal world and some fell short of their own progress and exaltation, but nothing is specified about the mechanism or about God's own status.
quote: there were some who were evil and had many weaknesses, and fell far short of doing the things that were necessary for their own progress arid exaltation.

claim: Apologetic answering the charge that Latter-day Saints are not Christians; no axis content (the 'exalted' instances are Acts 5:31 of Christ and the Sermon on the Mount's warning against self-exaltation).
quote: That we should not seek to exalt ourselves, for he who exalteth himself shall be abased.

claim: Easter sermon on the literal resurrection that reasons from Christ's persisting personality to the conclusion that God is 'a resurrected personal being' — a corporeality argument whose subject is most naturally Christ-as-God, not a claim that the Father passed through mortality; flagged as a conflation risk rather than a King Follett datum.
quote: Christ's personality, as his divinity, persisted after death. This being true, then God is beyond all doubt a resurrected personal being.

claim: Testimony on inspiration and agency; exaltation named only to insist that membership alone does not secure it.
quote: And I realize, too, that simply to be a member of this Church does not mean exaltation; for just as surely as the Lord has given us our free agency, just so surely must we exercise that agency in the right direction.

claim: Sermon on the gift of the Holy Ghost and the pre-mortal council; mortality is said to develop divine qualities so we may become like our Maker, but this is bare theosis with no mechanism, offspring, or divine-ancestry claim.
quote: But it meant an opportunity of development, of education, of growth of those qualities that are divine, to make us like our Maker, that we might become like him in very deed; for as we were told, our eyes were opened to the knowledge of good and evil.

claim: Priesthood-and-home sermon repeating his 'portion of Godhood' formula; deification-by-participation language only.
quote: The very holding of this power charges every man who is blessed with it to live more nearly a godlike life, for he holds a portion of Godhood itself.

claim: Anti-creedal sermon describing the Father and Son as separate glorified, immortal, exalted beings and endorsing Beecher's 'glorified form of a glorified man' as a picture of God; embodiment and anthropomorphism only, with no claim about God's past, His progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: It is a marvel, when Joseph Smith came forth with this story of his vision and the declaration that the Father and the Son were separate individuals, glorified, immortal beings, and exalted, stating that they had appeared to him and had told him that these religionists had gone astray, and that he was going to restore his true gospel, that our parents accepted the story and believed in it?

claim: Asserts a physical tabernacle is prerequisite to exaltation and that Christ needed a body 'like unto the one that his Father has' — divine corporeality only, with no claim about the Father's past, His progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: When we were born we received a physical tabernacle without which we could not be exalted in the presence of our heavenly Father. It was necessary for his Son Jesus Christ to be born into the world in order that he, too, might have a tabernacle like unto the one that his Father has.

claim: Answers press attacks on the Church; exaltation appears once as part of the generic salvation formula.
quote: We bear witness to the world that there is no other name under heaven, nor is there any other means by which man can attain to glory, exaltation and eternal life except through the medium of Christ our Lord.

claim: States that God's Godhood is an acquired status — 'The reason God is God is because he has acquired all for which we are laboring' — and that the purpose of gospel capacity-building is that we 'may learn how to be gods ourselves' and 'rise to be what he is,' with the human soul called 'a god in embryo.'
quote: The reason God is God is because he has acquired all for which we are laboring.

claim: Standard plan-of-salvation sermon (God is the Father of our spirits; we lived with him before); exaltation named only as conditional on endurance.
quote: Salvation and exaltation are promised only upon condition that we remain faithful unto the end.

claim: Mission-report sermon; exaltation named as the fruit of obedience to Christ's plan, with no further content.
quote: that he would offer his only begotten Son to redeem mankind, to introduce into the world a plan of life and salvation, that by yielding obedience to it we would receive our exaltation in God's celestial kingdom.

claim: Family-history testimony reading John Smith's 1851 patriarchal statement; no axis content ('exalted stations' means Church office).
quote: If the Presidency and Twelve who are now living had not been servants to the cause when Joseph lived, they would not have been worthy to fill the exalted stations which they now occupy ;

claim: Whitney's sharpest statement of the staged pre-existence: eternal 'lesser intelligences' were already there and the Creator 'found himself' in their midst at the beginning, after which they became His sons and daughters first in the spirit and then in the flesh — intelligences are thus uncreated and spirit-birth is a later, distinct stage.
quote: It was instituted in the heavens before the earth was formed, as the means of uplift and promotion for "the lesser intelligences," in the midst of whom the Great Creator found himself at the beginning, and who became his sons and daughters, first in the spirit and afterwards in the flesh.

claim: Missionary-conviction address; the only axis-adjacent line is a quoted aphorism that Christianity's influence will make men Godlike.
quote: "It is an ever-broadening wave of direct personal influence, destined ultimately to touch and transform all men, so that they like Jesus shall become Godlike."

claim: Sermon on Daniel's kingdom and the destruction of false systems; exaltation named twice as the reward of walking in the full light, with no doctrinal specification.
quote: I haven't the privilege of discarding some of the principles of the gospel and believing others, and then feel that I am entitled to the full blessings of salvation and exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: Convert's testimony; closes with a bare promise of exaltation for the faithful.
quote: It is my testimony that this is the work of the Lord, and that it will grow, and that we will be exalted in our Father's kingdom if we continue faithful and do our bit by taking part in this great organization.

claim: Missionary-joy sermon; exaltation named as the highest attainment available through Christ, with no content beyond that.
quote: It is the only way whereby we may attain the highest exaltation that the Savior of mankind intended that those who followed him should enjoy.

claim: Sermon on salvation and why creeds differ; affirms that we are literally born sons and daughters of God and that exaltation means dwelling where the Father and Son dwell, but adds nothing beyond the standard premise.
quote: What a glorious truth, what a glorious principle, that we are born sons and daughters of God.

claim: Three-part sermon on attitudes, knowledge, and habits; exaltation named as the Latter-day Saint's stated aim in life.
quote: The answer of the Latter-day Saints could possibly be something like this, "To be saved and exalted in God's kingdom is the prime aim and object of life."

claim: First-principles sermon calling the gospel 'the power of God unto exaltation,' designed 'by the wisdom of the Gods' before the world was, and holding that gospel principles are uncreated and self-existent; the 'endless increase' language is glossed by 'eternal progression,' so it reads as growth rather than offspring.
quote: "Adam fell that men might be" — that a race of spirits might tabernacle in the flesh, and thus become souls, capable of endless increase, of eternal progression and exaltation.

claim: Pre-mortal council sermon calling us God's 'begotten children in the spirit' and promising exaltation for those who prove themselves; standard premise plus bare theosis.
quote: We stood in the presence of our Maker; we stood in the presence of our Eternal Father — his begotten children in the spirit.

claim: Biographical tribute to Heber C. Kimball; the only axis-adjacent line is a closing wish to be saved and exalted.
quote: I sustain and uphold the hands of the priesthood, and I desire, as you do, to be saved and exalted in the presence of God. which, if I know anything, I know it must be the greatest gift of God to his children.

claim: Mission-field sermon on conversion and the Word of Wisdom; exaltation named once as what unrepentance forfeits.
quote: I fear we are still barring ourselves from participation in an ultimate exaltation in the kingdom of our Father in heaven.

claim: Whitney argues from the image-of-God premise to a Mother in Heaven — 'what more reasonable than the conclusion that we have a Mother as well as a Father in Heaven, in whose likeness we are, male and female?' — while also declaring God 'an exalted, glorified Man,' insisting matter and spirit are uncreatable and eternal, and describing souls as 'capable of endless increase and eternal progression.'
quote: And if men and women are indeed God's children, his sons and daughters, what more reasonable than the conclusion that we have a Mother as well as a Father in Heaven, in whose likeness we are, male and female?

claim: Anti-creedal sermon contrasting Presbyterian and Anglican formulas with the First Vision; God has body and parts like man and is 'a glorified and exalted being,' but nothing is claimed about His past, His progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: He saw that God the Eternal Father is a personage, having body and parts like unto man, or in other words that man is really and actually in his image and likeness, but that God is an immortal being, a glorified and exalted being, and that his Son Jesus Christ is like him.

claim: Isaiah 2 applied to America's prayerful founders, the First Vision, and interwar peace efforts; no axis content ('exalted above the hills' is the mountain of the Lord's house).
quote: The mountain of the Lord's house is established in the top of the mountains. It is here, exalted above the hills.

claim: Sermon on the Spirit of truth quoting the D&C 93 'grace for grace' text and concluding that a man filled with that light 'becomes like unto God' — bare theosis, applied to man only, with nothing said about God's own course.
quote: A man with that intelligence can be taken on and on until he receives a fulness of glory, and he becomes like unto God.

claim: Mission-travel report answering Brisbane on man's origin and destiny; quotes Abraham 3 on the pre-organized intelligences without developing it, and closes with bare theosis.
quote: It not only saves — it exalts men to where God and Christ dwell in the fulness of Celestial Glory.

claim: Sermon on faith, hope, and charity that calls these divine attributes inherited 'from our divine parents' as 'the offspring of Deity' — a passing plural rather than a developed Heavenly Mother claim; the file also carries David A. Smith's address on missionary preparation, which has no axis content.
quote: We inherit them from our divine parents. They are divine attributes transmitted to us as the offspring of Deity.

claim: Extended reading of Moses 1, 4, and 5 contrasting God's work with Satan's; the recited text includes 'there is no God beside me' but Richards makes no application of it to plurality of Gods, and exaltation appears only as the alternative to condemnation.
quote: These two great influences being wrought upon us, and having our agency, we are to be judged by the exercise of this agency, whether we exercise it in righteousness unto salvation and exaltation or in unrighteousness unto our condemnation.

claim: Richards affirms God is an embodied, glorified man in whose image we are made and whose attributes we inherited through spiritual birth and may perfect, but asserts no divine ancestry, no progression of God, and no begetting of new spirit children.
quote: If Henry Ward Beecher and the Latter-day Saints find in the scriptures evidence that God is a divine and glorified man, why cannot and why do not other religionists do likewise?

claim: A Word of Wisdom talk that closes with generic exaltation-in-the-celestial-kingdom language and a bare image-of-God statement; no regress, progression, spirit-birth, or Heavenly Mother content.
quote: For the purpose of our existence in the earth is an exaltation in the celestial kingdom of our Heavenly Father, and I know that the only way that may be is through faithful service rendered in obedience to his laws.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith affirms generic exaltation as sons and joint heirs with Christ, with no claim about God's own history, ancestry, or progression.
quote: I believe that our Father has prepared a place for every man according to his works and worthiness, but only through obedience to his laws in their fulness will men come back into the presence of the Father and the Son to receive an exaltation as sons and joint heirs with Jesus Christ.

claim: Talmage describes graded salvation culminating in exaltation and says God holds Himself accountable to law, but asserts nothing about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit birth.
quote: Salvation is graded ever upward until it culminates in the glorious condition of exaltation.

claim: Willard Young distinguishes salvation from exaltation in the celestial kingdom but says nothing about divine ancestry, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: If he complies with the requirements for exaltation in the celestial kingdom he will have eternal life and exaltation in that kingdom.

claim: A sermon on idolatry, Sabbath, and tithing whose only axis contact is one bare reference to exaltation in the kingdom of God.
quote: We cannot advance in the knowledge of God and the things pertaining to exaltation in the kingdom of God unless we have that training.

claim: Whitney frames the gospel as a system by which God exalts his sons and daughters and shares the empire of the universe with them, but this is bare theosis with no divine-ancestry, divine-progression, or spirit-begetting claim.
quote: The Gospel is a great system of laws, a code of eternal principles, whereby the omnipotent and all-wise Creator, our Father in Heaven, proposes to lift fallen mankind, his sons and daughters, and not only save them, but exalt them to his glorious presence, and so far as they prove worthy and capable, share with them the empire of the universe.

claim: Rey L. Pratt describes the Father seen in the First Vision as 'a man, an exalted man' in whose image humanity is formed, but makes no claim about God's prior mortality, ancestry, or progression.
quote: He came from out that forest and boldly declared, to the day of his death, that there came into his presence a being after whose image and in whose likeness he was formed, — in other words, a man, an exalted man, who proclaimed himself to be the Father of another being there also in his presence, they two being in the same likeness ; and he gave command to Joseph Smith to listen to the voice of his Son.

claim: George F. Richards affirms that those exalted in the celestial kingdom have eternal increase and a continuation of the seeds forever, and argues this is impossible unless the husband-wife marriage relation literally continues in the other world.
quote: Those who attain to a fulness of glory m the celestial kingdom are to have an eternal increase and a continuation of the seeds forever. It is unthinkable and untrue that that condition could exist without sustaining the marriage relation in the other world.

claim: A testimony on revelation, searching the scriptures, and avoiding deception; the only axis contact is a bare mention that Christ brought salvation and exaltation to the faithful.
quote: He brought salvation and exaltation to all who are willing to accept in faithfulness all of his teachings.

claim: Wells says humans inherited divine attributes from 'our divine parents' and may develop them to God-like proportions in a post-mortal 'Great University,' but this is generic theosis plus human (not divine) progression, with no regress, spirit-begetting, or Heavenly Mother claim.
quote: It is one of those divine attributes which we have inherited with all the others from our divine parents.

claim: Stephen L Richards refers generically to the exaltation God holds out to the faithful as a return to His presence; no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or eternal increase.
quote: Oh, I think so much of the glorious light of truth that God has given, of the great exaltation that he holds out to us, to come back into his presence by living the Gospel, that I would not have our youth miss the epitome of it all, the prime essentials, the glorious hopes, the rewards, the promises, that await those who live the truth and conform their lives to the teachings of the Church.

claim: Bare word-level mention of exaltation inside a Brigham Young quotation about tithing sacrifice; no divine-ancestry, progression, or spirit-birth content anywhere in the sermon.
quote: We are doing this for our own happiness, welfare and exaltation, and Inobody's else.

claim: David A. Smith refers in passing to exaltation in the kingdom as the reward of faith and works, with no ancestry, progression, or offspring content.
quote: He knew that the salvation of man, that which would secure for him exaltation in the kingdom of our Lord, must be obtained by faith and work.

claim: Frames premortal first estate / mortal probation / exaltation in generic Abraham 3 terms with no claim about spirit birth, heavenly parents, divine ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: We are here to be tried, to be proved, to be found worthy of exaltation in the kingdom of God, to go back into his presence, to become his sons and his daughters, entitled to a fulness, or to receive other rewards, according to works of lesser degree of importance.

claim: Elmer G. Peterson uses 'the exaltation of mankind' only as a rhetorical flourish for the social fruits of gospel living; no theological claim on any axis.
quote: These things have appealed to me as I have analyzed the doctrines of the Church which constitute a philosophy, aside from the religion, the spirituality that is in the doctrine, a philosophy so profound that it is beyond the comprehension of the most learned and the most intellectual, a profound formula for the living of clean and wholesome lives, and infinitely more than that of course, a formula by means of which a people united together can preserve and build up those great strengths that hold out the possibility of finding expression in the fulfilment of the teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, the exaltation of mankind.

claim: Generic conditional exaltation tied to obedience (specifically tithing); no divine ancestry, no God's progression, no spirit-birth or heavenly-parent content.
quote: If we obtain an exaltation in the kingdom of God we must observe and keep all the laws of God, and that includes the law of the tithe.

claim: Two-stage plan only (pre-existent spirits -> mortal living souls); names no third estate and terminates the 'destiny of man' in a fulness of joy, not godhood or increase.
quote: That is the destiny of man. But that destiny must be clearly understood by man and must be followed in order that he shall rise to exaltation and glory such as that which has been received by the Savior and his apostles of old and the Saints who have been resurrected who will enter into glory and exaltation.

claim: A warning sermon on the adversary and parental duty; axis contact is limited to bare celestial-kingdom/exaltation and 'sons and daughters of the living God' language.
quote: If we do that, then we have no promise of exaltation.

claim: A Word of Wisdom address; the only axis contact is a quoted John Taylor passage about being prepared for a place among the Gods, plus a Woodruff quote on being led to exaltation and glory — both bare theosis with no ancestry, progression, or spirit-birth content.
quote: and that we might be enabled to comprehend those principles w hich are calculated to elevate, to exalt and ennoble mankind, and to prepare them for the enjoyment of a place among the Gods in the eternal worlds.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith teaches bare theosis - the obedient become sons and daughters of God, receive all the Father has, and may become like Him - with no statement about God's own past, ancestry, or spirit offspring after this life.
quote: What a glorious thought this is ! Oh, how I rejoice to know that the Lord has made this known unto us, that it is within our power to become like him !

claim: Bare theosis: exaltation in the celestial kingdom is equally available to the humblest member; nothing on regress, divine progression, or generative exaltation.
quote: The humblest member of the Church, if he keeps the commandments of God, will obtain an exaltation just as much as any other man in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Richards uses plural-Gods council language and asserts a long pre-mortal spirit life culminating in eternal life and exaltation, but asserts no divine ancestry, divine progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: The Prophet Joseph tells us that we were all present in the council of heaven ; that we sat in council with the Gods ; that we saw the plan of salvation made, and the Savior chosen and appointed, and we sanctioned it.

claim: A mission report whose only axis contact is a closing reference to eventual exaltation in the celestial kingdom.
quote: and that only we ourselves can hinder our progress and our advancement, and, eventually, our joy and exaltation in the celestial kingdom of God.

claim: J. Reuben Clark names exaltation and human eternal progression as the great new truth of modern revelation, but says nothing about God's own progression, ancestry, or generative exaltation.
quote: Without that we would be as dead bodies and dead spirits, shut off from true salvation, from exaltation, from eternal progression, the great new truth of modem revelation.

claim: Closing benediction promises generic exaltation to the faithful; the address is otherwise reminiscence, anti-spiritualism, and a tribute to mothers with no axis content.
quote: May God help us to follow the teaching and example of our mothers who are true Latter-day Saints, and there will be an eternity of joy and an exaltation in store for each and every one of us

claim: Speaks of a premortal 'plan of the Gods' in the councils of heaven leading to man's exaltation, but the plural-Gods phrase is stock Abrahamic idiom and the talk makes no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: To enlarge a little upon that definition, we might say that the Gospel is the plan of the Gods in the councils of heaven before the world was, for the existence of this earth upon which we live and of man upon the earth, for the fall of man, for the redemption of man, and his exaltation through the atoning blood of Jesus Christ and obedience unto the laws and ordinances of the Gospel, and for the glorification of the earth.

claim: Clawson lays out an explicit three-estate chain (spirit preexistence -> mortality -> resurrected glorification), states flatly that God is a glorified man and anticipates the charge of blasphemy, and says temple marriage perpetuates the principle of fatherhood and motherhood into eternity.
quote: But now, we are told in the Book of Genesis, that man is in the image of God, is made like him with this difference, that God is a glorified being, a glorified man.

claim: George F. Richards calls God 'an immortal, glorified and exalted Being' and says men are His children 'born of him in the spirit,' but asserts nothing about God's own past, a Father of the Father, divine progression, or exalted couples begetting spirit children.
quote: They know not God, the Eternal Father, as we know him to be, an immortal, glorified and exalted Being, of all power and love to perfection; and his Son Jesus Christ.

claim: Stock spirit-parentage plus the two Abraham-3 estates; the Genesis 4:1 analogy is drawn to conclude that mortal children come from the Lord, not that spirits are viviparously born.
quote: From this we may readily conclude that all children born to earthly parents are gotten from the Lord and that earthly fathers and mothers are the divinely appointed guardians of God's children, for he is the Father of our spirits.

claim: Closing line promises glory and exaltation to the faithful; the discourse is otherwise about history vindicating Joseph Smith's defenders and condemning his opponents.
quote: God help us to do our part and to keep from everything that would lead us from the main path, which if we continue to travel in shall bring us to glory and exaltation

claim: Richards describes God as an embodied immortal being who is glorified and exalted and in whose image man is made, but makes no claim about God's origin, progression, or divine parentage.
quote: Mankind may now know of a certainty that the God of this world is a personage having a body of flesh and bones as tangible as the body of mortal man ; and that he is an immortal being, glorified and exalted, in whose image and likeness man is created and made ; and that the Son is in the express image of the Father.

claim: Defends an anthropomorphic, embodied God who eats and bathes and whose offspring we are, and says the obedient may sit on the throne and be exalted as sons and daughters of God, but asserts nothing about divine ancestry, God's progression, or the begetting of spirit children.
quote: But is there anything wrong in thinking of a God who eats? He did eat and has promised to eat again. What is wrong in it? He bathes, at least in fire, so he tells us. We are his ofT-spring, and he has given us commandments to serve him in the name of his only Begotten Son as sons and daughters unto God.

claim: A mission report; the only axis contact is a closing line that the gospel exists to exalt men and women here and hereafter, used in a general uplift sense.
quote: I close by leaving with you my testimony that this Gospel is in the earth to exalt men and women, not only after they die but while they are here, to lift them up from the common ways of life.

claim: Wells argues literal divine sonship means humans inherit God's own attributes, differing from Him only in degree of perfection, but never asserts divine ancestry above the Father, God's own progression, or spirit birth.
quote: We have inherited all of these divine attributes because we are the children of God in very deed, and so man is made in the image of God both in spirit and in body, in physical form and in all of his faculties ; the difference being that in the one they exist in their perfection, in the other in very imperfect form.

claim: Stephen L Richards lists as a distinctive Joseph Smith doctrine the fatherhood AND motherhood of our individual spirits, chained to spiritual creation preceding mortal creation and a transcendent scheme of eternal progression, and separately insists resurrection-salvation is not exaltation.
quote: The continuity of intelligence and intelligencies ; the fatherhood, — and motherhood too, of our individual spirits ; the free agency and choice which were ours in the pre-earth lif e ; spiritual creation preceding mortal creation ; the relationship of body to spirit in this life and in the hereafter, the transcendent scheme of eternal progression, — all these and many related items constitute a unified, logical, authoritative exposition without counterpart in Christian literature.

claim: Reminiscences on priesthood and testimony; the only axis contact is a single closing phrase about the gospel bringing eternal exaltation.
quote: "Man is that he may have joy," and there is no joy in the world that equals the joy of knowing in your heart of hearts that God lives, that Jesus is the Christ, that Joseph Smith was a prophet of God, and that we as individuals are living the Gospel that will bring eternal exaltation to us and our loved ones.

claim: Enumerates a formal three-estate scheme - pre-existent spirit, mortal living soul, and a future 'third estate' of exaltation and glory - and presents it as the complete brief of the purpose of life.
quote: it is only when we have attained to that condition that we can rise in the resurrection, after taking up these bodies, to exaltation and glory in that future third estate; so that we have in this matter of three estates a perfect brief citation of the purpose and meaning of life.

claim: Bowen affirms limitless post-mortal progression in knowledge and power for man (with D&C 130 quoted), and man's 'kinship with God', but never asserts godhood attained, divine ancestry, God's own progression, or spirit birth.
quote: that after death he would live again and enter upon a new life throughout the course of which he can go on acquiring knowledge, growing in power and understanding and intelligence without limit of time

claim: Describes the Father as an embodied personage 'glorified and exalted' and says the gospel is intended to make us like Christ and joint heirs of all the Father possesses — bare theosis with no ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring claim.
quote: It is intended to make us like him, to save us with him, joint heirs with Jesus Christ of all that the Father possesses.

claim: A talk on simple worship, welfare, and the Church's mission; the only axis contact is a single closing reference to spiritual salvation and exaltation.
quote: And so may God be with us at all times and help us in all ways that we may do his will ; that we may spread the Gospel ; that we may point to all humanity the way to temporal salvation, not only, as we are trying to do now, but spiritual salvation and exaltation also, is my prayer in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: Standard premortal-existence sermon: we lived as God's spirit children before this world and may attain exaltation, but no claim about God's own origin, progression, or new spirit offspring.
quote: My purpose in calling your attention to these paragraphs is to show the dual nature of all created things; that we lived in another world before this world was made, as the children of God, the spirit children of God.

claim: Bare theosis in passing: faithfulness will bring redemption and exaltation in an unspecified glory.
quote: we have assurance and promise that through our faith and diligence in the performance of duty, we shall be redeemed and exalted in a glory of which we have no thought nor can we understand fully at this time.

claim: Generic celestial-exaltation framing (preparation to live in the presence of the King); no ancestry, progression, or increase content.
quote: It is not practicing self-denial just because we are asked to do it, but it is to prepare for eternal living and exaltation.

claim: Richards makes the celestial kingdom the exclusive locus of 'eternal increase' and states flatly that man may there become divine, with humans framed as lesser but potentially divine intelligences in God's literal family.
quote: Only there do we have assurance of the reunion of families and the perpetuation of family relationship and eternal increase. In that kingdom man may ultimately become divine.

claim: Sermon on obedience to law (Word of Wisdom, Sabbath, tithing, fasting); no content on any axis.
Draws the general-salvation vs. exaltation distinction and ties exaltation to works, but says nothing specific about what exaltation consists of.
quote: I feel that salvation moves over into the realm of exaltation, and that before a man is completely saved he must be exalted in the presence of God, and to be exalted his deeds must justify that exaltation.

claim: Personal mission-call reminiscence; exaltation mentioned only as the reward for honoring priesthood service.
quote: It is not the Priesthood that assures to us exaltation, but the manner in which we honor and labor under the authority of that Priesthood.

claim: Hymn-book history and South Pacific mission travelogue; exaltation appears only as a conditional reward for sharing the gospel.
quote: We will attain our exaltation in the Celestial Kingdom only on the condition that we divide with our Father's other children the blessings of the Gospel of our Lord and observe the commandments that will enrich our lives here and hereafter.

claim: Testimony sermon plus Word of Wisdom exhortation; exaltation invoked generically as the end of obedience.
quote: the favor of heaven will be upon us in life, and we will attain to the blessings of eternal life and exaltation, and no mortal man can comprehend the magnitude and the greatness of the blessings in store for us.

speaker: Heber J. Grant
claim: Heber J. Grant puts the O My Father claim that there is a Mother in Heaven into the conference record by reading the hymn.

States the standard literal-spirit-parentage premise with a 'like begets like' heredity gloss (we possess intelligence 'in embryo'), but makes no claim about God's origin, God's progression, or post-mortal offspring.
quote: We are spirit children of God, our Father in heaven. A law of creation in the realm of life is that like begets like. Since intelligence is the glory of our Father, we his children possess at least in embryo a spark of this glorious attribute.

claim: Mission report and family reminiscence; 'exaltation' used once as a generic personal reward.
quote: not alone for her welfare and exaltation, but also to give encouragement and blessings to her offspring.

claim: Church-music and tithing sermon framing exaltation in the celestial kingdom as the goal; no ancestry, progression, or increase content.
quote: It is the mission of this Church to prepare men and women for eternal living in that glorified presence.

claim: Clawson lays out an explicit three-estate staging of God's spirit children (premortal, mortal, and a 'third estate' of exaltation) and makes eternal marriage the condition, with the exalted pair as king/priest and queen/priestess.
quote: Therefore Eve was created and given to him for a. companion, a helpmate, that he as a king and a priest and she as a queen and priestess might rise to exaltation and glory and together receive a fulness of joy.

claim: Liberty/free-agency address premised on man's literal spirit childhood of God and uncreated intelligence, but with no claim about God's own nature or eternal increase.
quote: In his first estate, that is, before he came to this earth, his spirit was the literal child of God.

claim: Affirms unlimited human progression toward the power of God, but this is bare theosis with no assertion about God's own progression, ancestry, or offspring.
quote: I like the idea of the Church that if you and I shall avail ourselves to the maximum of our possibilities, some time in eternity we may have the power of God, that there is no limit, if you will, to the progress that the spirit of man can attain to.

claim: Testimony address; calls the Father 'a glorified and exalted personage' and refers in passing to the works of 'the Gods' (plural), but asserts nothing about how God became God or about eternal increase.
quote: I bear testimony that God the Eternal Father lives, a glorified and exalted personage, in whose image and likeness we his children are born and existing.

claim: First-time speaker's testimony on returning to religion; exaltation named once as the goal of commandment-keeping.
quote: only by keeping that law, and by keeping all of the commandments of the Lord, can we expect to find that exaltation in the kingdom of our Father which we are striving to obtain.

claim: America-as-promised-land and free-agency sermon; 'salvation and exaltation' used once as a generic end.
quote: it is intended for the eventual salvation and exaltation of everyone who will accept and observe the eternal principles which lead into the presence of the Lord.

claim: Sermon on 'the abundant life' as spiritual rather than material, ending on eternal life as God's greatest gift; no content on any axis.
God-of-miracles survey and defense of President Grant; celestial exaltation appears only in the closing benediction.
quote: to the end that we may gain exaltation in the Celestial Kingdom when our life's labors are completed

claim: Tithing, fast offerings, and Word of Wisdom sermon; exaltation named once as the reward we are candidates for.
quote: If we obtain an exaltation, for which we are candidates, it will be not for believing in these principles : It will be for living them, as the Lord designed that we should.

claim: War, free agency, and divine sovereignty address; makes the exaltation of God's children His glory but says nothing about God's own origin or progression.
quote: God's sovereignty is absolute, but the exaltation and happiness of His children are His glory.

claim: Fulfilled-prophecy survey and call to member responsibility; celestial exaltation invoked generically as the promised outcome of repentance.
quote: all -- not just a few -- but all may be exalted in His celestial kingdom and obtain glory, immortality and eternal life.

claim: Commendation of faithful Saints plus internal/external evidences of the gospel; the highest degree of celestial glory is named but not described.
quote: I suppose that we are all candidates for the highest degree of glory in the Celestial kingdom.

claim: Welfare/war address that includes a warning against unauthorized pamphlets of garbled early-leader sermon extracts (on world conditions, not doctrine) and an exclusivity claim that temple marriage is the only source of man's greatest glory and exaltation; no increase, ancestry, or divine-progression content.
quote: This revelation and this restoration makes of marriage a holy relationship, out of which and out of which only, can come man's greatest glory and exaltation.

claim: Political address on the divine origin of the Constitution and self-government; no content on any axis.
Free-agency and leadership sermon; exaltation named once as one possible outcome of agency.
quote: God has also given unto each of us the one and only tool by which we might gain honor and success and exaltation, or on the other hand, misery and disgrace and absolute degradation.

claim: Lays out an explicit three-estates scheme (premortal spirit childhood, mortality, and a third estate of eternal life) and quotes the first verses of 'O My Father,' but stops at generic eternal life with no increase, offspring, or divine-origin claim.
quote: There are three estates of man: The first estate was when we dwelt with God as His spirit children, in His holy habitation, before the world was made

claim: Sermon on Jesus's works, vocational training, and labor/capital relations; 'exalted' used only of Christ's enthronement.
Counsel to soldiers plus Grant's account of the heavenly council vision behind his apostolic call; 'exalted position' refers to the apostleship, not to godhood.

Joseph Fielding Smith expounds D&C 132 to define exaltation as 'a continuation of the seeds forever' and eternal increase as the crowning glory, and defines 'the deaths' as being cut off from eternal increase and left as angels who are 'not gods'.
quote: the Lord continues, in this revelation, to say that if they are married by His word, then they shall pass on to the exaltation, and that exaltation is a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever. In other words, the family organization is intact throughout all eternity, and there shall be eternal increase, -- and that is the crowning glory, if you please, in the Kingdom of God.

claim: Counsel to young men facing the draft; no content on any axis.

Radio address summarizing the restored gospel's 'new interpretations,' including eternal progression to divinity and heaven as the projection of the home into eternity, but with no assertion of eternal increase, spirit offspring, or God's own origin.
quote: Men were given to understand that through obedience to the laws of the Gospel they might continue to grow and develop in knowledge and power until in eternity they would come to divinity itself

claim: Tribute to President Grant plus a sermon on agency, emotion, and reason; exaltation named once in the closing testimony.
quote: It is intended for the welfare of mankind, for their eternal salvation and exaltation.

claim: Obedience/gratitude sermon with Relief Society, choir, and wartime counsel; celestial exaltation named only as the conditional reward.
quote: He has provided a way for our safety not only here but for our eternal exaltation as well.

claim: Temple-marriage and sealing sermon with cautionary cases; makes exaltation depend on the new and everlasting covenant but never describes it in terms of increase, offspring, or godhood.
quote: some of the greatest blessings our Father has for His children, intended for the very elect of the Lord, are pronounced upon them through their faithfulness in the keeping of their covenants, blessings that are attainable in no other way but in the marriage relation in the new and everlasting covenant.

claim: Autobiographical address (health, 1918 succession, Kansas City speeches, tithing pledges); vault text is truncated mid-sentence at the source. No content on any axis.

Home-and-family address: heaven as the projection of the home into eternity, spirits as literal children of the Father entering mortality through homes, and a pro-natalist appeal; no eternal increase, spirit offspring, or claim about God's own origin.
quote: The spirits of men, which are the literal children of the Father, are by Him permitted to take on mortality through a home, it being the chief purpose of the administrators of the home to guide the spirits so entrusted to their keeping back to the eternal presence whence they came.

claim: Tithing/Word of Wisdom testimony followed by long readings from D&C 13, 20, and 121; reads the 'one God or many Gods' passage aloud without any comment or gloss on plurality of Gods.
quote: A time to come in the which nothing shall be withheld, whether there be one God or many Gods, they shall be manifest.

claim: Sermon on humility as strength, using Moses and Joseph Smith as examples; 'he touched divinity' is rhetorical, not a doctrinal claim about godhood.
Reads D&C 84's oath and covenant, including 'all that my Father hath shall be given unto him,' but adds no gloss beyond making the priesthood a prerequisite to exaltation.
quote: If a man would ascend to exaltation and glory he must have the Priesthood.

claim: Wartime First Presidency message (health, welfare, false isms, church and state, soldiers' moral standing); 'exaltation and eternal progression' appears as a generic promise to members, with no claim about God's own progression.
quote: leading them all to righteous living and a spiritual life that shall bring them to salvation, exaltation, and eternal progression in wisdom, knowledge, understanding, and power.

claim: Easter address on when a Christian may justly enter a war; 'self exaltation' is used of pride, not godhood.

Joseph Fielding Smith publicly reframes the Adam question against fundamentalist agitators -- Adam/Michael holds the keys of salvation only under Christ, 'for Christ is greater than Adam' -- and glosses D&C 76's 'they are gods' as meaning exalted men become 'sons of God, joint heirs with Jesus Christ' rather than gods in their own right.
quote: there are those who are trying to stir up trouble among the Latter-day Saints today by teaching doctrines that are not in accordance with the revelations of the Lord, and maintaining that Authorities of the Church who have gone before taught doctrines which they did not teach. So we must have it understood clearly that while Adam will preside over his posterity as Michael, the prince, and as he will hold the keys of salvation, as he does, all of that will be under the direction of Jesus Christ, the Holy One of Israel, for Christ is greater than Adam.

claim: George Albert Smith's charge to stake presidents on sustaining the prophet; exaltation named once as what leaders must merit.
quote: It remains for us to demonstrate whether or not we will do our part and merit exaltation.

claim: George F. Richards states that husbands and wives sealed for time and eternity 'are to have an offspring, an eternal increase,' and that this condition is unobtainable outside the ordained marriage relation -- explicit post-mortal offspring language, though he stops short of naming them spirit children.
quote: Those who have attained those higher blessings, that is husband and wife sealed for time and eternity, they are to have an offspring, an eternal increase. It is unthinkable that that condition could be obtained outside of the marriage relations that the Lord hath ordained.

claim: Reflection on abandoned Church historical sites and the Saints' heritage; exaltation named as the exclusive key the Church holds, with no elaboration.
quote: We are a little handful of people among the children of men, but possessing the only key to exaltation in the celestial kingdom of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Wartime reports from European and Middle Eastern missions plus a welfare appeal; exaltation appears only in the closing benediction.
quote: that we may have joy in this life and exaltation in the life to come

claim: Brief closing remarks on unity with the prophet; exaltation appears only in the closing benediction.
quote: all to the end that we and ours finally may be saved and exalted in his presence

claim: Priesthood-session plea to settle disputes through Church channels rather than the courts, drawing on Paul and John Taylor; no content on any axis.

Priesthood sermon glossing the D&C 84 oath and covenant as the promise that the faithful 'may have all that our Father possesses' -- a strong but bare theosis statement with no increase, offspring, or divine-origin content.
quote: If by bearing this Priesthood and magnifying it before the Lord, we may have all that our Father possesses, eternal life and exaltation in the Celestial Kingdom, what more can He offer as inducement and reward for magnifying the Priesthood?

claim: Address on unity and Church welfare independence; 'exaltation' appears only inside a quotation from the 1942 First Presidency message.
quote: We of this Church stand as the sole possessors of these mighty forces which we have for our own blessing, salvation, and exaltation, not only, but also we hold them in trust for all mankind.

claim: Address on juvenile delinquency statistics and Church standards for youth; exaltation named once as a distant motive.
quote: And if you look to the Great Beyond, and consider your eternal happiness and exaltation, it pays time and time again to maintain the standards of the Church.

claim: Stephen L Richards on national moral decline and LDS leadership; asserts the restored gospel gives man 'divine status' and makes the marriage compact perpetual, but names no increase, offspring, or claim about God's own nature.
quote: They give to man the dignity, the majesty, and the divine status that furnish the foundation for the most exalted conceptions of liberty and freedom that the world has known.

claim: Call to individual missionary work; closes with the plural locution 'the plan of the Gods' (a habitual usage for this speaker, cf. 'the works of the Gods' in 1939) but makes no claim about plurality of Gods, regress, or increase.
quote: I do know that the work in which we, as Latter-day Saints, are engaged is the work of the Lord, the plan of the Gods for the existence of the earth, and of man upon the earth, for their glory and for man's exaltation

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith names exaltation in the presence of the Father and the Son as the end of the atonement, but develops no claim about godhood, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: Can you imagine the suffering, the extent of the anguish of soul that our Savior passed through — He who is the Son of God — in order that we might receive the resurrection, and that we might receive the remission of our sins through obedience to the principles of the Gospel, and an exaltation in the presence of the Father and the Son ?

claim: Wirthlin makes work the 'power of God' and links it to salvation and exaltation, but the exaltation reference is a bare formula with no godhood mechanics.
quote: Therefore, any individual who denies himself the privilege of work denies himself salvation and exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: George F. Richards teaches that man inherits from the Father the very attributes that make God what He is and is placed on earth to perfect them, but this is bare theosis with no offspring chain, no ancestry beyond the Father, and no divine progression.
quote: It teaches me, that I inherited from the Father those qualities and attributes which in their perfection make God, the Father, what he is; that I am placed here on earth for the purpose, in part, of perfecting the qualities and attributes of Deity in me implanted

claim: Clark quotes the First Presidency's 1942 assurance of salvation and exaltation for slain soldiers; exaltation appears only as a formula.
quote: Their salvation and exaltation in the world to come will be secure.

claim: Wirthlin argues baptism and vicarious work open salvation and exaltation to all; no godhood content beyond the formula.
quote: We believe in a God who so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son to suffer, to bleed, and die to the end that everyone of us might enjoy salvation and exaltation in his kingdom.

claim: Stephen L Richards, in an open letter to non-Mormon friends, defines exaltation as investiture with the divine nature plus eternal increase — homes 'blessed with eternal increase so that families never cease growing in number' and 'never-ending posterity.'
quote: That these eternal homes of the future life shall be blessed with eternal increase so that families never cease growing in number, in virtue and power, ever continuing to subserve the eternal and beneficent purposes and designs of the Creator of. the universe.

claim: Bowen equates eternal life with exaltation in the celestial kingdom in a single clause; the talk is about the power of conviction, not godhood.
quote: Over and beyond all these, those doctrines taught the achievement of immortality through the Lord's death and the plan for achieving eternal life, which is exaltation in the celestial kingdom of God.

claim: A postwar sermon on peace, selfishness, and temperance; no content on any axis.
Richards repeats the D&C 84 'all that the Father hath' formula in one sentence and then preaches tithing for the rest of the talk.
quote: Everything is offered unto us that our Father in heaven has to give, if only we will be faithful as we have covenanted to do when we entered the waters of baptism into this Church.

claim: A charge to the seventies on priesthood history and missionary work; no axis content ('exalted purpose' is used of their calling, not of deification).
A defense of the Church welfare plan as preparation for celestial unity; no axis content.
Petersen lists denials of temple marriage's tie to exaltation among false teachings; exaltation is invoked but never unpacked.
quote: or when anyone comes and tells you that temple marriage is just a fad and that it has no relationship to your exaltation in the kingdom of God

claim: Hunter calls men 'gods in embryo' begotten and born of heavenly parents, says their hope is to become 'even like unto his heavenly parents,' and affirms the Snow couplet by name as 'powerful Mormon doctrine' — God once was as man now is.
quote: The only way we can know God is to live as he lives, to think as he thinks, and to experience what he experiences. Interpreted in this light, we are brought face to face with the powerful Mormon doctrine which declares that "As man is God once was, and as God is man may be."

claim: A tableau sermon on living 'in mine own way'; exaltation appears only in the closing benediction clause.
quote: Let us love the Lord and our fellow men and live the commandments of God that we may have a full and abundant life leading to exaltation, I pray, in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: A conference welcome; exaltation in the celestial kingdom named as the goal in one clause with no elaboration.
quote: We are here as sons and daughters of the Living God, trying to work our way through life until we shall be worthy of an exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Clark preaches the necessity of a personal testimony; exaltation is named once as what is forfeited without it.
quote: pointing out to us how we may get that comfort and that consolation to which each and every child of God is entitled, and without which we may not be happy or gain our exaltation

claim: Wirthlin's sermon on the name of Christ quotes D&C 76 on celestial heirs as 'priests and kings, who have received of his fulness' but stops short of the 'they are gods' verse and adds no godhood mechanics.
quote: They are they into whose hands the Father has given all things — They are they who are priests and kings, who have received of his fulness, and of his glory;

claim: A sermon on obedience; exaltation in God's presence is named as the objective in one sentence and never developed.
quote: We who are here have great hopes for peace in this world and exaltation in the presence of God in the world to come.

claim: Widtsoe quotes Brigham Young asserting that God is bound by His own eternal law and would 'cease to be exalted' if He violated it — God's exalted status presented as contingent, not intrinsic — and quotes Young's expectation of becoming 'like those who have gone before me' and being exalted with all power and keys.
quote: The volition of the creature is free. This is a law of their existence, and the Lord cannot violate his own law. Were he to do that he would cease to be exalted.

claim: A welfare-program sermon; 'man's eternal progression' appears once as a throwaway justification for industry and thrift.
quote: those pioneer virtues of industry and thrift which are the priceless possessions of every self-respecting person and which are indispensable to man's eternal progression

claim: A welfare and fast-offering sermon built on the Good Samaritan; the only 'exalted' is D&C 104's 'the poor shall be exalted.'
A fast-offering appeal; 'exalted' appears only figuratively (his own feelings, and Isaiah's mountain 'exalted above the hills').
Hunter's centennial history of the westward migration; spiritual qualities are said to 'exalt man to his full stature as a son of God,' but nothing on godhood mechanics.
quote: In fact, these intangible spiritual qualities exalt man to his full stature as a son of God.

claim: In his first conference address McConkie describes God the Eternal Father Himself as a 'glorified, exalted, resurrected' being — attributing resurrection, and so past death and mortality, to the Father; a single descriptive clause, not a developed argument, but a definite commitment.
quote: There then appeared to him two glorified, exalted, resurrected beings — God the Eternal Father and Jesus Christ his Son

claim: A short testimony address on the power of testimony; no axis content.
Benson ties exaltation to the eternity of the marriage covenant in a single sentence, then spends the talk on home evening and parental duty; no eternal increase or godhood content.
quote: In fact, our very exaltation in the celestial kingdom is directly related to the family and the eternity of the marriage covenant.

claim: Richards states the standard premortal-spirit-birth and eternal-progression frame with exaltation as the goal, but adds nothing specific on godhood, ancestry, or increase.
quote: Coming to this earth is an important part of the plan instituted in the councils of heaven for man's eternal progression toward the goal of our existence, which is an exaltation in the kingdom and presence of the Father and the Son forever.

claim: Clark's 'They of the Last Wagon' pioneer tribute; 'exalting joy' and 'more exalted station' are figurative, with no axis content.

speaker: Milton R. Hunter
claim: Milton R. Hunter says Joseph Smith interpreted the continuation of the seeds as the power to beget spirit children.
Richards argues every worthy son of God should hold priesthood and 'bear a portion of his power,' with priesthood indispensable to exaltation, but keeps it at the level of shared divine authority.
quote: And does it not seem reasonable that if the worthy sons of God are to enjoy his companionship in the world to come as a reward for their faithful labors here in this life that they should all bear a portion of his power and be endowed with a part of his spiritual intelligence which constitute the essence of divine authority and priesthood?

claim: A sermon on the peace of Christ; 'our exaltation and election will be sure' is the sole axis touch.
quote: if our lives are holy in his sight, our exaltation and election will be sure, and that eternity is so much more important than mortality

claim: A priesthood-session address on protecting young people and setting an example; 'exalt you in due time' is a quotation from 1 Peter with no axis content.
Closing conference remarks; eternal life in the celestial kingdom with one's family is named as the supreme gift, but with no eternal increase or godhood claim.
quote: the thing that God has given to you that is worth more than all the rest is the opportunity to obtain eternal life in the celestial kingdom and have as your companions, throughout the ages of eternity, sons and daughters, husbands and wives with whom you have associated here on earth

claim: A tithing sermon closing with exaltation as the goal; no axis development.
quote: We are all candidates for the blessings of eternal life and exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith on Elijah and genealogy; the Prophet Joseph quotation speaks of the dead being 'exalted to thrones of glory,' but nothing further on godhood, ancestry, or progression.
quote: redeem them that they may come forth in the first resurrection and be exalted to thrones of glory with them

speaker: Marion G. Romney
claim: Marion G. Romney affirms that humans were born as spirit children to God and a Mother in Heaven while admitting that he does not know the process.
Hunter's essay on what makes a prophet; the only axis touch is the closing hymn line 'Mingling with Gods, he can plan for his brethren,' quoted without comment.
quote: Hail to the Prophet, ascended to heaven! Traitors and tyrants now fight him in vain; Mingling with Gods, he can plan for his brethren; Death cannot conquer the hero again.

claim: A mission report on the Central States and early Missouri Church history; no axis content.
McKay on youth delinquency and environment; exaltation in the life to come is named once as what the gospel teaches men to obtain.
quote: The gospel is a rational philosophy that teaches men how to get happiness in this life, and exaltation in the life to come.

claim: Eldred G. Smith quotes D&C 132:19-21 in full ('Then shall they be gods... a continuation of the seeds forever and ever'), endorses the Snow couplet as the point of temple marriage, and states the penalty side: those who fail become ministering angels who 'in worlds without end shall have no increase.'
quote: We are told they will become ministering angels, and in worlds without end shall have no increase.

claim: Benson on the oath and covenant of the priesthood quotes D&C 84's 'all that my Father hath shall be given unto him' but does not unpack it toward godhood or increase.
quote: And then, even more significant, this great promise was made: ". . . therefore all that my Father hath shall be given unto him,"

claim: Lee closes a talk on happy homes by paraphrasing D&C 132:19 — the sealed pass by 'the angels and the gods' to exaltation — but stops before the continuation-of-the-seeds clause.
quote: the Lord has said that those who are sealed in the temple by the Holy Spirit of Promise shall pass by the angels and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation in all things

claim: Young credits Joseph Smith with revealing 'the divinity of man' and 'the doctrine of eternal progression' but names them only as headings.
quote: Joseph Smith stands out as the revealer of God's eternal principles that show above all writers in this age the divinity of man; the doctrine of eternal progression; the true meaning of salvation

claim: Hunter's whole sermon is on the character of God: God is 'a man — an exalted man,' the Snow couplet is quoted by name, the King Follett Discourse is quoted at length ('God himself, the Father of us all, dwelt on an earth'), and God is simultaneously said to be omniscient with 'knowledge absolutely unlimited' — the past-mortality claim held together with a completed-knowledge claim.
quote: We believe that God is a personal being. By a personal being, we mean that he is a man — an exalted man.

claim: McConkie on priesthood, keys, and legal administrators; being 'saved and exalted in our Father's kingdom' is the only axis touch.
quote: all of the laws, ordinances, and principles by obedience to which we can be both saved and exalted in our Father's kingdom

claim: A Tahitian Mission report; exaltation named once as a personal hope.
quote: and to receive, when I have passed beyond this sphere of action, an exaltation in God's presence

claim: Clark's priesthood-session appeal for unity and against private doctrinal innovation; 'saved and exalted in his presence' is a closing formula.
quote: may we so live that we may be saved and exalted in his presence, I humbly pray, in the name of Jesus

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith reads D&C 76:54-60 including 'they are gods, even the sons of God' and calls what divorcing temple-married couples forfeit 'the glory of godhood' — explicit deification language, but bare theosis with no ancestry, increase, or divine-progression content.
quote: How could they be good and want to separate and throw into the discard all these glorious blessings that would bring to them the glory of godhood, as set forth in the revelations which I have read to you?

speaker: Milton R. Hunter
claim: Milton R. Hunter defines eternal seeds as the power to beget spirit children on the same principle by which we were born to Heavenly Parents.
A sermon on keeping the commandments; exaltation appears twice as a heading word with no doctrinal development.
quote: if they really had a comprehension and knowledge of the Fatherhood of God, the brotherhood of man, and the eternal plans of the Father for the well-being and exaltation of his children

claim: Ivins ties priesthood, temple sealing, and eternal family to exaltation, but says nothing about godhood, increase, or the nature of God's own past.
quote: that priesthood is essential to the performance of the ordinances that he has set up as essential to our exaltation in his kingdom

claim: A Tongan Mission report closing with exaltation as a formula.
quote: if we would only do as well as we know how, our salvation and our exaltation would be secure

claim: Richards testifies the Father is 'a glorified and exalted being' with a tangible body — the standard D&C 130:22 corporeality formula, with no claim of past mortality or resurrection — and calls the atonement a love 'possessed only by the Gods.'
quote: God the Eternal Father lives, a glorified and exalted being, having a body of flesh, bones, and spirit as tangible as man's

claim: Clark retells the council in heaven and preaches chastity; 'the laws of salvation and exaltation are founded in righteousness' is the only axis touch.
quote: Certainly men cannot be saved in sin, because the laws of salvation and exaltation are founded in righteousness, not in sin.

claim: A sermon on Satan's reality and modern chastity; the only godhood language is Isaiah 14 applied negatively to Lucifer's ambition.

Romney quotes D&C 76 including 'they are gods, even the sons of God' and D&C 132:49 on the Prophet's sealed exaltation, but the talk's subject is assurance and calling and election, not godhood mechanics.
quote: He who obtains it will obtain an exaltation in the celestial kingdom of our Father in heaven.

claim: Hunter attributes to Joseph Smith 'the head God of all the Gods' who called the grand council, says Jesus Christ 'rose to the status of Godhood' during premortal life, and describes the Father as having 'many other kingdoms' while assigning this world to Christ as its God — a graded plurality of Gods in which godhood is attained rather than intrinsic.
quote: Joseph Smith tells us that at that grand council the head God of all the Gods called the council, and the purpose was to present a plan whereby his children were to come into mortal earth and have the experience of mortality and then return back into the presence of God.

claim: Kimball's repentance-and-forgiveness sermon; exaltation appears only in the opening and closing formulas.
quote: until we shall have perfected ourselves, looking toward the glories of exaltation awaiting the most faithful

claim: Hunter preaches the two great commandments of love; exaltation appears only as the generic reward for keeping all commandments.
quote: In fact, the Lord has said that if we receive exaltation in his kingdom, we will do so only on condition that we render obedience to "every word that proceedeth forth from the mouth of God."

claim: Moyle teaches that obedience makes us authors of our own exaltation — bare theosis with no mechanism, parentage, or progression claim.
quote: Just as surely as our Savior became the author of our eternal salvation, so must we through that same degree of obedience become the authors of our own exaltation.

claim: Richards catalogs the gifts of the gospel (discernment, wisdom, comfort); no content on any axis.
quote: I believe in the gifts of the gospel. I believe they will come to those who live and strive for them.

claim: Richards urges adult Aaronic Priesthood men to receive the Melchizedek Priesthood and temple sealing; exaltation and eternal marriage are named as the goal but with no generative or ancestry content.
quote: As Latter-day Saints, the goal of our existence and purpose in life is to obtain an exaltation in the kingdom and presence of the Father and the Son; and a man may not attain to that glory without receiving the Melchizedek Priesthood.

claim: Hunter's tithing sermon treats exaltation only as the generic reward for obedience; no ancestry, progression, or generative content.
quote: Furthermore, the Lord has given us the law of tithing to test our preparedness to enter the kingdom of God, to enter exaltation.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith preaches salvation by obedience and the sufficiency of modern revelation; exaltation and the nature of God are mentioned only generically.
quote: It comes through obedience to every principle and eternal truth pertaining to our exaltation.

claim: Cowley eulogizes George Albert Smith; the only axis-adjacent line is a generic hope of being exalted in God's presence.
quote: Let us so honor him that when we come to die we may be saved and exalted in the celestial presence of God our Father, and in that presence we will find his noble and prophetic son, George Albert Smith.

claim: Ivins calls seventies to missionary service; exaltation and the personality of God appear only as passing generalities.
quote: Because of its wonderful effect upon people, because of its essentiality to their exaltation, we have a tremendous obligation to carry that message to the world.

claim: Kimball preaches valiancy and loyalty to Church authority; exaltation appears only as the generic destination the lukewarm forfeit.
quote: Those were Saints who had been baptized into the kingdom, received the Holy Ghost, we would assume, and were supposed to be on their way to exaltation.

claim: Meeks closes with a strong but bare theosis claim — divine sonship gives him the inherited power to rise to Godhood and share all the Father's power, glory, and dominion — with no ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring content.
quote: But it tells me that I am a son of God, an eternal being; that as a son of God, there is within me all the qualities, all the powers of my Father which is in Heaven, that there is within me the power to rise to Godhood, that I may share with God, my Father in Heaven, forever and ever, all His power and glory and dominion, through Jesus Christ, our Savior, Amen.

claim: Eldred G. Smith preaches obedience and agency; godhood is named once as a temple blessing forfeited by disobedience, without elaboration.
quote: Some people sacrifice all the blessings of the temple endowment and sealing, including the blessings of godhood and exaltation just because they do not want to be obedient in wearing the temple garment.

claim: Hunter's missionary-work sermon names exaltation only as the generic greatest gift awaiting the obedient.
quote: I know also that if you and I will live according to the teachings of the commandments that we have received in the Church of Jesus Christ, someday we shall come back into the presence of God and receive exaltation, which he has declared to be the greatest gift that he has in store for those who love him and keep his commandments.

claim: Kimball preaches spirit over letter in tithing, Word of Wisdom, and fasting; perfection and 'all that he has is ours' appear only as generic promises.
quote: The Lord has promised to all of us who obey his commandments and live his statutes that all that he has is ours.

claim: Richards warns against worldly encroachments on Zion, including birth control; marriage is called an eternal compact between a priest and priestess and premortal spirits are assumed, but no exalted-parenthood, ancestry, or progression claim is made.
quote: The foe is attacking our divinely-given concept that marriage is an eternal compact between a priest and a priestess of the Most High, charged with the sacred mission of bringing children into the world, and then guiding them safely back into the presence of God, whence their spirits came.

claim: Eldred G. Smith preaches the art of living and bearing testimony; salvation and exaltation are named only as the generic end of priesthood ordinances.
quote: ...he has established his gospel in the earth, with the full power of the priesthood through which all the ordinances unto salvation and exaltation may be performed.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith glosses D&C 132 to teach that sealed couples receive 'eternal lives' meaning a continuation of the seeds forever after the resurrection, while the unsealed 'are not gods, but are angels of God forever and ever,' remaining separately and singly in eternity.
quote: And further, that the husband and the wife after the resurrection of the dead will not come to an end. By that the Lord means that they will have a continuation of the seeds forever, and the family organization does not come to an end.

claim: Wirthlin argues salvation requires faith plus works; exaltation in the kingdom is named repeatedly but only as the generic goal.
quote: The godly power Paul speaks of is the combination of faith, the divine motivator, and the works of the individual. These together make salvation and exaltation in the kingdom of God a certainty.

claim: Levi Edgar Young preaches wisdom, study, and education; 'eternal progression' appears only as a decorative phrase about viewing society, with no doctrinal claim.
quote: It looks upon society from a high plane and in the pattern of eternal progression.

claim: Hunter equates eternal life, exaltation, and godhood and promises the faithful power comparable to what the Father and Son 'have attained' — maximal theosis, but no ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring claim.
quote: If we prove faithful in keeping all of God's commandments, we shall receive a glorious celestialization, a comparable degree of happiness, joy, peace, and power with that which God, the Eternal Father, and the Only Begotten Son have attained.

claim: Kimball closes by itemizing the content of the Lord's 'all': immortality, eternal growth, eternal increase, perfection, and Godhood.
quote: The blessings of eternity contemplated in this "all" bring to men immortality and everlasting life, eternal growth, divine leadership, eternal increase, perfection, and with it all — Godhood.

claim: Longden preaches the two great commandments and the Good Samaritan; 'salvation and exaltation' appears once as a generic label for the Savior's doctrine.
quote: The Savior had been teaching his doctrine, the saving principles of salvation and exaltation.

claim: Hunter defends Christ's divinity and the necessity of taking His name; Christ's premortal godhood and the creation of many worlds are affirmed, but nothing is claimed about the Father's origin, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: In fact, in his pre-mortal life, even before this world was created, he enjoyed the status of godhood. Acting in that capacity, along with the Eternal Father, he helped to create this world, as well as many other worlds.

claim: Kimball surveys scriptural miracles to argue faith precedes the miracle; exaltation is named once as the harvest of faith.
quote: Indomitable faith can help us live the commandments and thereby bring blessings unnumbered with peace, perfection, and exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: ElRay L. Christiansen urges testimony borne in good works; exaltation appears only as the generic possible outcome.
quote: Such testimonies may well lead one to exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: George Q. Morris insists God is a knowable Father in the form of man rather than an 'oblong cloud'; exaltation and growth into all truth are asserted only generically.
quote: God has prescribed the principles that will save us and exalt us in his presence, and they are embodied in the teachings of the Church.

claim: LeGrand Richards warns youth against profanity, alcohol, and unchastity; the only axis-adjacent phrase is a quoted First Presidency line about 'the exaltations of eternities.'
quote: The exaltations of eternities await his coming.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith urges scripture study against deception; exaltation is mentioned only as the object of the commandments members neglect to study.
quote: ...we have not taken advantage of our opportunities to learn, to make ourselves acquainted with the plan of salvation, the commandments of the Lord pertaining to our exaltation.

claim: Benson speaks of his cabinet service, the Constitution, and prayer for the nation; the single axis-adjacent phrase is a generic reference to exalting souls.
quote: I know, my brethren and sisters, that the sweetest work in all the world is the work in which we are engaged in helping to save and exalt the souls of the children of men.

claim: Evans urges being doers of the word and reserving judgment on unanswered questions; exaltation is named once as the generic highest gift.
quote: I think we know enough for our salvation and exaltation in the highest that the Father can give us.

claim: Hunter defines eternal life as the sealed couple's power of eternal increase, distinguishes it from exaltation and Godhood as separate shades of meaning, and states on Joseph Smith's authority that 'continuation of the seeds' means literally bearing children in the celestial glory.
quote: The Prophet Joseph Smith points out that this "continuation of seeds forever and ever," means to have children in the celestial glory.

claim: Ivins expounds 'be thou an example of the believers'; exaltation in God's presence is named only as the conditional reward of faithful service.
quote: ...an exaltation in his presence is contingent only upon faithful service unto him and our fellows.

claim: Lee argues the gates of hell never prevailed because revelation and vicarious ordinances were always provided; he quotes D&C 121's 'Eternal God of all other gods' without gloss and mentions exaltation only generically.
quote: The gates of hell would have prevailed were it not for other vicarious work pertaining to the exaltation which those who accept the gospel might receive, both ordinances for the living and for the dead.

claim: Longden reviews the Articles of Faith and the light of the gospel; exaltation is mentioned twice as the generic object of gospel ordinances.
quote: Those Articles of Faith state that men should have authority to perform the ordinances which pertain to the salvation and the exaltation of our Heavenly Father's children.
