claim: LeGrand Richards argues for a literally embodied resurrected Christ against a God who is a universe-filling essence; no claim on any axis about human exaltation, divine ancestry, or progression.
quote: The whole premise of Mormonism is based upon the fact that the Father and the Son literally appeared to the Prophet Joseph Smith. They couldn't have done that if they were only an essence, everywhere present in the world.

claim: Hunter asks what a Saint would take in exchange for his soul; celestial marriage is called the crowning principle leading to exaltation, but with no elaboration of increase, parenthood, or godhood.
quote: The Lord has also given the great law of celestial marriage, which is the crowning gospel principle, giving the promise that those who abide by that law and keep the other commandments shall rise in the resurrection and receive exaltation or eternal life which he declares is the greatest gift that he has in store for man.

claim: Ivins preaches loyalty to the Church; the temple ordinances are said to lead to the highest exaltation and 'the powers of God' — bare theosis with no further specification.
quote: ...and enjoy the benefits of such ordinances as the temple extends to each of us here in order that we may attain to the highest exaltation and eventually to the powers of God.

claim: Longden preaches every-member missionary work and relays the Tolstoy 'American religion' story; exaltation is named only as the generic content of the message.
quote: ...that mission is to teach first, by example, and second, by precept, the truths of this gospel, which is the gospel of salvation and exaltation into the presence of our heavenly Father and his Son, Jesus Christ.

claim: Richards argues the restored gospel answers the world's human-relations problem; the body is called the tabernacle of God's premortal spirit child and exaltation is invoked generically, with no ancestry, progression, or increase claim.
quote: This ship, like the ark of old, bears all the essentials for the re-establishment of the personal reign of the Lord Jesus Christ in the earth, and the essentials for the exaltation of man in the celestial presence of God the Father and the Son.

claim: Eldred G. Smith warns against postponing temple marriage, quoting D&C 132:19-21 verbatim (continuation of the seeds, 'then shall they be gods') but adding no interpretive gloss beyond calling godhood the stake being gambled away.
quote: To those who have been given the knowledge and the opportunity of temple marriage and then procrastinate, they are gambling the eternal blessings of godhood for a few earthly pleasures.

claim: Wirthlin argues from scripture that Christ established one Church with one gospel; God is affirmed as an embodied personage and exaltation named generically.
quote: He reaffirmed to the world that God was a personage with body, parts, and passions; that Jesus Christ, the despised Nazarene who was crucified upon Calvary's hill, actually lived.

claim: S. Dilworth Young charges Melchizedek Priesthood quorum presidents to activate their men, citing Abraham 3's noble and great ones; exaltation is mentioned only as the direction leaders point people.
quote: If they prove worthy, and unwaveringly lead these people toward their exaltation, he then adds more and more responsibility until there is no limit to capacity, development, and glory of that leader.

claim: Benson preaches courage and trust in God; Moses 1:39 is glossed once as God's work being to make man's exaltation possible.
quote: It is his "work and glory" to make the exaltation of man possible.

claim: Evans lists the satisfying principles of the gospel and urges youth not to fear; God's purpose to exalt all his children is asserted generically.
quote: It is his purpose to save all his children and to exalt all his children, not merely to warn and turn them away, but to labor with them in love and in patience, and to bring them back into his presence, if they will.

claim: Hunter enumerates the laws of happiness; God is affirmed as literally the Father of our spirits and exaltation named as the generic reward, with nothing on ancestry, increase, or progression.
quote: We must have faith in God the eternal Father: that he is actually and literally the Father of our spirits; that he loves us abundantly; and that he controls within his hands, so to speak, the destiny of man and of nations.

claim: Kimball rebukes racial prejudice against Lamanites and other minorities; no content on any axis.
quote: And now, Mrs. Anonymous, when the Lord has made of all flesh equal; when he has accepted both the Gentiles and Israel; when he finds no difference between them, who are we to find a difference and to exclude from the Church and its activities and blessings the lowly Indian?

claim: Lee answers a serviceman's question about qualifying for exaltation with three cautionary stories; eternal marriage and exaltation in the celestial kingdom are affirmed only in general terms.
quote: While yet in your youth, you have done well to ask that question, young man, to seek counsel as to your course in life, for every soul who lives has the possibility, as you have, of an exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Richards asks why anyone would be ashamed of the gospel, reviewing revelation, priesthood, the body, and eternal marriage; premortal spirit birth and 'high places' with the Father are stated only generically.
quote: It has told us in plainness of our beginnings as spirit children of the Father, of our coming to earth to take on mortal bodies, of our probation here, and our destiny, if we so elect, to win high places on our return to the Father in the eternities to come.

claim: Romney urges laboring 'while it is called today' and warns against a second chance; he quotes D&C 132:49 on Joseph Smith's sealed exaltation but makes no claim about increase, ancestry, or progression.
quote: For I am the Lord thy God, and will be with thee even unto the end of the world, and through all eternity; for verily I seal upon you your exaltation, and prepare a throne for you in the kingdom of my Father, with Abraham your father.

claim: Wirthlin's priesthood address on activating Aaronic Priesthood boys quotes Brigham Young that the priesthood exalts the obedient to 'the same glory and power' and 'eternal lives,' but adds no gloss on increase, ancestry, or progression.
quote: The Gospel and the Priesthood are the means he employs to save and exalt his obedient children to the possession with him of the same glory and power to be crowned with crowns of glory, immortality and eternal lives.

claim: J. Reuben Clark enumerates the blessings of Latter-day Saint belief — premortal existence, an embodied God in whose image we are made, continuing revelation — but makes no specific claim on any axis.
quote: We are blessed that we know that if we observe and keep the commandments of the Lord that our salvation and exaltation is assured.

claim: Ivins urges priesthood officers to magnify their callings; an 'exalted position' hereafter is mentioned only in passing as the motive.
quote: ...then I am overpowered with the thought that I should bend every effort and every power within me to magnify my calling, so I should be worthy of a high and exalted position afterwards.

claim: Kimball distinguishes faith obedience from blind obedience across many scriptural cases; his closing list names the new and everlasting covenant as a requirement for exaltation without elaborating what exaltation contains.
quote: A man must enter into the new and everlasting covenant to be exalted.

claim: Longden bears a 'positive testimony' and traces testimony through Peter, Pentecost, Thomas, and Job; exaltation is named only as the object of priesthood ordinances.
quote: They had the power and authority necessary to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to administer in the ordinances thereof which pertain to the salvation and exaltation of our heavenly Father's children.

claim: Richards walks through the standardized missionary lesson plan, including man's premortal spirit birth from the Father and an exalted reward of endless progression in knowledge and power — but the progression predicated is man's, not God's, and no increase or ancestry claim is made.
quote: ...and that the reward to the truly faithful will be placement in the highest degree of glory in the presence of the Father and the Son, there to dwell forever in an eternity of progression in knowledge, power, and goodness.

claim: Romney preaches the 'royal law' and Church welfare; exaltation in the celestial kingdom appears once as the generic stake of obedience.
quote: It is as much a part of the requirements of the gospel of Jesus Christ, and obedience thereto is as certainly a prerequisite to exaltation in the celestial kingdom, as are baptism and the laying on of hands.

claim: Sermon on finding joy in work, home, and service; no content on any axis.
Passing generic reference to the Church's mission to exalt men, with no specification of what exaltation entails.
quote: Now, of course, the Church itself is God's great instrument to build and to save and to exalt men everywhere, through the application of the simple principles of the gospel.

claim: Generic covenant sermon: temple marriage yields eternal family association and Woodruff's 'exaltations, thrones, principalities' list, but no new spirit offspring or divine-ancestry claim.
quote: Who can comprehend that by obeying the celestial law, all the Father hath shall be given unto us, exaltations, thrones, principalities, powers, dominions.

claim: Priesthood-session appeal for doctrinal unity; exaltation appears only as an unelaborated closing hope.
quote: And I pray again that we may see the necessity of accepting the Gospel and all of it, that we may be saved and exalted in his presence.

claim: Sermon on prayer; exaltation appears only as a stock phrase inside a quoted missionary anecdote.
quote: I told the Lord that I believed his Church and kingdom had been established upon the earth; that men had the authority to proclaim the fulness of the gospel of Jesus Christ which pertained to the salvation and exaltation of our Heavenly Father's children.

claim: Bare theosis via D&C 93: obedience brings light and truth until we become like the Father, with no further specification.
quote: It is by keeping the commandments of God that we will gain in light and truth until we are filled with light and truth and know all things and become like unto our Father in heaven.

claim: Stapley states in his own words that those sealed in the new and everlasting covenant obtain 'increase of posterity in the eternal world' and 'a continuation of posterity,' while the unsealed remain single angels without increase — the same increase/no-increase contrast that made Eldred G. Smith's Oct 1948 remarks substantive.
quote: Those who do not enter this order of the priesthood, that is, the eternal covenant of marriage, become angels of God in a separate and single state forever and ever, and thus are without increase of posterity in the eternal world; therefore without posterity they have no need of a kingdom.

claim: Warning against worldly complacency; exaltation named only as the generic reward of gospel living.
quote: The praise of the world will not save us. It will not exalt us in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Bare theosis: obedience will exalt us to an eternal condition of continued growth and learning, with no mechanism or ancestry claim.
quote: obedience to which will bring us the blessings which we might as his children naturally expect if we are obedient to his will, and which will ultimately exalt us in that condition of beauty and glory which will allow us eternally to work, to grow, to learn, to love, to live with him who is our Father.

claim: Survey of the triple combination; recites D&C 131/132 ('cannot have an increase', 'continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods') as proof-text with only the standard gloss that neither sex can be exalted alone — no own-voice claim about eternal offspring.
quote: This revelation informs us that man cannot be exalted without woman, nor the woman without man.

claim: Sermon on testimony of Christ; exaltation appears once, generically, inside a quoted McKay statement.
quote: that he has broken the bands of death and has brought resurrection, that through him, by obedience to the gospel, we will gain eternal exaltation in his kingdom.

claim: Rich but still generic theosis: temple ordinances open the way to the fulness of the Father, all power and knowledge, and kingship — without asserting eternal increase, divine ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: The temple ordinances open the door to gaining all power and all wisdom and all knowledge. Temple ordinances open up the way to membership in the Church of the Firstborn. They open the door to becoming kings and priests and inheriting all things.

claim: Sermon on following living prophets; exaltation is a closing stock phrase only.
quote: May we be guided by their inspiring instruction, and may we undertake with them to build up God's kingdom upon the earth, and eventually be worthy of an exaltation in that kingdom, I pray, in the name of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Hugh B. Brown
claim: Hugh B. Brown quotes Widtsoe's account of God's development and then distinguishes human deification from humanizing God, a bounded reframe of divine progression.
Sermon on the lowliness of Christ and materialism; exaltation named once, generically, as open to the poor.
quote: His is the salvation and exaltation if we follow him, of all of us.

claim: In a priesthood-duty sermon Ivins specifies that the highest exaltation includes sitting with God in the councils of heaven and 'eternal progress and eternal increase' — B1 eternal parenthood named, though unelaborated.
quote: for we have been told today that to attain to the highest exaltation in the kingdom of God, to sit with God in the councils of heaven, enjoying the privileges of eternal progress and eternal increase, that eventually at least we will have to learn to obey all of the commandments of God.

claim: Sermon on the short road to sin; celestial marriage is credited only with family life continuing beyond the grave, no increase or godhood claim.
quote: celestial marriage promises us that family life will exist beyond the grave.

claim: In an atonement sermon Morris asserts that God the Father's own glorified, exalted, celestialized state came to him through death and the resurrection — i.e., the Father himself passed through mortality and was exalted by the same process, the Orson Hyde 'once a child, and mortal' type of claim.
quote: for God the Eternal Father is a being, a Glorified Being of flesh and bone, exalted and celestialized, and that comes through death and the resurrection by means of the atonement.

claim: Restoration/apostasy sermon; exaltation named twice as the goal but never specified, and the discussion of deity concerns only God's corporeality against creedal formulations.
quote: How this event should challenge our initiative and put us on our feet, earnestly seeking that greatest of all blessings, eternal exaltation!

claim: Missionary-invitation sermon; exaltation is the generic closing promise, with Joseph Smith's king parable ('made equal with him in all the affairs of the kingdom') quoted but not developed.
quote: I bear unto you my testimony that this is the gospel of Jesus Christ through which we may receive eternal life and become exalted in the kingdom of our Father in heaven.

claim: Report of a European mission tour; the single exaltation reference is a rhetorical list item about what the gospel does for a man.
quote: The gospel humbles a man; it mellows him; it gladdens him; it motivates him; it sustains him; it redeems him; and it exalts him.

claim: Apologetic address to non-member guests on the apostasy and restoration; no content on any axis (the only 'exalt' is Paul's 'man of sin').
Science-and-testimony sermon; quotes Moses 1 on innumerable created worlds and refers generically to the power to save and exalt, without touching plurality of Gods or increase.
quote: Think also of the power of the resurrection, when the elements that have gone back to mother earth can be assembled and united with the spirit to form a perfect, resurrected body; the power to save and exalt in the kingdom of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Sermon on obedience to law; the Father shares 'all that the Father has' including 'even exaltations' — bare theosis with no increase or ancestry claim.
quote: The gospel is a great system of laws — which laws are eternal principles by which our Father in heaven designs to save mankind, his sons and his daughters, and not only to save them, but also to share with them all that the Father has — associations with those we love, honor, powers, glory, dominions, and even exaltations.

claim: Sermon on sanctifying oneself; asserts strongly but generically that perfect obedience would bring us to the powers of God — bare theosis, no increase or regress content.
quote: Could we make a perfect effort at that, of course, we would eventually attain to the powers of God, for that is the promise which he has given us.

claim: Statement of Church beliefs and objectives for a foreign government; exaltation in the celestial kingdom is named as the goal but never unpacked.
quote: But if you mean by going to heaven, gaining exaltation in the celestial kingdom of our Father, where God and Christ dwell, then the answer must be yes.

claim: Rich but strictly theosis-only sermon on the 'four dimensions' of eternal life: a celestial body and a celestial mind 'that thinks like God,' offspring becoming like the parent — no eternal increase, Heavenly Mother, divine ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: The plan of eternal progression contemplates that the offspring may ultimately become like the parent, and therefore fulfils the scripture which says that "men are that they might have joy,"

claim: Sermon on faith; exaltation appears once as God's generic power to save and exalt the human family.
quote: Man's faith in God is an acknowledgment of God's power to save and exalt the human family.

claim: Enumerates twenty-three distinctive features of Mormonism; 'eternal progression' and 'exaltation' are listed as items but described only as an everlasting becoming and assurance of resurrection.
quote: Item 7. The Idea of Eternal Progression. An everlasting becoming!

claim: Address on how the Church differs from other Christian churches; the doctrine-of-Deity section argues only for a personal, material, comprehensible God and a Godlike status for man — no increase, ancestry, or divine-progression claim.
quote: Because the Father called us sons and the Savior called us brothers, we posit for man an exalted Godlike status with almost limitless possibilities.

claim: Sermon on personal responsibility and free agency; exaltation and 'limitless progress hereafter' appear only as undeveloped closing terms.
quote: For beyond our Savior's saving grace no one stands between us and our own salvation — or exaltation.

claim: Lee reads Joseph Smith's DHC gloss on D&C 132 into General Conference expressly to settle 'some misunderstanding as to just what the Lord meant' — that those sealed by priesthood authority will have children after the resurrection and those not sealed will cease to increase; explicit B2 new offspring in the celestial glory.
quote: Except a man and his wife enter into an everlasting covenant, and are married for eternity while in this probation, by the power and authority of the Holy Priesthood, they will cease to increase when they die; that is, they will not have any children after the resurrection. But those who are married by the power and authority of the priesthood in this life, and continue without committing the sin against the Holy Ghost, will continue to increase and have children in the celestial glory.

claim: Sabbath-observance sermon ('Father's Day'); quotes D&C 76:58 'they are gods, even the sons of God' and says honoring God makes one like God — bare theosis only.
quote: when one honors God he tends to become like God, and thereby helps to bring about his own eternal exaltation.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith on Sabbath observance; exaltation in the celestial kingdom named twice as the stake, never described.
quote: We have no right to transgress this law or any one of the other laws that are so fundamental to our exaltation, and how can the members of the Church expect to receive salvation and exaltation in the celestial kingdom of God, and show contempt for his sacred commandments?

claim: Sermon on the oath and covenant of the priesthood; states the standard couple-exaltation rule and refers in passing to 'the Gods' who share priesthood authority, but makes no claim about eternal increase, God's ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: No man can be saved and exalted in the kingdom of God without the woman, and no woman can reach perfection and exaltation in the kingdom of God alone.

claim: Easter address on the resurrection and the restored gospel; exaltation appears once as a conditional blessing with no content.
quote: But we must not assume because of this promise that regardless of what we may do we shall have exaltation and eternal life.

claim: Sermon to youth on choosing the right; premortal life, exaltation in the celestial world, and families perpetuated forever are all asserted only in generic form.
quote: How glorious is the doctrine that man was in the beginning with God! How glorious is the doctrine that families may be perpetuated forever!

claim: Sermon on being sanctified through the blood of the Lamb; exaltation and celestial glory are the frame but receive no specification of increase, godhood, or divine ancestry.
quote: Through the plan of salvation, or the gospel of Jesus Christ, he made it possible for all people who would receive him and the gospel the opportunity to work out their exaltation.

claim: Ivins states that men who fully live up to the Melchizedek Priesthood 'shall become gods with the power of eternal increase' — godhood plus eternal increase named as the concrete content of the 'pearl of great price'.
quote: All that our Father hath shall be given to him who magnifies that calling, and that means that he shall take his wife to the temple, because we are told also that men who succeed in fully living up to all of the privileges and responsibilities of the Melchizedek Priesthood shall become gods with the power of eternal increase.

claim: Extended address to 'Nicodemus'; exaltation is equated with the Lord's 'rest' and with rising to be a king with a great dominion — bare theosis imagery, no increase or ancestry.
quote: but is offering you citizenship in the kingdom of heaven, eventually to rise in stature and authority until you are a king in your own right with a dominion greater than the combined empires of all the earth.

claim: The Presiding Patriarch states flatly that in the premortal celestial kingdom we lived with our heavenly parents and 'knew how our Heavenly Father came to his exaltation' — asserting that the Father himself arrived at exaltation, alongside a plural heavenly-parents assertion.
quote: We are all children of our heavenly parents. We lived with them in the celestial kingdom. We walked by sight. We knew what the celestial glory was. As spirits only, we could not partake of the fulness thereof. We knew how our Heavenly Father came to his exaltation.

claim: Argument that there is only one true church and one gospel plan; exaltation is named as the stake but never described.
quote: Exaltation is founded upon true faith and good works, for it is by works that faith is made perfect.

claim: Brief remarks on accepting a new calling; a single closing reference to the possibility of exaltation.
quote: and that through his atonement we will have salvation and also the possibilities of exaltation through our acts.

claim: Sermon on rearing children; ties exaltation to having a family but frames it as mortal parental duty, not eternal increase.
quote: Without the family we shall not attain exaltation, as I understand exaltation to be. And of course without children the family would not be very much.

claim: Historical address on prophets, Israel, and America; the one doctrinal flash is a strong but bare theosis statement that man is latently a God.
quote: The eternal truth that man is himself a God in latent power had long been forgotten, for the religion of Jesus Christ had taught faith in the possibility of ascent from height to height.

claim: Sermon on the uses of adversity; the only exaltation language is the quoted D&C 121 promise and a play on it.
quote: So, in adversity we may have that which will exalt us, or we may have that which will degrade us.

claim: Priesthood-session talk on traffic safety and gambling; exaltation named only as the upside of honoring the priesthood.
quote: On the other hand, only men who hold the Priesthood can aspire to the highest things of life, and that is the balance — to use this Priesthood to reach exaltation in the Eternal Presence or to abuse it and lose it and be cast out.

claim: In a broadcast address aimed at non-members Romney reports as doctrine that Joseph Smith called God an 'exalted man' of flesh and bone, names the doctrine of eternal progression, and frames man's becoming like God on the analogy of mortal children becoming like their mortal parents.
quote: In after years Joseph referred to God as an "exalted man," and said that both he and the Son were personages of flesh and bone, as tangible as man.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith on covenants, the Holy Ghost, and sons of perdition; exaltation in the kingdom is referenced generically several times.
quote: Baptism and confirmation into the Church do not necessarily insure our exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: Report on missionary work; exaltation appears only inside the summary of the missionary message.
quote: That our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, is the Redeemer of this world, and through his atonement mankind is assured of salvation and has the possibilities of exaltation;

claim: Address on youth standards and temple marriage; exaltation in the celestial kingdom is named as the hoped-for end, without content.
quote: And we hope that they will then continue to live worthily so as to eventually be exalted in the celestial kingdom of our Heavenly Father.

claim: President McKay on youth fitness, parental duty, and the Word of Wisdom; a single generic reference to exaltation in the life to come.
quote: The restored gospel is a rational philosophy that teaches men how to get happiness in this life and exaltation in the life to come.

claim: Sermon on gratitude; divine sonship and the opportunity of exaltation are both stated in generic terms.
quote: Finally, I am deeply grateful for the knowledge that I am truly a spiritual son of our Heavenly Father, created in his image and after his own likeness

claim: Sermon on accepting modern revelation; exaltation appears twice as the generic reward of obedience to the revelations.
quote: These commandments are revelations from God which provide the laws and ordinances of the gospel, and by obedience to them will exalt man in the presence of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Sermon on the purpose of life and the commandments; premortal life with the Father of our spirits and exaltation in the world to come are both left generic.
quote: There is a Kingdom, and there is a King. And there are requirements for citizenship in the Kingdom — commandments, laws, ordinances, and obligations, and what is required of us for peace in this world, and exaltation in the world to come, is to follow him and keep his commandments.

claim: Two Lamanite conversion narratives from Guatemala; the closing line about working out eternal exaltation is the only axis-adjacent phrase.
quote: If we will follow his leadership in all things, we will work out our eternal exaltation.

claim: George Q. Morris expounds D&C 132 and glosses it in his own voice: those who reject celestial marriage are saved but 'cannot be enlarged' and are permanently stripped of 'eternal increase,' which he names the greatest power of exalted beings, tying godhood to 'a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.'
quote: They may be saved in the celestial kingdom, but they cannot be enlarged, and forever and ever they remain a person of a lower degree — a lower order of being, stripped of the greatest power, that of eternal increase.

claim: Sterling W. Sill praises the Bible as a source of great ideas and name-drops 'the doctrine of eternal progression' and 'individual exaltation' without developing either.
quote: Think of the profit our lives would show if we could absorb the lessons of the great parables, or the philosophy of the Golden Rule, or the spirit of man's individual responsibility to God, or the stimulation contained in the doctrine of eternal progression.

claim: Eldred G. Smith on how testimony comes; refers generically to the spirit's pre-existence and closes with the standard promise of 'blessings of exaltation.'
quote: We are made up of a spirit and a physical body. That spirit body lived in the pre-existence, and that spirit that is down inside of us and gives us light is what prompts us to a knowledge of truth.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith on Church membership as the means of salvation and exaltation; closes with generic crowning as sons and daughters of God with no mechanism or regress claim.
quote: There is only one reason for membership in this Church, as I understand it, and that is as a means of receiving salvation and exaltation in the celestial kingdom of God.

claim: Alma Sonne on the practicality of the Sermon on the Mount; the only axis-adjacent words are a formulaic closing wish for exaltation.
quote: May we be true to that sermon, and may we acquit ourselves in such a way that we may be worthy of an exaltation in God's kingdom, I pray, in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: Ezra Taft Benson's report on Soviet communism and American freedom; no theological content on any axis.
quote: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.

claim: J. Reuben Clark contrasts salvation, exaltation and damnation and argues the spirit grows or shrinks in mortality, but makes no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: It makes the difference between salvation and exaltation and damnation.

claim: Richard L. Evans on the search for truth and the everlasting continuance of personality; generic eternal-life language only.
quote: a great sense and assurance of the ultimate objectives and of the everlasting continuance of truth and intelligence and personality

claim: Antoine R. Ivins on teaching testimony to youth; exaltation appears only as the goal secured by priesthood ordinances.
quote: a Church organization to control the use of the privileges of the priesthood in the ordinances that are essential to exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: Henry D. Moyle on missionary work; promises converts they may be 'saved and exalted in the Kingdom of our Heavenly Father as his sons' without further specification.
quote: a promise that we will be saved and exalted in the Kingdom of our Heavenly Father as his sons.

claim: Mark E. Petersen on national honesty and integrity; no axis content.
quote: May we awaken to our responsibility to be honest and true, to exalt honor in our lives and in our thinking, I earnestly pray in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: Sterling W. Sill on parental example as 'spiritual paternity'; the paternity language is metaphorical and human, not theological.
quote: But what about mental paternity and spiritual paternity? Who are the fathers of our ideals, and what kind of fathers do we have for our children's spirituality?

claim: Delbert L. Stapley's litany of faith affirms God as the Father of our spirits in whose image we are made and whose traits and powers we share — the standard divine-sonship formula, without generative or regress claims.
quote: know that he lives, that he is the Father of our spirits, that we are created in the image of his Person, that we possess like traits, qualities, and powers, that we are in very deed his children

claim: Henry D. Taylor on shedding the 'excess baggage' of bad traits en route to perfection; bare theosis via Matthew 5:48.
quote: Our goal should be to become perfect, even as our Father in heaven is perfect.

claim: Antoine R. Ivins testifies that priesthood bearers who magnify their callings 'can eventually attain to the powers of God' — bare theosis with no mechanism.
quote: he who receives these callings in the priesthood and magnifies them fully can eventually attain to the powers of God.

claim: LeGrand Richards on missionary sacrifice and Wilford Woodruff's experiences; no axis content beyond temple ordinances 'for their exaltation.'
quote: before men could receive the holy ordinances of the house of the Lord for their exaltation.

claim: Carl W. Buehner frames the plan of salvation as a choice between God's purpose to exalt mankind and Satan's to degrade it; exaltation is asserted but unspecified.
quote: The primary purpose of our Father in heaven and his only Begotten Son is to exalt mankind.

claim: Marion D. Hanks on the needs of youth and the responsibilities of parents; no axis content.
quote: They need to know that families can be eternal.

claim: Milton R. Hunter argues that the 'Fair God' traditions of ancient America (Quetzalcoatl, Itzamna, Viracocha) are memories of the resurrected Christ; the plural 'gods' are pagan deities, not LDS godhood.
quote: In these Indian traditions the various aboriginal tribes gave different names to this white and bearded God; for example, in Mexico Valley he was called "Quetzalcoatl."

claim: Antoine R. Ivins on missionary work and convert fellowshipping; exaltation appears once as a formulaic destination.
quote: it is a regenerating force which tends to exaltation in the kingdom of God when it is accepted by baptism and when one makes a reasonable effort to live the teachings of God our Heavenly Father.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's Holy Land travelogue closes with the claim that Christ 'established the exaltation' and that we may grow like him in knowledge — bare theosis, no claim about God's own progression.
quote: that the Son of God broke the bands of death and established the exaltation, the way of life, and that we may grow like him in knowledge and perfected eternal life.

claim: Henry D. Moyle grounds missionary work in universal divine sonship and quotes D&C 76:24 that the inhabitants of the worlds 'are begotten sons and daughters unto God'; the begetting is Christ's spiritual rebirth, not new spirit children.
quote: This makes us all brothers and sisters, sons and daughters of God, with his only Begotten Son Jesus Christ, our elder brother.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley paraphrases the King Follett Sermon to define joint-heirship as ascending 'to the station of Godhood,' says 'To become like God we must possess the powers of Godhood,' and makes eternal marriage the condition of Godhood — an exalted condition he says 'assures continuation of the lives forever.'
quote: The everlasting covenant of marriage, ordained of God for man and woman, also is to be entered into and the marriage contract sealed eternally by the authority of the Holy Priesthood of God. Otherwise, the highest degree of the celestial kingdom cannot be attained nor Godhood acquired, which exalted condition assures continuation of the lives forever.

claim: Milton R. Hunter urges Saints to work out their exaltation now; mortality as probation per Abraham 3, no axis-specific claim.
quote: I strongly desire that all Latterday Saints work out their eternal exaltation now while the opportunity is ours.

claim: John Longden reports on chapel dedications in the Pacific and affirms that God is Christ's literal Father and the Father of our spirits — the standard formula, undeveloped.
quote: that we shall have the privilege of dwelling with him and his father — his literal Father and the Father of our spirits eternally.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley catalogs the 'designs of conspiring men' in commerce, science, education and philosophy; no axis content.
quote: I pray, my brothers and sisters, that we will have faith in the revelations and abide by the commandments, warnings, and admonitions which the Lord has given for our guidance, blessing, and exaltation

speaker: Henry D. Taylor
claim: Henry D. Taylor reads the O My Father closing prayer naming Father and Mother in the heavenly courts, alongside the path to exaltation.
Hugh B. Brown on the atonement, framing salvation as an endless process of becoming with eternity in which to pursue knowledge; the progression described is man's, not God's.
quote: Salvation is a continuing, on-going process. It is eternally improving, achieving, becoming — yes, and overcoming.

claim: Hugh B. Brown's priesthood-session sermon on D&C 121 and unrighteous dominion in the home; no axis content.
quote: Brethren of the priesthood, let us never exercise unrighteous dominion.

claim: Henry D. Moyle on Church finances, tithing and building programs; exaltation appears once as the reward of tithing.
quote: With its payment our eternal salvation and exaltation is all but assured.

claim: Henry D. Moyle argues for continuing revelation and Joseph Smith's prophetic role; no axis content.
quote: God has given to us the great plan of salvation whereby men through obedience can bring themselves back into the presence of God, saved and exalted eternally in his kingdom.

claim: Marion G. Romney on the oath and covenant of the priesthood; quotes D&C 76:56-58 that the faithful 'are gods, even the sons of God' and D&C 84:38 that all the Father has shall be given them, but supplies no generative or regress gloss.
quote: "They are they who are priests and kings, who have received of his fulness, and of his glory; "And are priests of the Most High, after the order of . . . the Only Begotten Son. Wherefore, as it is written, they are gods, even the sons of God — "

claim: Eldred G. Smith on baptism for the dead and the duty of genealogical research; exaltation appears only as the stake of neglecting temple work.
quote: To be exalted in the kingdom of God, one must keep all the laws of the gospel and keep all the commandments of God.

claim: David O. McKay on priesthood quorums as instruments of mutual aid; exaltation named only as the purpose priesthood serves.
quote: The Melchizedek Priesthood is power and authority vested in the Godhead and delegated to man for the progress, happiness, salvation, and exaltation of the human family.

claim: Henry D. Moyle on conversion and judgment; invokes 2 Peter 1:4 partaking of the divine nature progressively in this life — theosis language without further specification.
quote: We can become partakers of the divine nature progressively from the beginning of our conversion throughout the remainder of our faithful lives.

claim: Eldred G. Smith reads Job as a graduated program of testing by which men 'become perfect'; perfection and exaltation are asserted generically.
quote: For us to become perfect, in addition to performing the ordinances of the gospel, we must also have the strength that the Lord might say to Satan in reference to us

claim: Ezra Taft Benson on national righteousness, statism and the Constitution; the only premortal reference is a passing allusion to fighting for freedom in the pre-existence.
quote: May we be at least as valiant for freedom and righteousness, here and now, as we were when we fought for these principles in the pre-existence.

claim: Hugh B. Brown on excellence, education and agency; no axis content.
quote: Freedom of choice is a basic principle of the gospel. This was true even before the earth was created.

claim: ElRay L. Christiansen on individual salvation, loving neighbors, tithing and vicarious work; exaltation appears only formulaically.
quote: secure our individual and collective salvation and perhaps exaltation

claim: Alvin R. Dyer on the First Vision and the restoration; refers to God's plan in the pre-existence 'for the redemption and exaltation of his spirit children' — humans as God's spirit children, the standard formula, with no forward generative chain.
quote: all truths, all laws, all covenants, all promises planned by God our Heavenly Father in the pre-existence and revealed to man in part at various times in mortality for the redemption and exaltation of his spirit children, were now to be fully revealed and made available to mankind.

claim: Milton R. Hunter's letter to his son quotes the 1909 First Presidency statement that man, 'the undeveloped offspring of celestial parentage,' is capable of 'evolving into a God' — a strong but bare theosis formulation (borderline; no regress, no spirit offspring, no claim about God's own progression).
quote: Man is a child of God, formed in the divine image and endowed with divine attributes, and even as the infant son of an earthly father and mother is capable in due time of becoming a man, so the undeveloped offspring of celestial parentage is capable, by experience through ages of aeons, of evolving into a God.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's survey of the Book of Mormon's contents and appeal for its readers; no axis content.
quote: But after all, it is not the book's dramatic crises, its history, its narrative that are so important, but its power to transform men into Christlike beings worthy of exaltation.

claim: Harold B. Lee's priesthood correlation report on the new home teaching program; administrative, no axis content.
quote: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is being divinely led and offers happiness eternal life and exaltation for all who are willing to learn and to live its principles.

claim: LeGrand Richards on the restoration and missionary growth; notes the premortal spirits understood the gospel before the world was organized and that exaltation requires accepting it.
quote: we know that the gospel was understood by the spirits which were with our Father in heaven before the world was formed or organized.

claim: Marion G. Romney on the Lamanite covenants and their latter-day fulfillment; no axis content.
quote: It is concerning the covenants the Lord made with their fathers which run in favor of the Lamanites and culminate in their blossoming as the rose that I wish to speak.

claim: Eldred G. Smith lists truths knowable by the Holy Ghost, including a one-line 'true concept of Deity' — God as 'an Exalted Being' with Christ literally begotten (borderline wording; no claim that God attained that status through progression).
quote: Then you may also know of the true concept of Deity. God is truly an Exalted Being. Jesus Christ is literally his Begotten Son.

claim: N. Eldon Tanner defends the literal divine sonship and bodily resurrection of Christ against mythologizing readings; the paternity at issue is Christ's, not the Father's own ancestry.
quote: deny him the divine parentage and sonship of God, drag Christianity down to the level of paganism and completely wipe out the true God and his plan of redemption for his children.

claim: Hugh B. Brown narrates the premortal council: all men existed as intelligences with spirit bodies of which God was universal Father, Jehovah was the Firstborn, and mortality would bring 'the Godlike power of procreation' — suggestive but undeveloped, with no assertion of postmortal spirit offspring.
quote: At a time far antedating Eden, the spirits of all men had a primeval existence and were intelligences with spirit bodies of which God was universal Father.

claim: Antoine R. Ivins on faith, service and overcoming bad habits; exaltation appears once as re-entering God's presence 'in an exalted estate.'
quote: It was then possible, through death and the resurrection, for man to re-enter the presence of God in an exalted estate.

claim: LeGrand Richards on the great apostasy and the restoration of the everlasting gospel; no axis content.
quote: Thus men were again empowered by ordination to perform holy ordinances here upon the earth necessary for the salvation and exaltation of men so that such ordinances would be binding in the heavens

claim: Alvin R. Dyer on conviction, repentance and the Word of Wisdom; exaltation named only as the endpoint of conviction.
quote: Here is a power that can lead to the highest pinnacle of achievement in mortality and to exaltation in immortality.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball on knowing God and the protection required to endure his glory; says the restored program 'can carry men to exaltation and eternal life all the way to Godhood' and enumerates 'three Gods' of the Godhead — strong theosis wording, but no regress, no spirit offspring, no claim about God's own progression.
quote: But in our day, the whole eternal program is here and can carry men to exaltation and eternal life all the way to Godhood.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith on chastity and modesty; includes the standard 'fortunate fall' argument that without the fall Adam and Eve would have had no posterity, but makes no claim about divine procreation.
quote: The fact is clear, however, had Adam not partaken he and Eve would have lived alone without posterity.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley on the kingdom of God as the vehicle of man's perfecting; frames eternal life as 'a life like unto that of God' and growth 'toward Godlikeness' without generative or regress claims.
quote: it places one on the road to God — to enjoy a life like unto that of God, which is eternal life.

claim: N. Eldon Tanner's summary of LDS belief affirms an embodied God with 'body, parts, and passions' who is 'the Father of the spirits of all mankind' — the standard formula, with no ancestry or progression claim attached.
quote: The God we believe in is a Living God with body, parts, and passions, in whose image we were made, who is the Father of the spirits of all mankind, and under whose direction the world was created and all things therein.

claim: Hugh B. Brown on the apostasy, the dilemma of derived authority, and the restoration; answers the question of man's origin with the bare statement that man is a spirit child of God commanded to become perfect.
quote: Man is a spirit child of God. Man is here to gain strength in choosing between right and wrong, to obey the command, "Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect."

claim: A sermon on placing trust in God rather than man that mentions temple 'saving and exalting ordinances' only in passing, with no specific claim about exaltation, parenthood, or divine progression.
quote: We have the saving and exalting ordinances which are administered by proper authority in holy temples.

claim: Dyer's talk on continuing revelation includes a single generic remark that obedience to the commandments will exalt man in God's presence, with no specific claim about theosis, divine parentage, or divine progression.
quote: The commandments given by revelations from God provide the laws and ordinances of the gospel, and obedience thereto will exalt man in the presence of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Extended eternal-marriage sermon: temple sealing is required for exaltation and for 'increase', with the unsealed remaining 'angels of God' — but the treatment is the mainstream theosis/eternal-marriage frame with no specification of spirit offspring, regress, or divine progression.
quote: How sad to be separate and single and apart through countless ages when one could, by meeting requirements, have happy marriage for eternity in the temple by proper authority and continue on in everincreasing joy and happiness, growth and development toward Godhood.

claim: A CBS Church of the Air address calling Americans to love God and neighbor amid rising crime and materialism; the only doctrinal touch is man created in God's image.
Benson's talk on acting without being commanded, freedom, and the war in heaven touches theosis only in a single generic aside that self-directed initiative 'prepares men for godhood.'
quote: This attitude prepares men for godhood.

claim: A survey of restored-gospel doctrine that affirms premortal existence, divine parentage of all men, and exaltation on condition of obedience, but only in generic mainstream terms with no specific claim about spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: All men, sons and daughters of divine parents, are on this earth to experience an enlarged sphere of interest and activity in a terrestrial world preliminary to entrance into celestial glory.

claim: Longden expounds the first principles and ordinances of the gospel — faith, repentance, baptism by immersion, and the laying on of hands for the gift of the Holy Ghost.
A talk on safeguards against juvenile delinquency that touches exaltation only as the gospel's promised end.
quote: The gospel is a rational philosophy that teaches mankind how to attain happiness in this life and exaltation in the life to come.

claim: Counsel to high-school youth on dating standards, parental supervision, and honoring father and mother, with only a passing reference to marriage as an eternal covenant.
Taylor's sermon on fellowship and not standing alone mentions exaltation only as a generic goal of Church members working out their salvation together.
quote: As members of the Church, we are traveling along the same highway, each one working out his own salvation, with exaltation and eternal life in the celestial kingdom as the goal.

claim: A sermon on obedience to civil law and continuing revelation that closes with a bare, generic reference to attaining salvation and exaltation through obedience to divine law.
quote: I bear my testimony unto you that God has revealed his mind and will unto man in our own modern day, restoring divine laws, by obedience to which man can attain salvation and exaltation; that since the heralding of this last and greatest dispensation of the gospel of Jesus Christ by Joseph Smith unto this very minute, living prophets have been in communication with God for the salvation of the human race and have presided over his Church and kingdom here upon the earth for this purpose.

claim: Lee warns of apostasy, betrayal from within, and coming trials, urging the Saints to gain a personal testimony and stand in holy places.

Sustained treatment of premortal spirit childhood, eternal progress, and becoming godlike/perfect as the Father is, but entirely at the generic theosis level with no generative, regress, or divine-progression content.
quote: How much learning and how many experiences do we need to become godlike?

claim: Romney's sermon on making one's calling and election sure defines eternal life as the kind of life God enjoys and calls men God's offspring, but makes no specific claim about generative exaltation, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: Eternal life is the quality of life which God himself enjoys.

claim: Sill asserts a same-species ontology between God and man — God, angels, spirits, and men differ only in stage of development — and quotes B. H. Roberts at length that no limit can be fixed on the resurrected 'Godmen's' progress.
quote: We will understand the great scriptural teaching that God, angels, spirits, and men are all of the same species in different stages of righteousness and development.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith teaches that couples who willfully avoid parenthood in mortality forfeit the blessing of eternal increase in the next life, tying eternal posterity directly to the marriage covenant, and that only through mortal birth and resurrection can spirits become like the Eternal Father.
quote: If the responsibilities of parenthood are willfully avoided here, then how can the Lord bestow upon the guilty the blessings of eternal increase?

claim: Eldred G. Smith gives practical counsel on choosing associates who live Church standards so young people will qualify for temple marriage and generically named blessings of exaltation, without specifying what exaltation consists of.
quote: so that when the time comes and they are ready, they may go to the house of the Lord to be sealed for time and eternity and open the door of opportunity of receiving the blessings of exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: A testimony of God as Creator and Christ as Redeemer, with exaltation named only as the promised reward of the faithful.
quote: He offered the plan by which we may enter his kingdom and receive the exaltation promised to the faithful.

claim: Stapley expounds the parable of the pearl of great price as the kingdom of God, using exaltation only as a generic synonym for the goal of the gospel plan.
quote: Allegorically the Savior likens the kingdom of heaven unto the merchantman seeking goodly pearls, signifying that the true pearl of great price is God's kingdom which, for man to be happy and exalted, he must diligently seek.

claim: Tuttle's counsel to youth on honoring the priesthood refers to exaltation only generically, as the destination toward which priesthood power moves people.
quote: I have come to realize that by virtue of the priesthood which we hold, we do have more power to save ourselves and ultimately others than any earthly ruler, for power to move oneself or others toward exaltation comes only from God — from whence this priesthood comes.

claim: A sermon against avarice and in favor of tithing; exaltation appears only as a stock phrase inside a quoted Brigham Young statement that the law of tithing exists for the people's salvation and exaltation.
quote: It is an eternal law that God has instituted for the benefit of the human family, for their salvation and exaltation.

claim: Burton urges the three-generation temple-record program, describing vicarious ordinances as exalting the dead into God's presence but never specifying what exaltation consists of.
quote: This record containing the completed temple ordinances is a sacrifice of the living for those of their dead loved ones to bind them into the family of Jesus Christ — not only to be redeemed from death, but also, if accepted, exalting them into the very presence of God the Eternal Father.

claim: Frames the gospel as a plan for exalting man to 'an eternal creative opportunity with his Father,' but the phrase is an unelaborated gloss on theosis and asserts no spirit offspring or divine genealogy.
quote: The gospel is God's plan for the exalting of man to an eternal creative opportunity with his Father through giving him a vision of his great origins and heritage, his purposes and responsibilities, and his inspiring potential.

claim: A short priesthood-meeting address on the duty to serve others, noting only in passing that priesthood is the means through which exaltation comes.
quote: In fact, priesthood blesses us in two ways: first, it is the means through which exaltation comes to those who hold it; second, it is to be used in behalf of others that they also may be blessed.

claim: Brown teaches that under the law of 'like begets like' human progress through the eternities may be limitless, that faithful families will be crowned with eternal increase, and quotes Lorenzo Snow on celestial couples standing amid their posterity administering life and glory world without end.
quote: President Lorenzo Snow gave an intimation of what eternal marriage meant: "A man and a woman in the other life, having celestial bodies, free from sickness and disease, glorified and beautified beyond description, standing in the midst of their posterity, governing and controlling them, administering life, exaltation and glory, world without end."

claim: Theodore M. Burton argues from premortal existence and temple sealing to the necessity of eternal family life, but keeps the claims generic — spirit children of God, eternal companionship, and Christ exalting us into the Father's presence — with no assertion of spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: I know that it is the divine method by which Jesus Christ can exalt us into the presence of God the Eternal Father, and I bear you this witness in the name of Jesus Christ.

claim: Dunn distinguishes man's eternal, primal self from the spirit body it was later born into with God as its eternal father — a compact statement of tripartite staging (eternal self → spirit birth → mortality) — and grounds human divine potential in that literal descent.
quote: His eternal, primal self was born into a spirit body of which God is the eternal father.

claim: On tapping divine spiritual power through prayer, obedience, and recognizing revelation; exaltation appears only as a word inside a quoted 1942 First Presidency wartime message.

Joseph Fielding Smith defends the Fall as an essential part of the plan that let pre-existent spirits obtain bodies, then warns of latter-day judgments; exaltation appears only as a generic reward of thrones and kingdoms.
quote: Here we are tried, tempted, and proved to be either worthy of exaltation to thrones and kingdoms or partakers of his displeasure and thus assigned to some lesser kingdom.

claim: Burton's administrative counsel on temple attendance and quorum teaching invokes exaltation only generically as the blessing temple ordinances open to the living and the dead.
quote: This, then, requires genealogical activity to identify our kindred dead for whom we can then perform those temple ordinances that will open the doors of exaltation for them also.

claim: A sermon on obedience to God and to priesthood authority; exaltation appears only once as a generic aim of righteous living.
quote: Our leaders ask us to do right, to live pure lives, to do good to all men and evil to no one, and to respect the order of God's kingdom, that salvation and exaltation may come to all.

claim: Critchlow closes his seven-act drama analogy by stating that resurrected celestial exaltation carries not only eternal life but the power of eternal increase and a continuation of the seeds, and frames mortality as the point at which God's spirit children first receive powers of procreation.
quote: That glory holds a promise of eternal life, the power of eternal increase, a continuation of the seeds.

claim: A Tabernacle-centennial history and tribute to the pioneers, closing with generic exhortations to keep the faith.
Monson retells David and Goliath and applies it to conquering personal weaknesses with five stones of courage, effort, humility, prayer, and duty.

Stapley's sermon on building 'a house that will bear the weight of eternal life' rehearses the three degrees of glory in D&C 76 and speaks of exaltation only in the standard celestial-inheritance terms, with no claim about divine parenthood, ancestry, or God's own progression.
quote: They are priests and kings of the most high and receive of the fullness of God's glory.

claim: A political address on the breakdown of law and order, national moral erosion, federal spending, and the Communist threat to American freedom, with no content on exaltation, eternal parenthood, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
Hanks preaches human potential through believing, belonging, giving, and loving, with only a generic reference to divine attributes present in us in embryo.
quote: The major source of our self-image should be our Heavenly Father, whose children we are, in whose image we are made, whose attributes and qualities we have within us in embryo.

claim: Counsel to young women on chastity and temple marriage that frames motherhood as partnership with God in providing bodies for His previously created spirits and calls the man-woman pair 'God's equation for exaltation' — mortal procreation and the sealing requirement, not exalted couples begetting new spirit children.
quote: Can any young woman remain unmoved in the thought that within her is the potential of creation, of providing earthly bodies for spirits previously created by him?

claim: Sonne surveys the restored gospel as the plan to save and exalt mankind and affirms generically that man is a child of God endowed with the Father's attributes and moving toward perfection.
quote: A human being is therefore more than a physical creation; he is also a spiritual being endowed with the attributes of his Heavenly Father.

claim: Stapley's talk on light, truth, and opposing forces refers to man as 'the spirit offspring of Deity' and to exaltation in the life to come, but only as mainstream background to a sermon on obedience.
quote: The glory of God being intelligence, then the glory of man, the spirit offspring of Deity, must also be intelligence, for man is God's greatest and most important creation.

claim: A charge to the seventies to befriend and teach neighbors; exaltation appears only as a generic aim of obedience and in the closing testimony that Christ authors our salvation and exaltation.
quote: The Lord Jesus Christ lives and is the author of our salvation and our exaltation.

claim: Burton argues that accurate Church records plus righteous living are both required to claim exaltation in the celestial kingdom, treating exaltation only as an undefined reward.
quote: Only when you know the proper password and have a valid identification of yourself and your lineage can you enter through the gates of heaven to claim your eternal exaltation.

claim: Kimball states that the knowledge accumulated in mortality is needed by exalted beings in order to create worlds and furnish them, specifying world-creation as the concrete content of exaltation rather than leaving deification generic.
quote: We shall need all of the accumulated secular knowledge in order to create worlds and to furnish them, but only through the "mysteries of God" and these hidden treasures of knowledge may we arrive at the place and condition where we may use that knowledge in creation and exaltation.

claim: McConkie argues the true gospel is both word and power, describing it in passing as the Father's plan by which His spirit children may progress and become like Him — general theosis with no claim about spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: That is, God himself, the Father of us all, created the gospel; it is his plan of salvation through which all his spirit children, Christ included, have power to progress and become like him; it is the plan announced by the Father in the councils of eternity when he asked whom he should send to be the Redeemer, to put into full force the terms and conditions of his gospel; it is the plan of which Christ became the chief advocate, first in preexistence and then again in mortality, thereby gaining the distinction of having the very "gospel of God" itself named after him, named "the gospel of Christ."

claim: Packer describes the purposes and history of general conference, who attends and who speaks, and urges hearers to heed prophetic counsel.

Joseph Fielding Smith's testimony of the restored gospel and the growth of the kingdom, in which exaltation appears only in generic form — the gospel makes us sons and daughters of God worthy to dwell in the Almighty's presence — with no claim about spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: The gospel of Jesus Christ is the perfect law of liberty; it will lead man to the highest state of glory and exalt him in the presence of our Heavenly Father if he is willing to listen to the counsels of those whom the Lord has appointed to guide them.

claim: Sonne, expounding the Articles of Faith, quotes Bruce R. McConkie's flat species-identity claim that man and God belong to the same race and immediately draws the deification inference from it.
quote: "Man and God are of the same race," said President Bruce R. McConkie.

claim: A call to sound doctrine that affirms we are literal spirit children of God who can become like Him, but only at the generic theosis level.
quote: Jesus taught that as the spirit children of the Father, with that spark of divinity in us, we can become like him by keeping his commandments.

claim: Vandenberg preaches the law of the harvest and youth involvement, using exaltation only as a generic reward for sowing righteousness.
quote: If we plant seeds of righteousness and cultivate them properly, we reap peace, joy, and exaltation; but conversely, if we plant seeds of avarice, hate, and lust, we reap the whirlwind of sorrow and anguish.

claim: Brown, paraphrasing B. H. Roberts, takes a specific position on premortal staging — men existed as intelligences that were never created and cannot be, identifying that uncreated self-existent entity with the spirit or soul — and describes God as 'an exalted, perfected, and glorified Being' still in human form.
quote: These intelligences were not created or made, neither indeed can they be; the intelligent entity in man which we call spirit or soul is a self-existing entity, uncreated and eternal.

claim: A sermon of comfort in adversity that refers generically to the premortally accepted plan leading to salvation and exaltation and to each person achieving a divine destiny, without any specific claim on the exaltation axes.
quote: Indeed, it is the only plan that leads men to salvation and exaltation.

claim: Howard W. Hunter expounds 1 Corinthians 15 on the literal resurrection of a body of flesh and bones quickened by spirit instead of blood, with only a passing generic reference to eternal exaltation.
quote: The propositions of ethics may be noble, but they lack those elements of the gospel that lead men to eternal exaltation.

claim: An apologetic testimony of the Book of Mormon's origin, witnesses, and divinity; 'exaltation' appears once in a subordinate clause about restored ordinances.

Kimball's Easter testimony of the literal resurrection quotes Joseph Smith's promise that the faithful will be resurrected and become like Gods reigning in celestial kingdoms — bare theosis with no claim about spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: Hold out to the end; and we shall be resurrected and become like Gods, and reign in celestial kingdoms, principalities and eternal dominions. . . .

claim: Answering a member who could not believe 'that God himself was once as we are now,' Lee defends the King Follett statement as strengthened by John 5:19 and by Brigham Young's 'has had a body and been on an earth,' then quotes Young that every faithful man becomes 'a father of fathers' whose kingdom is his own progeny and that every God in all the eternities rules by means of his progeny — while simultaneously invoking 'If You Could Hie to Kolob' and Young's 'instead of inquiring after the origin of the Gods' to bar speculation past the revealed curtain, and affirming that God 'knoweth all things.'
quote: Every man who is faithful and gets a salvation and glory, and becomes a king of kings and Lord of Lords, or a father of fathers, it will be by the increase of his own progeny.

claim: Missionary-work address; touches exaltation only generically, saying converts will receive temple 'ordinances of exaltation' and become kings and priests.
quote: That is, before the millennial era, before the time when Christ shall reign personally upon the earth, the elect of God among every kindred, the saints who speak every tongue, the converts among all peoples and nations, having first believed the restored gospel, will go to the temples of God and receive the ordinances of exaltation whereby they qualify to become kings and priests.

claim: Repentance/integrity sermon; the sole brush with the axes is the stock phrase 'the exaltation of man' inside a gloss on Proverbs 6, with no claim about the nature or origin of God.

Generic exaltation-as-reward framing: celestial kingdom and exaltation require keeping the whole law, with fullness of the Father promised, but no specific claim about becoming God, parenthood, ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: To enter the celestial and obtain exaltation, it is necessary that the whole law be kept.

claim: Generic Easter/Christ-centered address; mentions in passing that the Savior's pattern of life will 'save and exalt his children' and that we are God's offspring, with no specific claim about becoming like God.
quote: The Lord Jesus set before us the only pattern of life which will save and exalt his children.

claim: Sermon on the power of example; 'exaltation and eternal life' appears only as an undefined goal-state, with no claim about becoming like God, divine parenthood, or divine progression.
quote: This church is true; it has value and is meaningful to those seeking exaltation and eternal life.

claim: S. Dilworth Young teaches that exaltation includes becoming a creator of worlds — God's most magnificent creations 'may be duplicated' by the exalted, who will master eternal physics, chemistry, and biology.
quote: In the gospel of Christ he offers us the opportunity to become not just gazers into the wonders of the heavens, but creators of them.

claim: Victor L. Brown states the tripartite staging explicitly: humans existed first as intelligences, then as spirit children of Heavenly Father, before mortal birth.
quote: It was interesting to note that these young people were thrilled with the knowledge that they had existed as intelligences and then as spirit children of their Heavenly Father before they were born into this life.

claim: A repentance sermon; touches theosis only in passing via the moral "become like unto him" challenge and a bare mention of hoping for exaltation, with no specific deification, parenthood, ancestry, or progression claim.
quote: This fits, it seems to me, the ennobling challenge of the Christ to become like unto him.

claim: Generic theosis only: we are God's spirit children who may 'advance and progress and become like him'; no specific claim on any axis.
quote: He is our Father in heaven; we are his spirit children, and he ordained the laws whereby we can advance and progress and become like him.

claim: Space-age meditation on God's numberless creations and the worth of souls; only bare theosis language ('you approach divinity, and eventually you may achieve that high exaltation'), no divine parenthood, regress, or progression claim.
quote: You alone are responsible, and by wielding and exercising that freedom of choice, you grow in character, you grow in intelligence, you approach divinity, and eventually you may achieve that high exaltation.

claim: Whole talk is generic theosis ('man is to be like God') built on Matt. 5:48 and 1 John 3:2, with a single stock aside that God is an exalted embodied man; no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: When I learned the truth — that God is an exalted man of flesh and bone and spirit — then I understood what John was saying: that love is God's distinguishing characteristic.

claim: Talk on the gospel of work; uses 'exaltation in the celestial kingdom' and 'spirit children of God' only as undefined goal/status labels, with no specific claim on any axis.
quote: Thus, we need not hesitate to establish our long-term objective as exaltation in the celestial kingdom, or eternal life.

claim: Talk on adversity and affliction; exaltation appears only as a generic reward term in quoted scripture and Joseph Smith material, with no claim about theosis mechanics, divine ancestry, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: We are aware, however, that should all men accept and live his teachings, adversity and affliction would still abound because, in the words of the Prophet Joseph Smith, "Men have to suffer that they may come upon Mount Zion and be exalted above the heavens." (Documentary History of the Church, Vol. 5, p. 556.)

claim: Sill asserts an ontological species-identity between God and humanity — God, angels, spirits, and men are one species differing only in stage of development — a specific formulation of theosis rather than a bare "become like God" statement.
quote: It is helpful for us to remember that God, angels, spirits, and men are all of the same species in different stages of development and in various degrees of righteousness.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith on the purpose of mortal existence; 'exaltation in the kingdom of God' used only as a generic reward-state, with no divinization mechanics, parenthood, regress, or progression content.
quote: Men can only be saved and exalted in the kingdom of God in righteousness; therefore, we must repent of our sins and walk in the light as Christ is in the light, that his blood may cleanse us from all sins and that we may have fellowship with the Lord and receive of his glory and exaltation.

claim: Dispensation-of-the-fulness-of-times address; 'salvation and exaltation' is generic, and the 'same God yesterday, today, and forever' side-head is a quoted D&C 20 proof that God still calls prophets, not a claim about divine immutability versus progression.
quote: Like unto other great prophets of ages past, in the pattern of God's way, there awaited this earnest young prophet, as also upon subsequent divinely appointed occasions, the revelation of eternal truths from God necessary for man's salvation and exaltation.

speaker: Bruce R. McConkie
claim: Bruce R. McConkie calls O My Father one of the Church's great doctrinal hymns and quotes its Mother in Heaven assertion.
Faith/wisdom sermon on James 1:5; exaltation appears only as an unspecified blessing obtained through Christ, with no claim about godhood, offspring, or divine progression.
quote: Don't we all, through the Savior's sacrifice, require his intervention with our Eternal Father and his help to achieve salvation, exaltation, and glory?

claim: A family-strengthening sermon; touches the axes only generically — eternal patriarchal order persisting past the Church, exaltation as something that can be jeopardized, and a scriptural "become like God, knowing good and evil" aside — with no claim about spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: The Church was created in large measure to help the family, and long after the Church has performed its mission, the celestial patriarchal order will still be functioning.

claim: A 1970 general conference address on the nature of God that twice quotes Joseph Smith's God-was-once-a-man teaching approvingly (TPJS 345-46 and DHC 6:305), presenting it as the doctrine that makes God intelligible as a literal Father.
quote: God himself was once as we are now, and is an exalted man, and sits enthroned in yonder heavens!

speaker: Conference record
claim: The King Follett conference record says future gods advance as prior gods have done and that the Father receives higher exaltation through kingdom upon kingdom.

Bullock's notes on Brigham Young's April 6, 1845 baptism-for-the-dead discourse record an endless-progression claim: a man keeps receiving until he attains the fulness of the Godhead, and even after progressing through millions of worlds eternity still lies ahead (fragmentary longhand notes, not a verbatim report).
quote: The Lord leads his people a little at a time, and when a man receives a little he shall continue to receive more, until he obtains to the fulness of the Godhead. When they have progressed through millions of worlds, it is eternity still before them.

claim: Four days of Kanesville conference minutes dominated by business (sustainings, teams and wagons for the westward emigration, thieving, poor relief, education); the only doctrinal touches are generic — Hyde on the Father begetting all human spirits and heirship to all things, Joseph Young on saving and exalting children, Woodruff that God would not know whether to exalt us without mortal probation — none rising to a specific claim on any axis.
quote: the same Fa[the]r who begets our Sp, begets theirs also.

claim: Bullock's minutes plus the First General Epistle: business, weather, tithing and sustainings; the only axis contact is John Taylor's generic 'be like God' / 'be exalted' exhortation, with no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: if we want to be like God - we av. got to learn these things

claim: Bullock's minutes preserve two pointed John Taylor claims: that the God above holds his station because he has been engaged in public enterprise all his days (divine attainment/ongoing activity), and that a man who cannot pay tithing and preach 'cant create a world'; Taylor also frames the Saints as a nucleus of posterity 'worlds without end' who will be kings and priests ruling.
quote: the God that sits above as been all his days engaged in public enterprize as he wod. not av. been there

claim: Conference minutes on San Pete settlement, the Perpetual Emigrating Fund, Orson Hyde's education lecture, sustainings, and Brigham Young's tithing discourse; no exaltation, divine-ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring content.

speaker: Joseph Smith, Jr.
claim: Joseph Smith's King Follett text joins human godhood to the prior Gods who followed the same path and to the Father's increase in kingdoms.

Administrative First Presidency epistle (emigration, crops, settlements, tithing, temple); 'future exaltation' appears once as a generic blessing and the endowment is tied to salvation, but no axis claim is developed.
quote: Beloved Brethren:--Ever mindful of the Redeemer's kingdom and of your interest therein, we gladly improve the present moment in expressing to you our watchfulness and care concerning you, and concerning those things which may tend to your present happiness and future exaltation.

claim: Brigham Young on mothers, child-rearing, and orthography reform; exaltation appears only as a one-clause statement of mortal purpose, with no divine-ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring content.
quote: We are at present low, weak, and groveling in the dark, but we are planted here in weakness for the purpose of exaltation.

claim: Brigham Young's Adam-God discourse: Adam is 'our Father and our God,' he himself took a tabernacle begotten by 'his Father in heaven' with the chain running 'on in succession,' and the Father in heaven begat all the spirits of this earth, who 'were born spirits in the eternal world.'
quote: He is the first of the human family; and when he took a tabernacle, it was begotten by *his Father* in heaven, after the same manner as the tabernacles of Cain, Abel, and the rest of the sons and daughters of Adam and Eve; from the fruits of the earth, the first earthly tabernacles were originated by the Father, and so on in succession.

claim: Brigham Young promises the faithful 'eternal lives,' rule over kingdoms, and 'power to be Gods,' with the corollary that the worldly class becomes servants to those sons of God in eternity — plural godhood with dominion, not bare likeness to God.
quote: They shall reign over kingdoms, and have power to be Gods, even the sons of God.

claim: Dedication/consecration sermon; 'exaltation' appears only as a generic synonym for the reward of consecrating oneself, with no claim about godhood, divine parentage, or divine progression.
quote: This is what you must do to obtain an exaltation.

claim: Short list of conference 'texts' (temple, wall, colonizing, wheat); the only axis-adjacent phrase is a generic reference to laying a foundation for future exaltation.
quote: we are endeavoring to lay the foundation for future exaltation and happiness.
