claim: Taylor on legitimacy/priesthood as the only rightful government; contains bare theosis and plurality-of-gods gestures ('take my seat among the Gods of eternity', 'the everlasting mansions of the Gods') and an unspecified 'on the increase worlds without end' applied to a man's eternal possessions rather than to posterity, plus generic sealing/eternal-family language.
quote: I find myself here in the midst of the creations of God, and it is for me to make use of the intelligence God has given me, and not condescend to anything that is low, mean, grovelling, and degrading—to anything that is calculated to debase the immortal mind of man, but to follow after things that are in their nature calculated to exalt, ennoble, and dignify, that I may stand in my true position before God, angels, and men, and rise to take my seat among the Gods of eternity.

claim: Brigham Young on the right of heirship and abuses of proxy sealing to widows; exaltation is invoked only generically as a blessing not contingent on being sealed to a grasping elder.
quote: Let every man and woman magnify their calling in the kingdom of God, and he will take care that we have our exaltation.

claim: Parley P. Pratt denies that God created intelligence at all: intelligence is uncreated, an inherent attribute of the eternal element 'spirit,' existing in a continuous scale of degrees running from the lowest agent up through the varieties manifested in the eternal God Himself.
quote: It never was created, being an inherent attribute of the eternal element called spirit, which element composes each individual spirit, and which element exists in an infinitude of degrees in the scale of intellect, in all the varieties manifested in the eternal God, and thence to the lowest agent, which acts by its own will.

claim: Dedicatory prayer at the Salt Lake Temple northeast cornerstone; no deification, offspring, ancestry, or divine-progression content (God is addressed as 'Eternal Parent' only as an invocation).
Discourse on spiritual communication and mediums; 'exaltation' occurs only as the object of vicarious temple work for the dead, with no claim about the nature, ancestry, or progression of God.
quote: Who revealed to him the plan of redemption, and of exaltation for the dead who had died without the Gospel?

claim: Pratt on the spirit world, spirit as a refined material element, and redemption of the dead; exaltation appears only as a generic goal term, and there is no divine-ancestry, divine-progression, or spirit-offspring claim.
quote: Is anyone else preparing a sanctuary for the holy conversation and ministrations pertaining to their exaltation?

claim: Temple-history cornerstone oration; the endowment is defined as what enables one to pass the sentinel angels and gain eternal exaltation, and a plurality of Gods is assumed in passing ("the Gods of the Eternal Worlds"), but no specific claim about becoming a god, spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: And they will share it sooner or later, if they do not keep their hands, and tongues too, in their proper places, and stop dictating the order of the Gods of the Eternal Worlds.

claim: A discourse on the cornerstone order and the primacy of the apostleship among priesthood offices; exaltation appears only as a generic promised destiny for the obedient, with no claim on any taxonomy axis.
quote: He did, to my certain knowledge, and I have many witnesses here that heard him declare that he had done everything he could do—he had revealed everything that could be revealed *at present*, he had prepared the way for the people to walk in, and no man or woman should be deprived of going into the presence of the Father and the Son, and enjoying an eternal exaltation, if they would *walk in the path he had pointed out*.

claim: Orson Hyde's calibration text: God the Father was 'perhaps once a child, and mortal like we ourselves' and rose step by step through progression until reaching his present station, with the sympathy argument developed at length.
quote: Remember that God, our heavenly Father, was perhaps once a child, and mortal like we ourselves, and rose step by step in the scale of progress, in the school of advancement; has moved forward and overcome, until He has arrived at the point where He now is.

claim: Parable-of-the-sower discourse applied to apostates leaving for California, the gathering of wheat and tares, and Utah defensive measures; no deification, spirit-offspring, divine-ancestry, or divine-progression content (only a formulaic closing wish that the Saints be exalted).
Kimball on discernment, merit, and discipline; exaltation and 'the celestial world with the Gods' appear as generic reward language, with no divine-ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring claim.
quote: I have come here and received my body to accomplish that which I could not accomplish in the spirit; and now I have got to leave this tabernacle to go again into the spirit world to perform a work I cannot do in the flesh, that I may be prepared to receive my body again and enter into the celestial world with the Gods; and if I am faithful, all things are mine, because I have been faithful in my Father's business.

claim: Orson Pratt publicly owns the plurality-of-Gods doctrine from the conference stand, affirming he believes both in 'one only wise God' and in 'an immense number of Gods', and defends having argued it in print (the Seer-era publications) alongside plurality of wives and plurality of worlds — a specific numerical plurality claim, though he does not here assert any backward chain of Fathers (so not C).
quote: I believe there is one only wise God, and I believe there is an immense number of Gods.

claim: George A. Smith on young leaders, the Word of Wisdom, and union in the settlements; 'eternal exaltation' appears only in the closing testimony as an undefined destination, with no axis content anywhere in the discourse.
quote: Joseph Smith was a true Prophet, and that which he has conferred upon this peo- ple is a true Priesthood, and if you listen to the instructions and be led by the keys of this kingdom, you are in the path to an eternal exaltation, and we shall overcome every power that would seek to prevail against us.

claim: Rebuke of iniquity plus a defense of plural marriage as permanent past the veil ('never will be done away'); eternal-lives sealing and 'the exaltation of man' appear only generically, with no claim about spirit offspring or divine ancestry.
quote: The principle of plurality of wives never will be done away although some sisters have had revelations that, when this time passes away and they go through the veil, every woman will have a husband to herself.

claim: Practical policy sermon (traditions, fencing and farming, Indian relations, grain storage); 'the keys of revelation and exaltation' is a single passing phrase with no axis content.

Lorenzo Snow's father-and-son analogy for increase in power and knowledge, applied to consecration; the increase language stays on the human side and never states the couplet or any claim about God's own nature.
quote: It is the design of the Almighty to work into the hearts of the people the principles to operate upon, in order to obtain an eternal exaltation and glory

claim: Woodruff on following the file leader over one's own scientific theories, and on line-upon-line revelation (baptism for the dead); 'exaltation' appears twice as a generic future reward, and the 'constantly learning' theme is about the Saints and the Church, not about God progressing.
quote: I hope we may all pursue the course laid down for us by the servants of the Lord; for, if we do this, I know that we shall be safe in this world, and secure happiness and exaltation in the world to come.

claim: Short Erastus Snow remarks on returned missionaries and trusting God amid the Utah War crisis; 'exaltation, and eternal lives' occurs only as an unexplicated item in a list of blessings (the technical D&C 132 term 'eternal lives' is never developed into an increase/parenthood claim).
quote: What there may be lying in our path—I was going to say, we neither know nor care; but we do know that the straightforward path is strewed with blessings, glory, honour, exaltation, and eternal lives.

claim: Deseret News minutes stub; the only axis-adjacent line is a one-clause paraphrase that Brigham Young 'described angels as exalted beings' — no quotable doctrinal claim survives.
quote: President Brigham Young emphasized acquiring spiritual knowledge, described angels as exalted beings, and encouraged agricultural diligence.

claim: Stub file: no discourse text survives here, only a two-sentence minutes summary (Job 32:8 and 'adding knowledge to knowledge'); the title's 'Exaltation' is a supplied editorial title, not content. Nothing classifiable.
Practical sermon on unity, duty, and home manufactures; 'exalted' appears only of righteousness, and there is no deification, offspring, ancestry, or divine-progression content.

Brigham Young teaches that the procreative power given to mankind ("power given them to propagate their species") is in no way diminished by exaltation but is retained and enlarged along with all other powers — an explicit eternal-procreation claim stated without the word "increase" or "spirit children."
quote: An exaltation to the celestial kingdom of God by no means lessens that power.

claim: Brigham Young's 'Intelligence' discourse: he explicitly names 'the origin of the Gods' as a question men should stop inquiring after (C-agnostic), says we were composed by 'superior Beings' out of an eternity of life, allows that Adam and Eve may be 'the parents of our spirits,' and frames life as eternal life-element organized into spirit and clothed with a tabernacle.
quote: Instead of inquiring after the origin of the Gods—instead of trying to explore the depths of eternities that have been, that are, and that will be—instead of endeavouring to discover the boundaries of boundless space, let them seek to know the object of their present existence, and how to apply, in the most profitable manner for their mutual good and salvation, the intelligence they possess.

speaker: Brigham Young
claim: Brigham Young says there was never a time when there were not Gods and worlds, presenting a beginningless divine series.

Family-government, Jackson County, and home-manufacture remarks; kings-and-queens theosis language appears but only as generic exhortation, with no claim about divine ancestry, spirit birth, or God's progression.
quote: No man will become a king, only by honoring his calling, and by obtaining a crown by experience, and continuing in well-doing. There is no woman that will ever be a queen except she is a good woman and well attached to a good king.

claim: Mostly an anti-creedal argument that God has body and parts and man is in his express image; the only ancestry-adjacent line is a garbled Watt-shorthand construction ('The Father of the God that the sectarians worship...') that presupposes rather than asserts a divine Father, so it cannot be counted as a C claim.
quote: The Father of the God that the sectarians worship is not the being who created man.

claim: Lorenzo Snow urges the Saints to increase 'in the principles and likeness of Deity' and calls them destined kings and queens, but states only generic theosis with no regress, no new spirit children, and no claim about God's own history or progression.
quote: They are destined to become saviors on the earth—rulers among the children of men, to teach mankind how to increase in the principles and likeness of Deity—how to increase in those principles of power that will enable them constantly to ascend in the path of eternal life.

claim: Wells teaches that obedient men may become 'like Gods in the eternal worlds' and as pure and holy as the Father — bare theosis with no generative, ancestral, or progression content.
quote: This light and knowledge has been imparted to the children of men, and by obedience to its directions they can make themselves like Gods in the eternal worlds.

claim: Entirely on ecclesiastical administration — bishop/branch-president jurisdiction, high councils, and the sins that cause apostasy; no theological content on any axis.
Wells exhorts against contention and Gentile trade, with only a passing generic reference to 'exaltation' and 'eternal lives' as the endpoint of righteous living.
quote: There is plenty to do to occupy all the talent, ability, and intelligence of all Israel without taking any such course as this, and of that nature too, which instead of promoting evil will tend to virtue and righteousness and finally to exaltation, things which will tend to the enlightenment of the mind and to the advancement and spreading abroad of the principles of salvation and eternal lives.

claim: Brigham Young on Aaronic vs. Melchizedek authority of bishops, branch organization, and assisting the mail and telegraph companies; no axis content.

Brigham Young describes eternal riches as power to organize native elements and direct kingdoms 'forever and forever,' and speaks of 'principalities, and powers in the eternities of the Gods' — a strong theosis-plus-creation picture, but with no new spirit children, no backward chain, and no claim about God's own progression.
quote: When we possess all things, it will be when we possess power to organize the native elements that fill the immensity of space, bringing forth and organizing, bringing forth and organizing, again and again, dealing out the providence of God, dictating, guiding, and directing the kingdoms that will be made forever and forever.

claim: Lyman applies an 'as they are, so may we be' formula to the glorified hosts around God's throne (not to God himself), teaching that they were once as we are and rose to their present glory — theosis stated of exalted humans only.
quote: As we are, so were they; and as they are in all their brightness and glory around the throne of God, so may we be with our wives and children, friends and associates in the kingdom of God on earth, when we have traveled along to that state of exaltation to which they have attained.

claim: Rich says gospel principles 'exalt and prepare us to dwell with the Gods in the eternal worlds,' but the sermon is about present salvation and learning; no generative or ancestral content.
quote: The instructions we have had today have been joyful to my heart, for they are those principles that are calculated to save, to exalt and to prepare us to dwell with the Gods in the eternal worlds.

claim: Hyde on the Civil War as judgment, the sinking-ship figure for Babylon, and building the Tabernacle and Temple; no axis content.
Kimball promises successive endowments leading to 'celestial glory and exaltation' and alludes to celestial marriage and plural wives, but makes no specific claim on any axis.
quote: Bless you, it will be one endowment after another till we pass through the veil into the other world, and until we have passed all the ordeals requisite to prepare us to enter into celestial glory and exaltation.

claim: Lyman's counsel to missionaries and teamsters, with practical advice on plural marriage and a bare 'if we are going to be like God' theosis aside; no specific claim on any axis.
quote: Let us especially be careful to abstain from all that is impure, unjust, and unholy; for if we are going to be like God our justice must be just.

claim: Rich on building the Temple and Tabernacle, with only a generic promise of 'glory and exaltation in the life which is to come.'
quote: We wish to be freed from the error and from the evils of the world, in order that we may be happy in this life and prepare ourselves for glory and exaltation in the life which is to come.

claim: Taylor describes the future temporal glory of Zion — cities, temples, arts, sciences, Jackson County — with no content on divine ancestry, divine progression, or eternal increase.
Practical instruction on tithing labor and temple/tabernacle construction, closing with a generic promise of exaltation and 'eternal lives.'
quote: Let us abide these teachings and calls, for in this we can attain an exaltation in the presence of our Father in heaven.

claim: Brigham Young on passing gold-seekers, produce prices, the Civil War, and the curse of Ham; no axis content.

Brigham Young states flatly that God the Father inherits his own faculties, attributes and powers from His Father — an explicit divine-ancestry claim — and adds that God became rich 'by faithful labor, ceaseless perseverance, and constant exertion,' i.e. attained what He has by effort.
quote: We inherit what we possess from Him, and he inherits his faculties, attributes and powers from his Father.

claim: Lyman on the need for developed understanding among Saints and teachers, with a generic theosis endpoint of becoming 'fit associates' for God.
quote: The object of our being here is to find and realize within ourselves that development of our natures that we inherit from our Father and God, that will exalt us till we can be fit associates for Him.

claim: Taylor on revelation as the sole source of knowledge of God, with a generic endpoint of 'everlasting life and exaltation in the celestial kingdom'; no specific claim on any axis.
quote: Prepare all that are capable or worthy to receive everlasting life and exaltation in the celestial kingdom where he dwells.

claim: Wells's homecoming discourse from Europe; the gospel teaches man 'how to exalt his being' and the hope of becoming 'associated with the Gods of eternity,' but nothing beyond generic theosis.
quote: Of aiding to lay a foundation to build upon for time as well as for eternity, that we may come forth in the great hereafter and become associated with the Gods of eternity.

claim: Taylor on home manufacture, political unity, and plural marriage as elevating women, with a generic promise that the faithful will 'be associated with the Gods in the eternal world.'
quote: That when they have done with the things of time they may be transplanted to a celestial kingdom and be associated with the Gods in the eternal world.

claim: Orson Pratt asserts that God the Father is a material personage of flesh and bones who literally begat us as spirits — that we 'were born male and female in the spirit world' — and that the redeemed will become innumerable personal gods, each as fully a god as the God of this creation; he also defends this as the settled doctrine of the Church and invites correction if it is not.
quote: We also believe that in the eternity of eternities, in the heaven of heavens there will be innumerable millions of persons who will occupy that exalted station—each one being a personal god, as much so as the God of this creation—the Father of our spirits is.

claim: Cannon on the Order of Enoch, cooperation, and the failure of secular socialism; only a closing generic reference to revelations 'intended to elevate and exalt us.'
quote: Prepare us, as a people, to receive the revelations of His will, which are true and perfect and intended to elevate and exalt us, and to bring us back into His presence, there to be crowned with glory and immortality.

claim: Wells on cooperation, home industry, and the Word of Wisdom; he names 'exaltations... thrones, dominions, principalities, and powers' only as the familiar language Saints use, without unpacking any of it.
quote: We can talk of exaltations in the Kingdom of God, of thrones, dominions, principalities, and powers, but how are we going to attain to these things?

claim: Cannon defends plural marriage as the means by which 'Eternity is peopled,' and teaches that the power of procreation is God's own greatest power, granted in the life to come only within one particular degree of glory — an explicit continuation-of-lives claim rather than bare theosis.
quote: Hence we were told by brother Pratt that there are degrees of glory, and that the faithful man may receive the power of God—the greatest He has ever bestowed upon man—namely, the power of procreation.

claim: Orson Pratt teaches that only the highest order of resurrected beings — exalted husbands and wives — may propagate their species, and that they will 'bring up their spirit offspring' in the eternal worlds; celestial angels who never received eternal marriage are denied 'the privilege of increasing their posterity to all ages of eternity' and serve as servants to those on thrones.
quote: Now it is wise, no doubt, in the Great Creator to thus limit this great and heavenly principle to those who have arrived or come to the highest state of exaltation, excellency, wisdom, knowledge, power, glory, and faithfulness, to dwell in His presence, that they by this means shall be prepared to bring up their spirit offspring in all pure and holy principles in the eternal worlds, in order that they may be made happy.

claim: Woodruff on Brigham Young's authority, cooperation, and home manufacture; the only axis-adjacent language is a generic reference to principles revealed 'for the exaltation and glory of man.'
quote: When I look at the glorious principles which God has revealed for the exaltation and glory of man, I rejoice in them, and ask who will obey them?

claim: Cannon states that God's own glory consists in the number of His posterity, that worlds will keep being rolled into existence for that posterity to increase upon endlessly, and that the exalted will 'increase and multiply and fill this earth, go to other earths' forever — each man ruling his own family and kingdom under God as King of kings.
quote: And the glory of God consists in the number of his posterity; and as generation succeeds generation, until the earth is filled and glorified, other worlds will be rolled into existence, upon which the posterity of God, our heavenly Father, shall increase throughout the endless ages of eternity.

claim: Brigham Young on gathering, apostasy, miners and lawyers, the curse on Cain and the Indians, and tithing; the only axis-adjacent line is that the law of tithing exists 'for their salvation and exaltation.'
quote: It is an eternal law that God has instituted for the benefit of the human family, for their salvation and exaltation.

claim: Brigham Young states that the Gods themselves were exalted by walking the same path of perfection, purity and holiness that is now open to the Saints — a past-attainment claim about deity rather than bare theosis; he adds that every creature has as good a right to choose for himself 'as the Gods.' Note the referent is the plural 'Gods,' not narrowed explicitly to the Father.
quote: There is but one thread that can be followed that can endure forever, but one path that we can walk in that is eternal—and that path is the path of perfection, purity and holiness. By this, and this only, have the Gods been exalted, the angels live and the heavenly hosts bask in purity.

claim: George A. Smith's conference-opening remarks on persecution, temples, and cooperation name 'endless increase' as the gospel's promised reward, but the phrase is a bare formula in a list and is never unpacked into a claim about spirit offspring or eternal parenthood.
quote: Undertake to introduce system and principles calculated to elevate mankind from degradation and destruction, and exalt them to eternal glory and endless increase.

claim: Taylor exhorts the Saints to contend for the faith, naming 'eternal lives and exaltations' and thrones and principalities as the object of temple work, but without any specific claim on ancestry, progression, or generative exaltation.
quote: Our main object is eternal lives and exaltations; our main object is to prepare ourselves, our posterity and our progenitors for thrones, principalities and powers in the eternal worlds.

claim: Erastus Snow on Zion, obedience to law, and his testimony of Joseph Smith by revelation; only a closing generic wish to 'inherit exaltation with the sanctified.'
quote: May God seal the testimony of the Twelve upon the hearts of those who desire it, that they may come unto and walk in the light, be saved through the truth, and inherit exaltation with the sanctified.

claim: Brigham Young Jr. on testimony, scripture study, and the Word of Wisdom; he alludes to a premortal existence ('those with whom we dwelt in the eternal worlds') and to 'gaining an exaltation,' but makes no specific claim on any axis.
quote: We have the opportunity of gaining an exaltation in the kingdom of God if we have a mind to improve it.

claim: Brigham Young's practical sketch of a united-order community — communal kitchens, schools, silk, doctors, lawyers — with a generic statement that obedience ends in being crowned with 'glory, immortality and eternal lives.'
quote: When we have passed through all the ordeals necessary, and have proved perfectly submissive to all the rules and regulations which give life eternal, he then sets us free and crowns us with glory, immortality and eternal lives.

claim: Brigham Young insists God is literally a man with a body who eats, drinks and has a residence — a strong corporeality claim against sectarian immaterialism — but he stops there: no Father of the Father, no divine progression, no eternal increase beyond the stock 'eternal lives' formula.
quote: We know that he is a Being—a man—with all the component parts of an intelligent being—head, hair, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, cheek bones, forehead, chin, body, lower limbs; that he eats, drinks, talks, lives and has a being, and has a residence, and his presence fills immensity as far as you and I know.

claim: George A. Smith on temple construction logistics, tithing, the Word of Wisdom, and his travels in the Holy Land; exaltation appears only as the generic purpose of temple ordinances.
quote: Remember that the ordinances by which we gain exaltation for ourselves and our relatives, who have gone before us, are only administered in a holy house.

claim: George A. Smith on tithing, debt, home manufacture and wooden shoe soles, opening with the generic Lectures-on-Faith point that eternal life costs the sacrifice of all things.
quote: We are told that if we would have the blessings of exaltation, we must continue unto the end.

claim: George A. Smith on the Missouri expulsions, the law of consecration, and organizing the United Order; exaltation appears only as a generic endpoint of becoming one.
quote: We can never be prepared for the coming of the Savior only by uniting and becoming one, in temporal as well as in spiritual things, and being prepared to enjoy the blessings of exaltation.

claim: Cannon's long United Order report; his only doctrinal claim is the 'spheres' form of theosis — that man may be as perfect in his sphere as God is in His — which is bare theosis with a hedge, not a claim about ancestry, progression, or increase.
quote: It is man's privilege, the Latter-day Saints believe, to be as perfect in his sphere as God our eternal Father is in his sphere, or as Jesus in his sphere, or as the angels in their spheres.

claim: Orson Pratt on the books of judgment, the Saints judging the world and angels, and the Adam-ondi-Ahman assembly under Adam as Ancient of Days; he closes with sealed families whose children inherit priesthood 'throughout the eternal generations that are to come,' but never states new spirit offspring or any claim about God's ancestry or progression.
quote: It will then be known that their children are the legal heirs to the inheritances, and glories, and powers, and keys and Priesthood of their fathers, throughout the eternal generations that are to come.

claim: Rich on guarding against temptation, temple work for the dead, and present salvation; exaltation appears only as a generic reward 'among the sanctified.'
quote: The time will come when we will be counted worthy of an inheritance and exaltation among the sanctified in the presence of our Father.

claim: George A. Smith reads through the rules of the United Order; the only axis-adjacent line pairs 'endless lives' with thrones and dominions as the reward of chastity, a stock D&C 132 formula left unexplained.
quote: If we ever are made partakers of the thrones, dominions, principalities, powers and endless lives which pertain to the exaltation of the kingdom of God, we shall do so by maintaining a purity like that of Joseph who was sold into Egypt.

claim: Taylor surveys the dispensations, defending the Flood as mercy toward unborn spirits who would otherwise inherit degenerate bodies; he speaks of principles that 'originated with the Gods in the eternal worlds' but makes no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or eternal increase.
quote: The principles that we believe in reach back into eternity, they originated with the Gods in the eternal worlds, and they reach forward to the eternities that are to come.

claim: Orson Pratt on the Book of Mormon as the sign of Israel's gathering, the Three Nephites, the lost ten tribes in the north, and the 144,000; no content on any axis.

Taylor teaches that man is literally the offspring of Deity and that spirits take bodies so as to be raised to greater exaltation — pre-existence plus bare theosis, with no claim about God's own ancestry or progression and no new spirit offspring.
quote: Man was created in the image of God, and he was the offspring of Deity himself, and consequently made in his likeness; and being made in that likeness, he was a son of God.

claim: Daniel H. Wells grounds God's fitness to guide us in His own biography: God is wiser than we are because He has already 'passed through all the ordeals and trials of a lower estate' and gained experience beyond that of men — a past-progression claim about deity, immediately identified in the next sentence as 'the God of heaven' whose 'children' we are.
quote: There is one whose guidance we need, he is wiser than we are, for he has passed through all the ordeals and trials of a lower estate, and has gained an experience far beyond the experience of men, and he is now willing to lead and guide his children here on the earth if they will only allow him to do so.

claim: Wells on the St. George Temple, reformation, and the degrees of glory; he notes in passing that the priesthood is the authority 'by which the Gods themselves are governed,' but makes no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or eternal increase.
quote: It is the same authority that exists in the heavens, by which the Gods themselves are governed, and by which they control all things.

claim: Joseph F. Smith on the new birth, baptism for the dead, and the Holy Ghost; the closest axis language is that the Spirit will 'eventually cause him to appear like unto his Maker' — bare theosis.
quote: Drawing him who possesses it nearer unto God, and will eventually cause him to appear like unto his Maker.

claim: Taylor on God as the author of every dispensation, Church organization, and his conversation with Baron Rothschild about temples; the Saints are 'a nation of Kings and Priests' who will 'appear like unto him in glory' — generic theosis only.
quote: Then it is that we are the sons of God, and it does not yet appear what we shall be, says the sacred writer; 'but when he who is our life shall appear, then shall we appear like unto him in glory.'

claim: Wells on unbelief, temple building, and self-sufficiency; he urges laying here 'a foundation to progress upon' after death and for exaltation in the celestial kingdom, but the progression in view is man's, stated generically.
quote: Before we go behind the veil we should lay a foundation to progress upon after we have finished our course here.

speaker: Brigham Young
claim: Brigham Young says spirits were begotten, born, and brought forth by celestial bodies, an explicit viviparous account of spirit birth.

Taylor's charge to the quorums on their neglected duties, plus emigration fund, tithing, education and the Relief Society; he refers to 'councils that existed in the heavens among the gods' and being 'united with the Gods in heaven,' but makes no specific claim on any axis.
quote: He has brought us here according to certain eternal principles which he had in his mind before the world was, and according to certain councils that existed in the heavens among the gods.

claim: Wilford Woodruff states that God Himself received his endowments long before we were born and 'passed through his probation,' and that we must walk the very same path and receive the same ordinances to inherit the same glory He has — an explicit claim that the Father underwent the same probationary course now required of us.
quote: We do not do it to benefit the Lord at all, he had his endowments a long time before we were born, and also passed through his probation.

claim: Joseph F. Smith on temporal duties, the Perpetual Emigration Fund, tithing, home manufacture and silk culture; exaltation appears only as a generic reward whose 'title' grows surer with faithfulness.
quote: Our enjoyment of the gifts and blessings of the Holy Spirit will increase as we become more diligent and so will our knowledge extend and our title to exaltation and eternal life become more and more sure.

claim: Erastus Snow on Church organization, common consent, civil government, and the fate of the disobedient; he names 'everlasting increase' among the keys the damned forfeit and the obedient receive, and refers to 'priests and priestesses' who may yet administer for them — but the increase phrase is a clause in a stock list, never unpacked into spirit offspring or a mechanism. Graded down for consistency with the other stock-formula cases; the quote is preserved in case the caller wants to promote it.
quote: For being deprived of the presence of God and the Lamb, and the holy angels and the sanctified ones, and of the keys of immortality and eternal life and everlasting increase vouchsafed to the obedient.

claim: Taylor on temporal affairs, the Constitution, ZCMI and the United Order; he speaks of 'the intelligence that dwells in the bosoms of the Gods' and of marriage principles that will exalt the Saints and their progenitors, but states no specific claim on any axis.
quote: The information we have pertaining to our associations with our wives, and wives with their husbands has been revealed to us by God, and we are striving to carry out those eternal principles--principles that will exalt us, our progenitors and our posterity in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Counsel on deferring to experienced leaders; "exalt" used only in the ordinary sense of elevating mankind.
Generic eternal-family language: wives and children bound in the celestial world, with no claim about new offspring or divine ancestry.
quote: Let us obey the celestial law of God, that we may have our wives and children with us in the morning of the first resurrection; that we may come forth clothed with glory, immortality and eternal lives, with our wives and children bound to us in the family organization in the celestial world, to dwell with us throughout the endless ages of eternity

claim: Bare theosis in passing ("there is exaltation in it"); the talk is about the peculiarity and union of the Saints.
quote: There is glory in it, there is happiness in it, there is peace in it, there is virtue in it, there is wealth in it, there is exaltation in it

claim: Asserts a plurality of past and future worlds made by the same eternal laws, but makes no claim about God’s ancestry, progression, or new spirit offspring.
quote: And this earth has been brought together and arranged according to eternal principles, eternal laws, by which other worlds have been made, and by which other worlds will yet be made, that are behind us, that will follow this earth.

claim: Plural Gods in the eternal worlds asserted as the setting of the gospel, but only as a stock phrase with no backward or generative claim attached.
quote: God feels interested in the welfare of the whole human family, and for this purpose he has established principles upon the earth which exist in the heavens—a Gospel that has prevailed among the Gods in the eternal worlds, containing principles which are calculated to elevate, ennoble and exalt the human family.

claim: Bare theosis: the Saints are entitled to the same exaltation and glory as the resurrected Christ. No generative or ancestry claim.
quote: we understand fully, that as Jesus Christ dwelt here in a body, and that he received that body and now dwells in it glorified, that we are entitled to the same blessing, the same exaltation, and the same glory.

claim: Mission of the Saints, the Constitution, and the anti-polygamy test oath; no content on any axis.
Standard thrones-and-dominions inheritance plus "perfection to perfection" progression of the Saints; nothing about God’s own past or new offspring.
quote: it is to pass these ordeals that we came here; to prove our integrity and worthiness to come back into his presence to inherit thrones, kingdoms, principalities, powers and dominions that are prepared for the righteous.

claim: "A nation of kings and priests to God" as the aim of the Saints — generic exaltation imagery only.
quote: Do you realize that you are raising up and professedly educating in the name of the Lord a nation of Kings and Priests to God?

claim: Bare theosis: humans may be "exalted to the Godhead" through the intelligence God imparts; no mechanism or regress.
quote: It is said "the glory of God is intelligence," and He is desirous to impart this intelligence to the human family, that through it they may be exalted to the Godhead.

claim: Joseph Smith’s corporeal God and exalted angels who were once men — anthropomorphism without a claim about God’s own origin.
quote: He bore testimony also that angels did not have wings, that they were men who had kept their covenants with their Father and their God, and had been exalted, through obedience to the commandments of God to that condition that they could dwell in His presence and become His ministers.

claim: Plural Gods guarding the celestial kingdom (D&C 132 idiom) and the three-degrees scheme; no ancestry or generative claim.
quote: We are told that before we can enter into the celestial kingdom of God, we shall have to pass by the angels, and the Gods, and if the Latter-day Saints aim at a celestial exaltation, they must live and abide by the celestial law, or they will not get it

claim: Pre-existence of spirits and association "with the Gods" stated generically; no claim about God’s Father or new spirit children.
quote: according to eternal laws that exist in the heavens, men must be governed by certain principles, if they desire to associate with the Gods

claim: Joseph Smith’s prophetic mission and the growth of the work; "exalted" used only of humility rewarded.

George Q. Cannon states that a newborn human infant may itself become a God in eternity, wielding dominion in the eternal worlds and fathering "unnumbered millions" — theosis carried explicitly into eternal parenthood of an innumerable posterity.
quote: That little puling infant may become, in the eternity of our God, a God, to sway power and dominion in the eternal worlds, to be the father of unnumbered millions.

claim: Franklin D. Richards states that the exalted family’s posterity has no end — the D&C 132 endless-increase promise applied directly to the Saints’ own future — and separately locates the source of mortal increase in spirits sent from "the great and glorious presence of God our Father."
quote: We look forward to inheriting the blessings of the kingdom of God with our children, and that to their increase there shall be no end.

claim: Taylor’s stock formula that God’s spirit progeny take bodies and return "as Gods among the Gods"; the full arc is sketched but no backward ancestry, no new spirit children, no mechanism.
quote: it was requisite that bodies should be prepared for those spirits to inhabit, in order that the purposes of God pertaining to His progeny might be accomplished, and that those spirits might be enabled, through the medium of the everlasting Gospel, to return unto the presence of their Heavenly Father, as Gods among the Gods.

claim: Pre-mortal existence and conflict alluded to, and the Adamic promise "thus may all become my sons"; sonship only, no divine ancestry or increase claim.
quote: and when we get back to the most remote items of history — or items of information which history is permitted to furnish us — we find that even in the spiritual state of man’s existence, before the family of Adam came to dwell in the flesh, that there was antagonism there between truth and error

claim: Encouragement under persecution and temple attendance; no axis content.
Defense of celestial/plural marriage as eternal contract whose "domestic ties" bear fruit in the celestial kingdom — eternal family, unspecified.
quote: Under an infatuated, mistaken and suicidal policy they seek to blast those hopes which are a solace to the life of the believer in the revelations of God, and to sever those connubial ties which bud in time and will blossom and bear fruit in the Celestial Kingdom of our God in the eternities to come.

claim: Eternal marriage lays "the foundation of a kingdom" and of eternal dominions; also pre-existent spirits seeking parentage among the Saints. Generic on both counts.
quote: we were, while in the flesh, laying the foundation for eternal dominions, crowns and exaltations; that our wives and our children were given to us of God for the purpose of laying the foundation of a kingdom

claim: Quotes the D&C 132 phrase "exaltation and continuation of the lives" without unpacking it; the epistle is otherwise a legal and political defense of plural marriage.
quote: "Strait is the gate," says Jesus, "and narrow the way that leadeth unto the exaltation and continuation of the lives, and few there be that find it."

claim: Long First Presidency epistle on persecution, civic duty and home life; only generic "eternal exaltations" language touches the axes.
quote: What in this case becomes of all our hopes of eternal life, eternal exaltations in the mansions of the just?

claim: Brief remarks on temporal law, disunion among the nations, and Zion; no axis content.
Bare theosis framed as the highest degree available to man — joint heirship with Christ, no generative or ancestry content.
quote: We, as Latter-day Saints, have started out for an exaltation in the celestial kingdom. We desire to be heirs—even joint heirs with Jesus Christ.

claim: George Q. Cannon quotes the Snow couplet from the General Conference pulpit ("As man now is, God was; as God now is, man may be"), calls the Saints "the literal offspring of Deity" descended from the Being who formed this earth, promises them a posterity numberless as the stars, argues from Christ’s birth of Mary that other Gods may likewise be born of women, and refers to knowing "our mother" alongside the Father in the pre-existence.
quote: And if one God was born of woman, may not others be also?

claim: Short remarks urging the young to keep the higher law; exaltation mentioned only as a future reward.
Brief remarks on judgment according to opportunity; no axis content.
Short exhortation to purity and covenant-keeping; no axis content.
Says the Saints must keep "the same law that has exalted those who have gone before us" and that we waited in the spirit world — both generic.
quote: In order to get there, we have got to keep the same law that has exalted those who have gone before us.

claim: Exaltation as the greatest blessing for intelligent beings, reached by approximating perfection; nothing further.
quote: We have set out for an exaltation in the Kingdom of God—the greatest blessing that can be bestowed upon intelligent beings.

claim: Two masters, two powers; exaltation named only as the opposite of destruction.
Union and perfecting as prerequisites to "the great exaltation and glory"; bare theosis.
quote: We must perfect ourselves before we can attain to the great exaltation and glory which have been promised unto the faithful.

claim: Co-heirship: whatever exaltation Christ attains the Saints receive in like manner. Also condemns birth control as thwarting "the natural increase of the race," but only in mortal terms.
quote: He has promised us that we shall be co-heirs with Him, and joint heirs in whatever glory He receives. Whatever exaltation He attains unto we shall in like manner receive, if we follow His precepts and His example.

claim: Historical defense of the test cases and the Manifesto; no axis content.
Resurrected Saints pass by "the Gods and the angels" to their thrones and dominions — the standard D&C 132 idiom, no further claim.
quote: in the morning of the resurrection, when they come out of their graves, they will pass by the Gods and the angels who are set there to watch the interests of the celestial world; they will go to those thrones, kingdoms, principalities and powers which have been ordained of God for them to occupy

claim: Continuing revelation as the means by which Saints "become godly" and become sons and daughters of God; bare theosis.
quote: so study the laws of the Priesthood and the everlasting Gospel that we can become godly, become the sons and daughters of the living God

claim: The fullest forward-chain statement in this chunk: Cannon teaches that the procreative power survives into eternity, that "to the increase of their seed there shall be no end" for every faithful couple, that the creative power will be given to exalted men who will organize worlds for their own posterity as God did for us, and that Abraham will have to emigrate from this earth for want of room — the visible stars being worlds created by God and peopled by His children. Explicit first-estate/second-estate staging as well. Asserts the chain only forward; makes no claim about God’s own Father.
quote: He called together the elements and formed the earth as a habitation for man; and man, if he is faithful, will progress until he will do that very same thing for his posterity.

claim: Pastoral counsel on the peculiarities and duties of the Saints; exaltation named only in the closing prayer.
Progression "from one degree of perfection to another" via the Holy Ghost; Snow states no part of his couplet here.
quote: Thousands of the Latter-day Saints have received this supernatural aid and power, which will enable them to advance from one degree of perfection to another.

claim: Dedicatory prayer of the Salt Lake Temple; sealing of the whole family chain "from now, back to the beginning" and exaltation, all in devotional register.
quote: We praise Thee that our fathers, from last to first, from now, back to the beginning, can be united with us in indissoluble links, welded by the Holy Priesthood

claim: Self-examination, love of God, and the Holy Spirit; exaltation only in the closing prayer.
Families retained in the next life if the head gains exaltation — eternal family, unspecified, and no increase claim.
quote: In the future life we would have our families—our wives and children. Even if they did not follow our counsels, if we shall be successful in gaining exaltation we would eventually have them, for they will be where we shall be.

claim: Calls "O My Father" a revelation from the pulpit — an indirect endorsement of the Heavenly Mother hymn, but Thatcher states no doctrinal claim; the talk is otherwise about money and interest rates.
quote: See the impression made upon the hearts of thousands of people by the revelation contained in that beautiful hymn, "O, my Father."

claim: Says Joseph Smith went to "mingle with his brethren and the Gods" — plural Gods in passing, nothing developed.
quote: He fulfilled his mission in a great and wonderful manner, and when he laid his body down he went to mingle with his brethren and the Gods.

claim: Despite the title, the talk is chiefly on secret societies and the United Order; the linking of generations is treated as stewardship and inheritance, not as a chain reaching to Deity.
quote: it is the only plan by which we can ever get into the celestial kingdom and become joint heirs with Jesus Christ

claim: Duty of parents to teach and baptize children at eight; no axis content.

Anti-trinitarian argument that Father and Son are one in attributes and not in person, quoting "gods many, and lords many"; plurality asserted polemically, with no ancestry, progression, or generative claim.
quote: Paul says: "There be gods many, and lords many, but to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him."

claim: Priesthood lineage traced backward through the fathers by record and revelation; a human genealogical chain only, terminating in exaltation for the faithful.
quote: It is evident the eye of God has been over us, and the eyes of His angels have watched over the continuation of the fathers down through the generation that have come unto us.

claim: Standard immutability formula ("God is the same yesterday, today and forever, and His course is one eternal round") stated about God’s dealings with men, not as a denial of divine progression; otherwise Church-organization testimony.
quote: God is the same yesterday, today and forever, and His course is one eternal round.

claim: Woodruff’s reform of temple adoption: seal every man to his own father and run the chain back as far as it can be traced, with the last man adopted to Joseph Smith. A human sealing chain, deliberately terminated at Joseph Smith rather than extended toward Deity.
quote: let every man be adopted to his father; and then you will do exactly what God said when he declared He would send Elijah the prophet in the last days.

claim: Thrones and exaltation promised generically; strongest material is a curse pronounced on birth prevention, framed as mortal duty rather than eternal increase.
quote: But I know that He intends to exalt you, to give you glory, to crown you, and to have you sit upon the thrones.

claim: Lorenzo Snow recounts receiving the couplet by vision and states it from the pulpit as "As man now is, God once was" — then goes past it: the Saints, begotten in God’s image, are capable of enlargement "until His fulness is reached," sitting on thrones and governing their own posterity from eternity to eternity and increasing eternally. The couplet itself overlaps the existing dataset entry snow-couplet (dated 1892), but that entry does not carry this eternal-increase extension or this date.
quote: He has given us faculties and powers that are capable of enlargement until His fulness is reached which He has promised—until we shall sit upon thrones, governing and controlling our posterity from eternity to eternity, and increasing eternally.

claim: Church organization and conference business; exaltation only in the closing prayer.

Snow lays out the first-estate/second-estate staging explicitly — we dwelt and knew one another in a first estate, kept it, and were therefore permitted mortality — and names the purpose of that mortal ordeal as qualifying us to sit on thrones and govern our own posterity "worlds without end"; a third of God’s offspring forfeited bodies of their own.
quote: And in consequence of having kept our first estate, we had the privilege of coming into this estate, in order to pass through the ordeal and get that necessary experience and education that should prepare us to sit upon thrones and govern and control our posterity worlds without end.

claim: John W. Taylor preaches loyalty to the presiding authorities and warns against fault-finding and apostasy; no content on any axis.
Heber J. Grant treats spiritual growth as the measure of progress toward exaltation and dwelling with God — bare theosis, no mechanism or ancestry claim.
quote: The blessings of God were not to be measured by individual financial prosperity, but the exercise and growth of spiritual powers would be found to be the measure of advancement toward exaltation.

claim: Franklin D. Richards echoes D&C 132 that Abraham has entered his exaltation and holds 'power with the Gods,' but asserts no divine ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring claim.
quote: The Lord has told us that he has passed the angels and the Gods and gone into his exaltation.

claim: Lorenzo Snow teaches men are to become equal with God by receiving of His fulness and that family relationships continue hereafter, but keeps it at generic theosis with no ancestry, progression, or spirit-offspring specifics.
quote: The Lord would be pleased with one ambitious to attain to spiritual advancement, and to become equal with God, through receiving of His fulness, in accordance with the original design.

claim: George Q. Cannon asserts humans are literal offspring of God in the same sense our children are literally ours (explicitly against evolution), and endorses 'O My Father' as containing truths revealed through Joseph Smith — an authority claim for the Heavenly Mother verse.
quote: We have descended from God, and can claim our parentage from Him, as much as our children can claim their parentage from us.

claim: Joseph Anderson frames the goal as salvation and exaltation in the celestial kingdom involving eternal growth and activity, but never specifies what that growth consists of or touches ancestry, parenthood, or God's own progression.
quote: The salvation that I am thinking of, the salvation that Latter-day Saints seek, is eternal life in the presence of our Heavenly Father and his divine Son, not only eternal existence but eternal growth and activity.

claim: Ezra Taft Benson affirms premortal spirit existence, universal divine siblinghood, and 'the first lesson toward exaltation,' but only in generic terms; the D&C 76 'begotten sons and daughters unto God' quote is applied to Christ's atonement, not to divine reproduction.
quote: We are eternal beings. We lived as intelligent spirits before this mortal life.

claim: Victor L. Brown states that we are literally spiritual sons of our Father in heaven, physically resembling Him as we resemble our earthly fathers, and that the spirit 'was fathered' by God — literal divine parentage stated generically, with no mechanism, ancestry, or forward chain.
quote: Being sons of God, we were created in his image. In other words, our physical appearance is similar to his, just as it is to our earthly father.

claim: James A. Cullimore quotes Joseph Fielding Smith that eternal marriage is the foundation of eternal exaltation and that without it there is no eternal progress, but the talk is about divorce prevention and says nothing about heavenly parenthood or divine ancestry.
quote: Marriage, as understood by Latter-day Saints, is a covenant ordained to be everlasting. It is the foundation for eternal exaltation, for without it there could be no eternal progress in the kingdom of God.

claim: LeGrand Richards catalogues fulfilled prophecy (temples, gathering, Elijah, missionary work); 'eternal exaltation in the world to come' appears only as a stock phrase.
Marion G. Romney argues for the literal reality of Satan and the premortal council; the phrase 'God the Father and his spirit children' is incidental and undeveloped.
Joseph Fielding Smith charges priesthood holders to forsake worldliness; 'save and exalt ourselves' is a passing phrase with no doctrinal development.

President Joseph Fielding Smith, formally 'restating for the Church and for the world' the eternal principles, declares the Father a glorified exalted personage with all power and all dominion who 'knows all things' and is 'infinite and eternal' — an omniscience/absoluteness assertion cutting against divine progression — and says the worlds without number are all peopled by His spirit children.
quote: We know that our Heavenly Father is a glorified, exalted personage who has all power, all might, and all dominion, and that he knows all things.

claim: Henry D. Taylor on gaining and keeping a personal testimony; 'salvation and exaltation' appears once as a stock phrase.
A. Theodore Tuttle summarizes the Restoration message (divine sonship of Christ, apostasy, First Vision, Joseph Smith); no axis content beyond a single 'way to exaltation' phrase.
Ezra Taft Benson's warning against rock music, drugs, and permissiveness; no content on any axis.
Alvin R. Dyer on agency, habit, and self-restraint; no axis content.
Gordon B. Hinckley on obedience to priesthood counsel; 'eternal salvation and exaltation of this people' is a closing stock phrase.

Bruce R. McConkie calls the Father 'an exalted and perfected personage' and reads D&C 93's grace-to-grace as Christ's *mortal* progression completed at the resurrection ('he received a fulness'), with the same pattern promised to us — a progression frame applied to Christ and man but never to the Father, so it stays generic on axis D.
quote: We must learn that God is our Father; that he is an exalted and perfected personage in whose image we are created.

claim: LeGrand Richards draws lessons on trial and endurance from Zion's Camp and Liberty Jail; no axis content.

Joseph Fielding Smith says eternal marriage is an order of the priesthood whose participants are 'promised kingdoms and thrones,' and that covenant-keeping brings exaltation in the highest heaven — D&C 132 language used generically with no parenthood or increase content.
quote: Marriage for time and for all eternity is an “order of the priesthood,” in which the participating parties are promised kingdoms and thrones if they are true and faithful to their obligations.

claim: Eldred G. Smith treats withstanding Satan as the path to 'a stage of perfection, even exaltation'; premortal council material is recounted but no ancestry, parenthood, or divine-progression claim appears.
quote: If we withstand that, then we will have attained a stage of perfection, even exaltation.

claim: Henry D. Taylor on mortality as a testing ground, illustrated by Lyman Wight, Peter, and Joseph Smith; no axis content.

Joseph Anderson affirms man's existence 'without beginning' before mortality, God as Father of our spirits, and growing 'more nearly like our Father,' but keeps all of it at the level of generic exaltation rhetoric.
quote: Our philosophy of life contemplates an eternity of existence—life without beginning in the preexistent world and life hereafter throughout the eternities.

claim: Marvin J. Ashton warns against treating temple marriage, a mission, or a calling as a destination and insists exaltation is a continuing process, but supplies no content about what that process leads to beyond the celestial kingdom.
quote: To gain exaltation after celestial marriage, continued devotion and righteousness are required. It is a continuing process, not a state of arrival.

claim: Theodore M. Burton devotes a whole conference address to defining exaltation and lands on eternal family relationship as its entire content — quoting D&C 132:16-17 ('they cannot be enlarged … are not gods, but are angels of God forever and ever') while glossing the loss as living 'separately and singly in an unmarried state' rather than as loss of increase or godhood, a definitional narrowing of exaltation toward family preservation.
quote: That possibility of an eternal family relationship is what is meant by exaltation and eternal life.

claim: ElRay L. Christiansen equates eternal life with 'exaltation in the celestial world' and calls parenthood 'an approach to the divine,' quoting Joseph F. Smith that procreating parents are as responsible as God is for His own works — suggestive but wholly undeveloped.
quote: Parenthood is a sacred trust. It is an approach to the divine—a God-given privilege that, with its never-ending responsibilities, brings rich and lasting rewards.

claim: Marion D. Hanks on six causes of unhappiness and the joy available through Christ; no axis content.
Sterling W. Sill on books and scripture as 'medicine for the soul'; 'the Father of our spirits' and 'eternal exaltation of our souls' are stock phrases.

A. Theodore Tuttle makes obtaining and magnifying the priesthood the condition of exaltation and quotes the oath and covenant ('all that my Father hath shall be given unto him'), but does not unpack what receiving all the Father has entails.
quote: In order to gain exaltation a man must obtain, then magnify, the holy priesthood.

claim: ElRay L. Christiansen ties the new and everlasting covenant of marriage to living eternally with companion, children, and posterity in the 'family kingdom,' but supplies no content on increase, godhood, or divine ancestry.
quote: …we will observe his laws, which, after all, are the principles by which we must learn to live in order to qualify ourselves for the greatest of all the gifts of God, which he says is eternal life, our life in the “family kingdom.”

claim: James A. Cullimore opens a home-teaching address by quoting Hugh B. Brown that 'the very essence of divine government is fatherhood' and Joseph F. Smith that 'eternal increase in the kingdom of God is laid in the divinely ordained home,' plus JFS on the patriarchal order continuing through eternity — eternal-increase vocabulary present but entirely unexplicated.
quote: The very foundation of the kingdom of God, of righteousness, of progress, of development, of eternal life, and eternal increase in the kingdom of God is laid in the divinely ordained home.

claim: Thomas S. Monson's meditation on hands (child, youth, mother, father, prophet, the Lord); no axis content.
Marion G. Romney on the priesthood obligation to care for the poor and the welfare program; no axis content.

Eldred G. Smith explains temples as the required venue for the ordinances of exaltation, but treats exaltation only as a status requiring all ordinances, with no content on increase, godhood, or parenthood.
quote: To receive the fullness of the blessings of exaltation, even eternal life, man must receive all the law and the ordinances of God’s kingdom.

claim: N. Eldon Tanner frames prophetic revelation as 'space communication' from God; 'a loving Father whose spirit children we are' and 'we can gain exaltation' are stock phrases, and the other-worlds language is rhetorical rather than doctrinal.

A. Theodore Tuttle says we lived with Heavenly Father in a celestial home before this world and that the earthly home is 'patterned after' it, and quotes J. Reuben Clark casting Eve/motherhood as 'a creator of bodies' for waiting spirits — heavenly-family imagery and a mortal-body-creation role, but no heavenly parenthood, increase, or ancestry claim.
quote: To Latter-day Saints, the home is a holy place, patterned after the celestial home whence we came.

claim: Joseph Anderson attributes God's foreknowledge to 'his experience and his omniscience' — an omniscience affirmation with an unexplained appeal to divine experience — but the talk is about prophecy and premortal foreordination, not divine progression.
quote: Through his experience and his omniscience, our Heavenly Father knows the end from the beginning.

claim: David B. Haight on the reality of Satan and parents' duty to teach children to recognize evil; no axis content.
Marion D. Hanks on Christlike compassion toward the lonely, disabled, and repentant; no axis content.
Howard W. Hunter retells 3 Nephi and expounds Christ's definition of his gospel; 'eternal life and exaltation' appears once as a stock phrase.
Bruce R. McConkie on teaching doctrine and then sealing it with personal testimony, framed by two of his own poems; 'save and exalt a human soul' is a stock phrase.

Sterling W. Sill argues from Genesis 3:22 that knowledge 'still tends to make men and women become as God' and that we may learn as much as we want about God and His program for our eternal exaltation — bare theosis via the knowledge motif, with no further specification.
quote: I would just like to point out in passing that the right kind of knowledge still tends to have that effect upon people. It still tends to make men and women become as God.

claim: Robert L. Simpson defines exaltation simply as living eternally in God's presence, with godhood, increase, and parenthood absent from the definition — the same narrowing Burton makes at length, but here only in passing.
quote: We also know and understand that total fulfillment can only be found in that ultimate celestial state called eternal life or exaltation, which, of course, is to live eternally in his holy presence.

claim: N. Eldon Tanner says we are 'actually spirit children of God' and, in an anecdote about temple marriage, that a sealed couple 'could then be parents of spirit children of God' — phrasing that most naturally means providing bodies for God's spirits, though it reads ambiguously toward heavenly parenthood; nothing is developed either way.
quote: …how lovely it was to see a young couple married in the temple, realizing that they could then be parents of spirit children of God, and what a great privilege it was for them to be there in the temple.

claim: James E. Faust on sustaining fathers at the head of the home; the one eternal-family line ('marriage and the family unit can extend into and continue throughout all eternity') is stock, and 'the exalted position of a father' refers to mortal fatherhood.

David B. Haight tells LDS youth that if worthy they may 'inherit thrones, kingdoms, principalities' with exaltation and glory sealed on their heads (D&C 132:19), and notes in passing that nonmember friends would find these terms strange — the vocabulary of godhood quoted but never explicated.
quote: You can, if worthy, “… inherit thrones, kingdoms, principalities,” and have “… exaltation and glory … sealed upon [your] heads, … forever and ever.” (D&C 132:19.) Chances are your nonmember friends wouldn’t understand these terms.

claim: Marion D. Hanks on forgiveness as the ultimate form of love; no axis content.

Spencer W. Kimball, cataloguing 'the blessings of eternity,' reads D&C 132:19-20 and D&C 76:58 verbatim from the conference pulpit — the exalted pass by 'the angels, and the gods which are set there,' their glory is 'a continuation of the seeds forever and ever,' and 'then shall they be gods' — presenting the full increase-and-godhood text as the promised reward, though he adds no gloss of his own.
quote: …and they shall pass by the angels, and the gods which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.

claim: Harold B. Lee, urging marriage on unmarried priesthood holders, quotes Joseph F. Smith that neither man nor woman can be exalted alone and states that only those sealed in the temple will have exaltation in the celestial kingdom; he also calls procreating men those who 'link hands with the Creator' — firm but standard, with no content on increase, ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: …remember, brethren, that only those who enter into the new and everlasting covenant of marriage in the temple for time and eternity, only those will have the exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Bruce R. McConkie counsels an affirmative outlook and control of one's thoughts, closing with his own psalm of praise; 'the family unit shall go on everlastingly' is a stock phrase in a list of blessings.
Boyd K. Packer on using a favorite hymn to control one's thoughts and on avoiding degrading music; 'you are a son or a daughter of Almighty God' is a stock phrase.
Marion G. Romney reviews welfare fundamentals (labor, family responsibility, the bishop's role) for newly called bishops; no axis content.

Marion G. Romney, then in the First Presidency, reads long stretches of Orson F. Whitney's 'Elias' from the conference pulpit as 'majestic lines' paraphrasing revealed truth — a premortal council of plural Gods ('In solemn council sat the Gods'; 'Go forth, thou Chosen of the Gods') and the Father's decree that redeemed man 'with God shall be, As God forevermore' — a plurality-of-Gods and man-becomes-God text endorsed by selection, though Romney supplies no gloss.
quote: “‘By arm divine, both mine and thine, / The lost thou shalt restore, / And man, redeemed, with God shall be, / As God forevermore.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley defines eternal life as God's own life which He hopes to share with all His children and insists exaltation requires abiding the fulness of celestial law — the standard theosis formula with no further specification.
quote: Eternal life is God’s life, which he hopes to share with all his children.

claim: O. Leslie Stone names salvation, exaltation, and eternal life as the reward of loving and forgiving, with no further doctrinal specification.
quote: This means if we are to gain salvation, exaltation, and eternal life we must live in accordance with the principles of the gospel.

claim: Joseph Anderson calls all people children of God and names the salvation and exaltation of souls as the purpose of life, but says nothing about divine nature or progression.
quote: it is of the utmost importance that we keep in mind the great purpose of life, which is to prepare us for eternal life—the salvation and exaltation of the souls of God’s children.

claim: Marvin J. Ashton's parable-of-the-ten-virgins talk refers once to the saving, exalting gospel and otherwise stays on preparedness.
quote: they were informed people who had the saving, exalting gospel in their possession, but had not made it the center of their lives

claim: Ezra Taft Benson invokes premortal association with Harold B. Lee and calls missionary work a partnership with Heavenly Father in the exaltation of His children, both in generic terms.
quote: We are happy to be engaged in a partnership with our Heavenly Father in the great work of the salvation and exaltation of his children.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball quotes D&C 132:63 on virgins given to man for their exaltation in the eternal worlds and the Father's work being continued, and calls the body the sacred home of the spirit child of God, but offers no commentary extending the proof text past mortal childbearing.
quote: “… for [virgins] are given unto [man] to multiply and replenish the earth, according to [God’s] commandment, … and for their exaltation in the eternal worlds, that they may bear the souls of men; for herein is the work of my Father continued, that he may be glorified.”

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's priesthood-session talk on missions and celestial marriage closes with a generic reference to the program of salvation and exaltation.
quote: It is a great program of salvation and exaltation, and it is the only way, and there never was found happiness in unrighteousness.

claim: H. Burke Peterson tells mothers that their present calling is training for becoming an eternal mother and cocreator of spiritual offspring — an explicit assertion that exalted women will produce new spirit children.
quote: —A mother whose energy is so sapped that she is sometimes neglecting her call from the Lord, a call that will one day prepare her to become an eternal mother—a cocreator of spiritual offspring.

claim: Ed J. Pinegar frames the Church as existing for the exalting of the family and calls parents partners with Heavenly Father in the joy of creation, but the partnership described is ordinary mortal procreation.
quote: In partnership with our Heavenly Father, they experience the joy of creation as children bless their home and enlarge their family circle.

claim: Hartman Rector Jr. says testimony coupled with conversion and endurance will exalt us, without specifying what exaltation consists of.
quote: Testimony won’t save us, but testimony coupled with faith and conversion, which includes, staying power, which is endurance, will exalt us.

claim: Marion G. Romney's welfare-services address uses exalt only in the D&C 104:16 economic sense of the poor being exalted and the rich made low; no axis content.
quote: this is the way that I, the Lord, have decreed to provide for my saints, that the poor shall be exalted, in that the rich are made low.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley's talk on Christ's ministry mentions salvation and exaltation as what the Atonement makes possible, with no further specification.
quote: We can never fully repay our Savior for his sacrifice made to help us achieve salvation and exaltation.

claim: Joseph Anderson rehearses premortal spirit childhood and says the Father's plan had already been used on other worlds, but the plurality-of-worlds aside is lateral rather than a backward chain, and the theosis language stays generic.
quote: In the councils where consideration was given to the matter of the creation and the peopling of this earth, the Father presented an unselfish plan. It had been used in other worlds.

claim: Ezra Taft Benson's twelve remedies for despair include the lifetime goal of perfecting ourselves as Christ has, quoting 3 Nephi 27:27 — bare theosis with no divine-nature content.
quote: “Therefore, what manner of men ought ye to be?” asked the Master, and he answered, “Verily I say unto you, even as I am.” … Now there is a lifetime goal—to walk in his steps, to perfect ourselves in every virtue as he has done

claim: Thomas S. Monson's tribute talk quotes a missionary son on the blessings of exaltation in the celestial kingdom as a family reunion, nothing more.
quote: Today we taught a choice family about the plan of salvation and the blessings of exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: LeGrand Richards argues that those who die young or never marry must still receive everything the married faithful receive, cites D&C 132:19's continuation of the seeds forever and ever as the celestial promise, and says he expects to meet the bride his dead son selects in the spirit world — an explicit post-mortal marriage-and-increase argument.
quote: Then I think of the revelation concerning those who will inherit the celestial kingdom, and the Lord said: “… which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.”

claim: Marion G. Romney's second welfare address again uses exalt only in the D&C 104:16 economic sense, plus one passing line that working out one's salvation is indispensable to exaltation.
quote: That he work out his own salvation is indispensable to one’s exaltation.

claim: Marion G. Romney ties individual exaltation to faithfully discharging trust and quotes Joseph Smith's “Son, thou shalt be exalted,” without specifying the content of exaltation.
quote: Our individual exaltation depends upon our proving to the Lord that we will at all hazards and under all circumstances faithfully discharge the trust he has placed in us.

claim: Wm. Grant Bennett affirms a preexistent world where we were spiritual children of the Father and says exaltation in the highest degree will be family exaltation, both in standard generic terms.
quote: exaltation in the highest degree of the celestial kingdom will actually be family exaltation

claim: ElRay L. Christiansen echoes D&C 132's list — honor, power, glory, dominions, even exaltation — as what the Father will share with His sons and daughters, without unpacking any of it.
quote: not only to save them, but also to share with them all that the Father has—associations with those we love, honor, power, glory, dominions, even exaltation.

claim: James E. Faust's anti-abortion address calls procreative power a partnership with God in creation and notes that body and spirit unite before birth, but makes no claim about divine parentage, progression, or offspring.
quote: The exercise of a man or woman’s sacred procreative powers makes each a partner with God in creation and brings to them in parenthood their greatest happiness.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's counsel talk on obedience, gardens, gambling, abortion, and divorce closes with a generic exhortation to become like the Lord and calls mothers partners with God, but makes no claim about divine nature or progression.
quote: We bless you in your efforts to become like our Lord that you will become more like him.

claim: Neal A. Maxwell's discipleship talk quotes the hymn line about having wandered from a more exalted sphere but makes no claim on any axis.
quote: for we have indeed “wandered from a more exalted sphere.”

claim: Delbert L. Stapley quotes Brigham Young that the exalted have no bounds to their privileges and increase through all eternity, but the increase is framed as blessings and privileges rather than posterity, and Stapley adds no independent claim.
quote: the difference between the righteous and the sinner, eternal life or death, happiness or misery, is this, to those who are exalted there are no bounds or limits to their privileges, their blessings have a continuation … they increase through all eternity

claim: O. Leslie Stone says we are God's children created in His own image and quotes D&C 76:24 that the inhabitants of the worlds are begotten sons and daughters unto God, without further comment.
quote: “That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.”

claim: N. Eldon Tanner's retelling of 3 Nephi mentions salvation and exaltation once in passing; no axis content.
quote: He gave them many parables and taught them in all things pertaining to their salvation and exaltation.

claim: Wm. Grant Bennett affirms literal premortal spirit childhood and the temple sealing of families for eternity, but keeps exaltation and progression at the generic covenant-blessing level.
quote: From the scriptures we learn that all of us existed as spirits, literally spirit children of our Father in heaven, before we were born in the flesh.

claim: Ezra Taft Benson testifies that God is a personal being and the Father of our spirits and names the exaltation of His children as the purpose of the Church, all in generic terms.
quote: I know that God lives, that he is a personal being, the Father of our spirits, and that he loves his children and hears and answers their righteous prayers.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball, as Church President, tells the priesthood session that all 225,000 men present may literally become gods with worlds of their own made for them, and describes them passing beyond the angels and the gods already waiting — explicit plural godhood with worlds, though he names no new spirit offspring.
quote: Brethren, 225,000 of you are here tonight. I suppose 225,000 of you may become gods. There seems to be plenty of space out there in the universe. And the Lord has proved that he knows how to do it. I think he could make, or probably have us help make, worlds for all of us, for every one of us 225,000.

claim: N. Eldon Tanner organizes his talk around the laws of God as they pertain to salvation and exaltation, but never specifies what exaltation involves.
quote: third, the laws of God as they pertain to our salvation and exaltation.

claim: Joseph B. Wirthlin closes with a generic hope that we attain a glorious exaltation as beloved children of Heavenly Father.
quote: that we might attain the heights of a glorious exaltation as the beloved children of our Heavenly Father

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's sesquicentennial-themed address on gardens, debt, and Daniel's stone mentions the gospel's doctrines of salvation and exaltation only as a standing invitation, with no content on divine nature or progression.
quote: I feel a special urge today to invite all people everywhere to investigate the restored gospel of Jesus Christ with its doctrines of salvation and of exaltation.
