claim: H. Burke Peterson states flatly that no man is exalted alone and quotes Widtsoe that a spirit was male or female in the far-off beginning, but makes no claim about God's nature, progression, ancestry, or new spirit offspring.
quote: No man will ever be exalted by himself, no matter how great his works on the earth.

claim: LeGrand Richards commends scripture study as the way to know we can be exalted in the presence of our loved ones and Heavenly Father, with no doctrinal expansion.
quote: a knowledge that we can live after death with our loved ones and be exalted in the presence of our dear ones with our Father in heaven

claim: Marion G. Romney argues that because our spirits are literally God's begotten offspring, we inherit the capacity to reach the full status of our heavenly parents by the same natural inheritance logic that lets us reach our mortal parents' status.
quote: As to why we are here on earth, I reminded him of the self-evident fact that, as the offspring of God, we inherit the capability of reaching, in full maturity, the status of our heavenly parents just as we inherit from our mortal parents the capability to attain to their mortal status; and that since God has a body of flesh and bones, it was necessary and perfectly natural for us, his spirit offspring, to obtain such bodies in order that we might be like him.

claim: Robert L. Simpson ties exaltation to perfection and temple work for the dead, without specifying the content of exaltation.
quote: We seek exaltation. To achieve that means perfection, and the direction is clear. We cannot be made perfect without our dead.

claim: James E. Faust cites 3 Nephi 27:27 and Peter's partakers of the divine nature as the standard for discipleship — bare theosis with no divine-nature specification.
quote: Peter counsels us to be “partakers of the divine nature.”

claim: Howard W. Hunter notes that Jesus would inherit all that the Father hath and that any other son or daughter of God may do the same — theosis by inheritance, stated generically.
quote: Jesus knew that if he were faithful to his Father and obedient to every commandment, he would inherit “all that [the] Father hath”—and so would any other son or daughter of God.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's brief closing remarks testify that the gospel will save and exalt mankind, with no doctrinal detail.
quote: I know the gospel truths will save and exalt mankind if men will accept the truth and fully live up to their commitments and covenants.

claim: Bruce R. McConkie describes God the Father as an exalted, glorified Holy Man of flesh and bones and says the plan exists so His spirit children can reach the very same state of glory and exaltation He Himself possesses, capping it with Joseph Smith's line that some are raised to become Gods.
quote: We know, because the Lord has revealed it in this our day, that we are the spirit children of an exalted, glorified Being, a Holy Man who has a body of flesh and bones and who is our Father in heaven.

claim: Marion G. Romney's welfare talk uses exalt in the D&C 104:16 economic sense throughout and cites D&C 76:24 to establish universal siblinghood, without axis content.
quote: We Latter-day Saints know that all men are brothers and sisters—“begotten sons and daughters unto God”

claim: Marion G. Romney glosses 2 Peter's partakers of the divine nature as literally putting on the nature of God through obedience — bare theosis with no further specification.
quote: that by these [we] might be partakers of the divine nature [This has always been interesting and most impressive to me—to put on the nature of God by doing the things the Lord commands.]

claim: Delbert L. Stapley strings together Pauline passages including the joint-heirs verse and twice invokes exaltation as the goal, but offers no comment that goes past generic theosis.
quote: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.”

claim: Royden G. Derrick reads the Beatitudes as sequential steps qualifying us for exaltation, capped by Matthew 5:48 — bare theosis.
quote: Each of the Beatitudes represents a specific step in our orderly progression towards perfection, and teaches us how to qualify ourselves for exaltation

speaker: Spencer W. Kimball
claim: Spencer W. Kimball quotes O My Father in a talk about human potential, including its assertion that there is a Mother in Heaven.
Bruce R. McConkie's South America gathering talk refers to temples where the fulness of the ordinances of exaltation are performed, with no further specification.
quote: There alone were the temples of the Most High where the fulness of the ordinances of exaltation are performed.

claim: Marion G. Romney quotes Joseph Smith's calling-and-election passage and D&C 132:49 on a sealed exaltation and a prepared throne, without commenting on what godhood entails.
quote: “for verily I seal upon you your exaltation, and prepare a throne for you in the kingdom of my Father, with Abraham your father.”

claim: Marion G. Romney's united-order talk uses exalt in the economic sense and says consecration qualifies the rich to become the sons of God; no axis content beyond that.
quote: The united order exalts the poor and humbles the rich. In the process both are sanctified.

claim: Marion D. Hanks's talk on patience with imperfect people quotes Isaiah 30:18 on the Lord being exalted; no axis content.
quote: “And therefore will the Lord wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you.”

claim: Bruce R. McConkie defines eternal life as the kind of life God lives — continuation of the family unit plus a fulness of the Father's glory — and says spirit children may advance until they become like Him, but the claims stay at generic theosis and eternal-family level.
quote: Eternal life is the name of the kind of life God lives. It consists, first, of the continuation of the family unit in eternity, and second, of an inheritance of the fulness of the glory of the Father.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley says the Eternal Father endowed His children with the capacity to be as He and Christ are — perfected, glorified, holy personages — but the rest of the talk is obedience and degrees of glory, with no further specification.
quote: Disobedience to God and His chosen servants ignores the fact that we are all the children of an Eternal Father who has endowed us with the capacity to be as He and His Son Jesus Christ are—perfected, glorified, holy personages.

claim: N. Eldon Tanner refers to young women preparing to be mothers of God's spirit children and calls the priesthood holders God's spirit children, but this is the ordinary mortal-motherhood-of-premortal-spirits usage, not new spirit offspring.
quote: You young men should be kind and considerate of the girls you choose for friends, girls who love the Lord and are preparing themselves to be mothers of the spirit children of God.

claim: Joseph Anderson mentions salvation and exaltation as the reward of obedience and quotes Kingsley on being good/righteous/holy as God is, but the likeness is moral rather than ontological.
quote: If accepted and lived, it will bring salvation and exaltation in his kingdom.

claim: Spencer W. Kimball's Zion-and-materialism address uses exalt only of things that exalt the mind; no axis content.
quote: No, Zion is not things of the lower, but of the higher order, things that exalt the mind and sanctify the heart.

claim: Bruce R. McConkie's apostasy-and-restoration set piece charges that Nicaea and Athanasius debased the true gods of heaven into an incomprehensible spirit essence — a striking plural-gods polemic, but it makes no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or offspring.
quote: At Nicaea and later by the pen of Athanasius he aided in the writing of creeds which debased the true gods of heaven and defined them as an incomprehensible spirit essence which fills the immensity of space.

speaker: Sterling W. Sill
claim: Sterling W. Sill quotes O My Father, including the claim that eternal truth tells us there is a Mother in Heaven.

Eldred G. Smith quotes the Lorenzo Snow couplet in full from the pulpit and then reasons forward from it, treating God's past manhood and man's future godhood as an operative premise for how mortals must learn to decide.
quote: When the gospel plan was explained to Lorenzo Snow, he put the whole plan in a nice epigram: “As man now is, our God once was; as now God is, so man may be.”

claim: N. Eldon Tanner endorses the Lorenzo Snow couplet in the Church's own voice while simultaneously locating the God/man difference purely in knowledge and insisting God knows all truth and is therefore unchanging — affirming God's past manhood but implicitly closing off ongoing divine progression in knowledge.
quote: We believe also that “as man now is, God once was: As God now is, man may be.”

claim: A welfare-session address that invokes exaltation only as generic motivation for living welfare principles.
quote: President Harold B. Lee said, “Priesthood plus womanhood together bring exaltation!”

claim: Extends genealogical ancestry one step into the premortal to reach the Eternal Father, making all humans siblings, but terminates there and asserts no chain beyond God.
quote: I’m reminded that now I must think of mortal generations, but it has also occurred to me that reaching back one premortal generation leads me to our Eternal Father, and I suddenly realize that every name I see in the record is my brother or my sister.

claim: Standard three-degrees resurrection sermon; defines eternal life as exaltation in the family unit without any generative or ancestry content.
quote: Eternal life is to gain exaltation in the highest heaven and live in the family unit.

speaker: Spencer W. Kimball
claim: Spencer W. Kimball directly tells women that their Mother in Heaven helped give eternal intelligence spirit form and pairs that parentage with possible godhood.
Says exalted families form the divine patriarchal order that will be the source of eternal kingdoms, but stops short of new spirit children or any backward chain.
quote: Inspired men have long taught that the home is the cradle of civilization and the foundation of society. But the Lord, through his prophets, teaches us much more than this, for we know that it is exalted families that will make up the divine patriarchal order which will be the source of kingdoms and glory for the faithful in eternity.

claim: Welfare covenant sermon; quotes the oath-and-covenant “all that my Father hath” text purely as a priesthood-obligation proof, with no development.
quote: “And he that receiveth my Father receiveth my Father’s kingdom; therefore all that my Father hath shall be given unto him.”

claim: Relief Society address on citizenship and prophetic counsel; one bare mention of exaltation as the goal of women's work.
quote: And perhaps more important for us, it will take all our heart, might, mind, and strength to do the work the Lord has given us—that is to live so that we, and those we can influence, will gain exaltation in the kingdom of God.

claim: Ten Commandments sermon; exaltation appears only as the generic outcome of ordinances plus conduct.
quote: We obey the ordinances which make exaltation possible.

claim: Sacrifice sermon that quotes D&C 132:19 (thrones, gods, continuation of the seeds) verbatim as the temple-marriage promise and says God desires us to become as He is, but adds no claim of its own beyond the scriptural text.
quote: “Ye shall come forth in the first resurrection; … and shall inherit thrones, kingdoms, principalities, and powers … ; [Ye] shall pass by the angels, and the gods, … to [your] exaltation … , which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever”

claim: Sermon on repentance, forgiveness, and God's individual love; no exaltation, parentage, or divine-progression content.
Commitment sermon; mentions exaltation hereafter and sealing in a patriarchal order without elaboration.
quote: The family is eternal. We may be sealed together forever in a patriarchal order if we are righteous.

claim: Welfare-session address on self-reliance, fast offerings, and priesthood council implementation; no exaltation, parentage, or divine-nature content ('the poor shall be exalted' is economic).
Conversion-testimony sermon; refers once to 'the way to exaltation' and quotes a convert praising celestial marriage, with no doctrinal development.
quote: May I invite you all to study the scriptures, wherein are found the words of eternal life and the way to exaltation.

claim: Sermon on the divine origin and moral weight of language; no axis content.

Restoration sermon that asserts God's corporeal form and premortal human existence and quotes George Albert Smith that any faithful member obtains exaltation, but makes no claim about God's own past, progression, or parentage.
quote: Joseph now knew God is in the form of a man.

claim: Book of Mormon sesquicentennial reading challenge; no axis content.
Sabbath/prayer/journal counsel; states that men cannot be exalted without their wives, but this is the standard celestial-marriage prerequisite with no offspring or parenthood claim attached.
quote: Brethren, we cannot be exalted without our wives. There can be no heaven without righteous women.

speaker: Adney Y. Komatsu
claim: Adney Y. Komatsu quotes the claim that suffering makes people more like their Father and Mother in Heaven while discussing exalted blessing.

McConkie's creedal summary to the world simultaneously calls God 'a holy man' and 'the Eternal Absolute' who 'knows all things, has all power'—an absolutist formulation of God that forecloses divine progression, stated a year before his 1980 'Seven Deadly Heresies' denial, while still promising Mormonism will 'make of man a god.'
quote: He is the Supreme Being, the Eternal Absolute, the Creator and peopler of worlds without number.

claim: Lists Joseph Smith's doctrinal contributions including God's corporeal form, spirit childhood, and becoming 'Godlike' through eternal progression, but renders deification only in the softest generic terms and says nothing of God's own past or parentage.
quote: …that we are spirit children of God, that we had a premortal existence, that we are in mortality to prove ourselves, and that if we are faithful we can return to live eternally in the presence of God and through eternal progression become Godlike.

claim: Priesthood sermon on 'salt of the earth' and being 'saviors of men' through fellowshipping and temple work; no theosis, parentage, or divine-nature claim.

Argues that the world's Gods are man-made and only the restored God is real, but never specifies what God is—no statement of His past, progression, or parentage; premortal acquaintance and 'the path of exaltation' appear only generically.
quote: …we all long for our Heavenly Father and desire after him, because we knew him before we came to this earth.

claim: Narrative Easter sermon on Lazarus, the Atonement, and the Restoration; 'God shall exalt thee on high' is quoted of Joseph Smith's trials, not of deification.
Sermon on adversity as necessary resistance for eternal progress; 'achieved their exaltation' appears once, of scriptural figures, with no content on the nature of that exaltation.
quote: Documented in scripture are episodes from the lives of many former-day Saints who, by personal sacrifice, opposition, and adversity, achieved their exaltation.

claim: Official sesquicentennial proclamation of the First Presidency and Twelve; affirms divine sonship of all people and eternal family sealing, but renders the postmortal destiny only as 'working and growing toward perfection'—no godhood, increase, or divine-ancestry language in a document explicitly summarizing the Church's doctrine to the world.
quote: We bear witness that all men and women are sons and daughters of God, each accountable to him; that our lives here on earth are part of an eternal plan; … and that we shall there have the opportunity of working and growing toward perfection.

claim: Temple and genealogy sermon; asserts flatly that exaltation is by family unit but develops nothing beyond sealing and vicarious work.
quote: This work welds eternal links that bind us to each other and to our fathers. We are exalted as family units.

claim: Sermon on adversity as an instrument of growth; no axis content.
Report on Church growth among Latin American members; one passing reference to 'our progress toward exaltation.'
quote: Their lives teach of the basics of the gospel—godly traits—traits that we could do well to emulate in our progress toward exaltation.

claim: The General Conference restatement of McConkie's June 1980 'Seven Deadly Heresies' denial of divine progression: he ridicules the view that God is still learning as a 'student god' bordering on blasphemy, insists God is 'from everlasting to everlasting the same unchangeable God' who 'knows all things,' while also affirming that we are 'the offspring of celestial parents.'
quote: And there are even those who champion the almost unbelievable theory that God is an eternal student enrolled in the University of the Universe, where he is busily engaged in learning new truths and amassing new and strange knowledge that he never knew before.

claim: Fatherhood sermon; 'ordinances of exaltation' and 'family exalted in the celestial kingdom' appear as the goal but with no content on what exaltation consists of.
quote: Fatherhood is not a matter of station or wealth; it is a matter of desire, diligence, and determination to see one's family exalted in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Priesthood-session instruction on fast offerings and ward budgets; no axis content.

Sermon on moral values and eternal families; describes the sealing chain running backward to progenitors and forward to posterity, but the chain is entirely human and terminates in neither divine ancestry nor spirit offspring.
quote: How could any thinking person who loves his family not want such a precious gift—to be with his wife and his family in this life and the next, and then to include parents and other progenitors (going back) and grandchildren and their continuing posterity (going forward) in an eternal family relationship.

claim: Packer closes a General Conference sermon on marriage by naming 'eternal increase' as the third term of the celestial ideal—and concedes the doctrine 'is new to many'—after a recited poem placing the procreative power inside 'God's own plan' by which 'spirit offspring of our God can come through mortal birth.'
quote: Eternal love, eternal marriage, eternal increase! This ideal, which is new to many, when thoughtfully considered, can keep a marriage strong and safe.

claim: Welfare-session sermon on family responsibility and charity; 'preparatory steps for exaltation' and universal spirit siblinghood appear only as framing.
quote: To those who are not members of a “typical” LDS family—and there are many—may we offer a reminder that we are all literally brothers and sisters. We are members of that heavenly family.

claim: Frames eternal progression as a human trajectory across all three estates and quotes only the opening, anodyne half of the King Follett Discourse (knowing God's character and conversing with Him), omitting the exalted-man claim that follows in the same sermon.
quote: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints teaches the value of eternal progression. We progressed in the premortal existence, and we have the opportunity to progress in this estate and throughout all eternity.

speaker: Angel Abrea
claim: Angel Abrea quotes Joseph Smith's claim that people become gods by the same path as the Gods who went before, from exaltation to exaltation.
Welfare-session address on self-reliance, empathy, and debt; no axis content.

Relief Society address grounding women's role in a premortal council assignment and promising a woman may become her husband's 'queen for all eternity,' but keeps the maternal role strictly to ushering God's existing spirit children into mortality—no postmortal spirit offspring and no Heavenly Mother.
quote: Since the beginning, a woman's first and most important role has been ushering into mortality spirit sons and daughters of our Father in Heaven.

claim: Missionary-service appeal that lists D&C 132:19's promises—including 'a continuation of the seeds forever and ever'—as the reward outweighing worldly careers, and says the faithful will 'live the kind of life He lives,' but adds nothing beyond the scriptural phrases.
quote: He has promised “thrones, kingdoms, principalities, and powers.” He has promised “exaltation and glory in all things.” He has promised “a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.”

claim: Testimony of Joseph Smith's prophetic mission and human fallibility; 'eternal exaltation to mankind' appears once as a summary of the restored ordinances.
quote: By revelation from God, the Church also possesses those keys, saving principles, and ordinances which will bring eternal exaltation to mankind, living and dead.

claim: Personal anecdotes about Spencer W. Kimball; preserves Kimball's quip distinguishing being saved from being exalted, but with no content on what exaltation is.
quote: When we tried to save his strength, he'd say, “I know you are trying to save me. But I don't want to be saved; I want to be exalted.”

claim: Sermon on divine and human mercy; no axis content ('will he be exalted' is Isaiah 30:18 of the Lord's graciousness).

Welfare sermon that pairs Moses 1's innumerable worlds and 'no end to my works' with the question of becoming as God is, but frames the likeness entirely as unselfish service, not godhood or increase.
quote: Hence, we see the complete unselfishness of our Father in Heaven. His whole work and glory is to bring eternal life and happiness to his children. … If not, how can we ever hope to be as he is?

claim: Sermon on agency versus Satan's robot-like bondage; says the obedient child's destiny is to partake of God's glory and share his exalted work, but with no godhood, increase, or divine-ancestry content despite the title.
quote: …whose potential for growth and accomplishment is limitless; whose destiny, if he is fully obedient, is to return to the presence of God to partake of his glory and to share in his exalted work.

claim: Relief Society address on supporting sisters through life transitions; one generic reference to becoming worthy of exaltation.
quote: Then, with him as the center of our lives, we can develop those Christlike qualities which will make us worthy of exaltation.

claim: Sermon on valiance and loyalty to Church leaders; exaltation appears only as a stake that can be lost, plus the D&C 121:29 'thrones and dominions' promise quoted without development.
quote: One who rationalizes that he or she has a testimony of Jesus Christ but cannot accept direction and counsel from the leadership of His church is in a fundamentally unsound position and is in jeopardy of losing exaltation.

claim: Practical instruction on reactivating Aaronic Priesthood youth; exaltation named twice as the destination but never described.
quote: …they have taken a road which, if not changed, will eventually prevent them from receiving the greatest gift of God to man—that of eternal life and exaltation.

claim: McConkie tells the General Conference priesthood session in plain terms that the Melchizedek covenant admits men to a patriarchal order guaranteeing 'eternal increase, or in other words of spirit children in the resurrection' and 'exaltation and godhood,' with families 'patterned after the family of God our Heavenly Father'—while defining the Father as one 'who knows all things and is infinite in all his attributes,' again foreclosing divine progression.
quote: In return the Lord admits them to his eternal patriarchal order, an order that prevails in the highest heaven of the celestial world, an order that assures its members of eternal increase, or in other words of spirit children in the resurrection.

claim: Eight-step sermon on repentance and starting over; 'will be exalted' appears once in the closing testimony with no content.
quote: I testify that the gospel of Jesus Christ has been restored and that we are to live its principles and precepts, and by so doing will be exalted.

claim: Relief Society address on unity amid diversity; names exaltation as distinct from salvation and speaks of developing 'the divine within us,' but never says what exaltation is.
quote: By knowing and witnessing that he lives and that his great mission is to make it possible for us to attain not only salvation but also exaltation.

claim: Temple-history sermon on Elijah and the sealing power; makes becoming like God conditional on that sealing power but supplies no content about what becoming like Him entails.
quote: Without the authority and use of that power, in all ages of the world, none of our Heavenly Father's children can enter His presence or ever become like Him!

claim: Testimony of Christ's premortal, mortal, resurrected, and millennial roles; affirms Christ's premortal likeness to the Father but claims no progression, parentage, or increase.
quote: I bear testimony that Jesus Christ was the first begotten Son of God in the Spirit. Like the Father himself, he was a personage of great power and intelligence in the universe.

claim: McConkie opens with 'He is a Holy Man' of the Father, then stages Christ's own rise to deity—a spirit child who 'over long ages and eons … advanced and progressed until he became like unto God'—and promises the faithful 'the same glorious exaltation enjoyed by the Father himself'; a completed progression to godhood is thus affirmed of the Son by the same man who denies ongoing progression of the Father.
quote: By obedience, by righteousness, through faith, over long ages and eons, this Firstborn of the Father, our Elder Brother, advanced and progressed until he became like unto God in power, in might, in dominion, and in intelligence.

claim: Welfare sermon that defines godhood functionally as service and says we want to be 'as He is,' but the content of that likeness is moral (unselfish service), not generative, genealogical, or progressive.
quote: Can we see how critical self-reliance becomes when looked upon as the prerequisite to service, when we also know service is what Godhood is all about?

claim: Priesthood-session counsel on strengthening families (prayer, scripture study, work, discipline, loyalty); no theosis, parentage, or divine-nature content.
Sermon on the sacrament ordinance; 'advancement and exaltation in the kingdom of God' and 'the blessings of eternal progression' appear as generic framing.
quote: Associated with the partaking of the sacrament are principles that are fundamental to man's advancement and exaltation in the kingdom of God and the shaping of one's spiritual character.

claim: Balloon-flight analogy for shedding spiritual ballast; one closing reference to Christ as mediator for salvation and exaltation.
quote: He is the Savior of mankind, the great mediator for the salvation and exaltation of all of our Heavenly Father's children, if they are willing to follow his outlined flight plan.

claim: Reads Malachi's 'neither root nor branch' as the loss of the eternal family—roots being one's ancestors and branches one's children—and makes exaltation dependent on retaining that chain, but the chain is entirely mortal-genealogical and never reaches spirit offspring or godhood.
quote: In other words, those who pay tithing will have roots and branches at the last day and those who do not will have neither roots nor branches. … Then those who walk in holiness before the Lord, which includes the payment of tithing, will have an eternal family at the last day.

claim: Names exaltation only as the purpose behind Church programs; no doctrinal content on any axis.
quote: All should be engaged in for the purpose of saving and exalting souls.

claim: Quotes Joseph Fielding Smith that exaltation requires a sealed man and wife who then “continue and become like the Lord” — couple-exaltation plus bare theosis, with no offspring or increase claim.
quote: No man shall receive the fulness of eternity, of exaltation, alone; no woman shall receive that blessing alone; but man and wife, when they receive the sealing power in the temple of the Lord, … shall pass on to exaltation, and shall continue and become like the Lord.

claim: A full talk on premortal life asserting we are spiritually God's children and lived with Him in spirit form, but it never specifies mechanism, spirit birth, or anything about God's own origin.
quote: The doctrine is simply this: life did not begin with mortal birth. We lived in spirit form before we entered mortality. We are spiritually the children of God.

speaker: Gene R. Cook
claim: Gene R. Cook quotes O My Father in a family-and-eternal-pattern talk, including its Mother in Heaven assertion.
Uses “exalt” almost entirely in the Lukan humility/abasement sense; one generic reference to attributes qualifying for exaltation.
quote: Each of the parables spoken by the Savior seems to teach a principle or give an admonition regarding the attributes necessary to qualify for exaltation.

claim: Model prayer thanks God for a plan by which His spirit children may “advance and progress and become like thee” — bare theosis, no regress, increase, or divine-progression claim.
quote: We thank thee that thou didst ordain and establish the great and eternal plan of salvation whereby we, as thy spirit children, are given power, if faithful and true in all things, to advance and progress and become like thee.

claim: Temple covenants are called the covenants of exaltation by which children can “become like our Heavenly Father” — bare theosis.
quote: Teach your children that only by receiving these ordinances and making these covenants can they be exalted and become like our Heavenly Father.

claim: Endurance sermon; exaltation and eternal life appear only as the finish line of a race metaphor.
quote: To become a winner in the race for eternal life requires effort—constant work, striving, and enduring well with God’s help.

claim: Aaronic Priesthood charge; equates eternal life with exaltation as the greatest gift, nothing further.
quote: As a preparatory priesthood it is preparing you ultimately, of course, for eternal life and exaltation.

claim: In his creedal “Test one,” McConkie defines the true God as a “Holy Man” and “a glorified and exalted being” who already “knows all things and has all power, all might, and all dominion” — a general-conference assertion of complete divine omniscience and omnipotence by the central figure in the eternal-progression debate, i.e. progression in knowledge foreclosed, while God's own exalted status is left as an accomplished fact.
quote: He is a glorified and exalted being in whom all fulness and perfection dwell, who knows all things and has all power, all might, and all dominion.

claim: Gospel-vs-Church distinction; exaltation named as the goal of the divine plan without doctrinal specification.
quote: The gospel is the divine plan for personal, individual salvation and exaltation.

claim: Atonement sermon; the faithful “shall become as their Maker and sit with him on his throne,” and heaven is where “gods and angels dwell” — bare theosis language with no regress or increase claim.
quote: …all shall become as their Maker and sit with him on his throne and reign with him forever in everlasting glory.

claim: Quotes D&C 76:58 (“they are gods”) and D&C 93 in defining exaltation as candidacy declared in the sacrament — scriptural theosis, unelaborated.
quote: “They are they into whose hands the Father has given all things. … Wherefore, as it is written, they are gods” who “shall dwell in the presence of God and his Christ forever and ever.”

claim: The oath and covenant's promise of “all that my Father hath” is glossed as eternal life/inheritance, explicitly left unexplained.
quote: Few of us, I suppose, can comprehend all that this promise means. Even though we know that it includes eternal life, or the inheritance of exaltation, still it is so great and so wonderful that it defies proper explanation.

claim: Love sermon; calls loving one's neighbor “a godlike trait” and the gospel one “of salvation and exaltation.”
quote: To love our neighbor is a godlike trait and can take many forms.

claim: Asserts the mutual dependence of man and woman for exaltation, but attaches no increase or parenthood claim to it.
quote: The man cannot be exalted without the woman; neither the woman without the man.

claim: Spirituality sermon; children-of-God language and exaltation as eventual outcome, nothing on the axes.
quote: …these enterprises called forth the sacrifices that molded pioneers into Saints and prepared Saints for exaltation.

claim: Exclusivity sermon; one generic statement that ordinances are required to exalt mankind.
quote: Good conduct without the ordinances of the gospel will neither redeem nor exalt mankind; covenants and the ordinances are essential.

claim: Defines a fulness of joy as exaltation in passing while treating salvation, judgment, and grace; no axis content.
quote: …the Judgment requires the spirit and the body inseparably connected in order to receive a fulness of joy, meaning exaltation—or damnation.

claim: Missionary-history talk; references the Father's plan for the exaltation of His children and “man's eternal possibilities” without specifying them.
quote: From them we glean the truths that will open to us a clear understanding of man’s eternal possibilities.

claim: Welfare-program sermon; the single occurrence of “exalts” is socioeconomic (Romney on giving), and nothing touches divine nature, ancestry, progression, or increase.
quote: The process of giving exalts the poor and humbles the rich.

claim: Testimony of the living Christ; exaltation named once as an outcome of obedience.
quote: …there is a way for them to gain salvation and exaltation.

claim: Welfare/poverty sermon; the one “exalted” is the scriptural socioeconomic sense (D&C 104), and no axis content appears.
quote: “But it must needs be done in mine own way; and behold this is the way that I, the Lord, have decreed to provide for my saints, that the poor shall be exalted, in that the rich are made low.

claim: A deliberate public statement of Hinckley's “position on this most important of all theological subjects” written against an anti-Mormon tract: it affirms God's embodiment and spirit-fatherhood but says nothing about God having been a man or having a Father, and distinguishes God's eternal body from his own mortal one.
quote: I do not equate my body with His in its refinement, in its capacity, in its beauty and radiance. His is eternal. Mine is mortal.

claim: Joy sermon; ordinances “of salvation and exaltation” and the crown of “glory, immortality, and eternal life” as the closing promise.
quote: Joy comes from our posterity, and we rejoice as they are blessed by the ordinances of salvation and exaltation.

claim: Uses the plural “household of our heavenly parents” for the premortal home and frames mortality as required for progression, but asserts nothing about a Mother in Heaven.
quote: Sisters, the anxiety and disquieting influence of this earth life could have been avoided had we stayed nestled in the household of our heavenly parents, but then how could we have progressed?

claim: Home-teaching program address; exaltation appears only as a program outcome.
quote: …a program so vital that, if faithfully followed, it will help to spiritually renew the Church and exalt its individual members and families.

claim: Grounds chastity in our being God's spirit children and heirs to eternal life — a compact recital of standard premortal-parentage doctrine with no elaboration.
quote: We are his spirit children (see D&C 76:24). We were with him in the beginning (see D&C 93:23). Bringing to pass our exaltation is his work and glory (see Moses 1:39).

claim: Spiritual-gifts sermon; “Love brings eternal progression” is about human relations, and exaltation is named generically.
quote: What a spiritual comfort and blessing it is to know that, if we look to our Savior Jesus Christ and endure to the end, eternal life and exaltation can be ours.

claim: Fatherhood/roles address; exaltation of the family is the stated stake, with no doctrine of eternal increase attached.
quote: Oh, husbands and fathers in Israel, you can do so much for the salvation and exaltation of your families!

claim: Faith sermon responding to the Hofmann forgeries; exaltation named once in a closing prayer sequence.
quote: …and that through the atonement of the Son of God all shall rise from the grave and the faithful shall go on to exaltation.

speaker: Howard W. Hunter
claim: Howard W. Hunter repeats Orson F. Whitney's language that suffering makes people more like their Father and Mother in Heaven.
Missionary anecdotes; the only axis-adjacent line is inside a quoted missionary letter about teaching the plan of salvation.
quote: Today we taught a choice family about the plan of salvation and blessings of exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Perseverance sermon; “fill the measure of our creation as sons and daughters” and the Matthew 5:48 perfection command, unelaborated.
quote: Our goal should be to fill the measure of our creation as sons and daughters of our Heavenly Father—that is, to reach exaltation and eternal life.

claim: Celestial marriage is made a requirement for a fulness of glory and unmarried delay is said to withhold “choice spirits” from mortality — premortal spirits awaiting bodies, not new spirit children of exalted parents.
quote: Without marriage, the purposes of the Lord would be frustrated. Choice spirits would be withheld from the experience of mortality.

claim: Quotes Kimball that men cannot be exalted without their wives and says married couples “literally become partners with God in creating new human life” — mortal procreation as divine partnership, not postmortal spirit increase.
quote: When within the covenant of marriage a man and a woman invoke the great powers of creation, they literally become partners with God in creating new human life.

claim: Argues exegetically that since the body comes from mortal parents, Paul's “offspring of God” must mean the spirit — an unusually explicit statement of literal divine spirit parentage, but strictly backward-looking about us, with no claim about God's own Father and none about exalted humans producing new spirit children.
quote: It is the spirit which is the offspring of God. The writer of Hebrews refers to Him as “the Father of spirits” (Heb. 12:9). The spirits of all men are literally His “begotten sons and daughters” (D&C 76:24).

claim: Celestial marriage as the goal; temple marriage called “a gospel ordinance of exaltation” with no further doctrine.
quote: Temple marriage is a gospel ordinance of exaltation. Our Father in Heaven wants each of His daughters to have this eternal blessing.

claim: Instruction on funeral decorum; the single “exaltation” denotes an emotional state of peace at graveside, and nothing in the talk touches the axes.
quote: Many have come to marvel in their hearts that such a feeling of peace, even exaltation, can come at the time of such grief and uncertainty.

claim: Quotes Benson that young women are “literally the royal daughters of our Father in Heaven” and frames life as a “quest for exaltation”; divine-potential language only.
quote: Remember who you are and the divine heritage that is yours—you are literally the royal daughters of our Father in Heaven.

claim: Priesthood/marriage counsel quoting Benson that temple marriage is essential to exaltation; no axis elaboration.
quote: Understand that temple marriage is essential to your salvation and exaltation.

claim: Defines exaltation as the earned reward and the highest of three degrees in the celestial kingdom, and repeats the Matthew/3 Nephi perfection command — structure without content on any axis.
quote: The reward is exaltation in the celestial kingdom of God. Exaltation is the highest of three degrees of glory in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Growth statistics and a sermon on love; exaltation named as the destination of the Father's plan.
quote: Out of His love for us, He has given an eternal plan which, when followed, leads to exaltation in His kingdom.

claim: Young-men sports-metaphor talk; exaltation named once as an outcome.
quote: Making these points will help lead them to joy and happiness and exaltation.

claim: Commitment sermon; exaltation named once alongside salvation as based on endurance.
quote: Salvation and exaltation are here emphasized as being based primarily upon commitment and enduring.

claim: Counsel to older members; “eternity will be but an extension of righteous family life” asserts continuity of the family unit without any claim about increase or spirit offspring.
quote: After all, eternity will be but an extension of righteous family life.

claim: Temple-service reflections; the temple's promise is “the blessing of eternal life and exaltation,” unelaborated.
quote: The Lord invites all to come unto Christ through the ordinances and covenants of the temple, that we might receive the greatest of all God’s gifts to His children, the blessing of eternal life and exaltation.

claim: Near-death account and sacrament sermon; distinguishes free immortality from earned eternal life but adds nothing on the axes.
quote: Immortality comes to us all as a free gift by the grace of God alone, without works of righteousness. Eternal life, however, is the reward for obedience to the laws and ordinances of His gospel.

claim: Sermon against seeking personal recognition; the one “exalt” is self-exaltation in the pejorative sense and no axis content appears.
quote: Men and women who even momentarily take their eyes off of God’s glory and seek to exalt themselves … will find that the kingdom quickly moves on without them.

claim: Closes by promising faithful Saints “thrones, kingdoms, principalities, glory, immortality, and eternal lives” with a D&C 132:19 citation, but quotes the increase formula without unpacking it and never mentions a Mother in Heaven.
quote: To all faithful Saints He has promised thrones, kingdoms, principalities, glory, immortality, and eternal lives. (See Rom. 2:7; D&C 75:5; 128:12, 23; 132:19.)

claim: Sermon on obscure faithfulness; exaltation invoked as the ultimate goal reached by covenant-keeping regardless of position.
quote: Prominent position—“hanging on the wall at seminary”—does not put anyone on a fast-track to exaltation.

claim: Report on humble members abroad; exaltation in the celestial kingdom is named as the outcome of basic gospel essentials.
quote: They know that faith, repentance, baptism, the Holy Ghost, service to others, and keeping the commandments are the essentials for exaltation in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Administrative address announcing centralized funding; exaltation named once as the Church's purpose.
quote: Its purpose is to bring salvation and exaltation to both the living and the dead.

claim: Quotes Brigham Young's council-in-heaven narrative in which the Father says His own attributes are in His children, and Woodruff on law and glory — theosis premise stated at second hand, without regress or increase.
quote: They are my children; the attributes which you see in me are in my children and they must use their agency.

claim: Patterns-for-living sermon; exaltation named twice as the goal of righteous patterns.
quote: To gain exaltation and happy daily life, we must follow a pattern of righteousness.

claim: Temple/premortality sermon: affirms preexistence as a restored doctrine and quotes D&C 130:18–19 on knowledge rising with us, but every claim stays on the human side of the ledger.
quote: One of these restored doctrines, premortality or preexistence, should give us a greater appreciation for ourselves and the work assigned us, for each one of us existed as a spirit entity before we were born on this earth.

claim: Sermon on Christ's yoke; exaltation appears once in the closing appeal.
quote: In meekness and lowliness, we must learn of him in order to receive eternal life and exaltation.

claim: Bare mention of dependence on Christ for salvation and exaltation, with no content about what exaltation entails.
quote: After sharing his testimony of the mission of our Lord, Jesus Christ, President Carter declared his complete dependence on Christ for salvation and exaltation.

claim: Generic divine-image and premortal-home language addressed to women; no claim about divine parentage mechanism, progression, or spirit offspring.
quote: If we will but realize that we have been created in the image of God, we will not find Him difficult to approach, for God did create “man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”

claim: Standard three-degrees eschatology plus generic divine-daughter and premortal-reserve language; exaltation named but not unpacked.
quote: There the faithful will dwell together with their families, enjoying exaltation with our Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son.

claim: Moral-issues sermon; exaltation appears only as a bare term in an argument about interdependence, with no doctrinal content on any axis.
quote: And the simple truth is that we cannot be happy, nor saved, nor exalted, without one another.

claim: Affirms the standard embodied-Father / Father-of-spirits doctrine without asserting divine ancestry above the Father, God's progression, or new spirit offspring.
quote: I testify that the Savior is a resurrected being, having a tangible body of flesh and bones, and that his Heavenly Father, who is also the Father of the spirits of us all, similarly has a tangible body of flesh and bones.

claim: Closing benediction relaying President Benson's words; only a bare reference to ordinances necessary for exaltation.
quote: God has again revealed himself from heaven and restored to the earth his holy priesthood with power to administer in all the sacred ordinances necessary for the exaltation of his children.

claim: Administrative state-of-the-Church report; exaltation appears once as a bare term tied to temple ordinance work.
quote: The exaltation of our Father’s children rests upon the completion of required ordinances, if all are to move forward on the road that leads to immortality and eternal life.

claim: Quotes Joseph F. Smith that neither man nor woman can be exalted alone, but stops at generic marital exaltation with no claim about heavenly parenthood, spirit offspring, or divine ancestry.
quote: President Joseph F. Smith once declared “that no man can be saved and exalted in the kingdom of God without the woman, and no woman can reach perfection and exaltation in the kingdom of God, alone.

claim: Quotes Spencer W. Kimball on young men's possibility of becoming a god — explicit deification language, but bare theosis with no spirit-offspring, progression, or ancestry content.
quote: President Spencer W. Kimball stated that “you are the sons of God. You are the elect of God, and you have within your [grasp] the possibility to become a god and pass by the angels … to your exaltation”—possibilities which seem beyond ordinary imagination, yet the promises are divine

claim: Sermon on reverence, revelation, and worship music; no content on any taxonomy axis.
quote: It is about reverence and how it relates to revelation that I wish to speak.

claim: Asserts parental titles persist after this life and names God's plan of exaltation, but only in generic terms with no spirit-offspring or divine-ancestry content.
quote: The titles of Mother and Father will persist after this life.

claim: Temple sermon quoting Brigham Young on gaining eternal exaltation and describing sealed couples as organizing an eternal family; no claim beyond generic eternal parenthood.
quote: When sweethearts kneel at the temple altar and are joined by the power of the holy priesthood for time and all eternity, an eternal family is organized and is created.

claim: Relief Society sesquicentennial address using exaltation as the metaphorical summit of the journey; bare theosis via Moroni 7:48, no axis-specific content.
quote: We will lift our eyes to the mountains and move ceaselessly towards exaltation.

claim: Relief Society anniversary charge with four practical challenges; divine potential mentioned only in passing, no taxonomy content.
quote: Expand your knowledge, both intellectual and spiritual, to the full stature of your divine potential.

claim: Relief Society history and priesthood-authority sermon; states only that eternal marriage is the sole relationship culminating in exaltation, without unpacking what exaltation entails.
quote: The ultimate and highest expression of womanhood and manhood is in the new and everlasting covenant of marriage between a man and a woman. Only this relationship culminates in exaltation.

claim: Brief conference-opening tribute to the ailing President Benson; only a bare quoted phrase about following a course to exaltation.
quote: May we do so regardless of what the world may say or do, that we may hold fast to the iron rod, that we may be true to the faith, that we may maintain the standards set for us and follow this course to safety and exaltation.

claim: Doctrinal sermon on grace as enabling power; exaltation appears only as a bare endpoint phrase.
quote: If we can obtain the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, that divine enabling power to assist us, we will triumph in this life and be exalted in the life to come.

claim: Teaches premortal assignment of fatherhood/motherhood roles to God's spirit sons and daughters and an eternal-family goal, but stays generic on parenthood and says nothing about spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: Our Heavenly Father assigned different responsibilities in mortality to men and women when we lived with Him as His spirit sons and daughters. To His sons He would give the priesthood and the responsibilities of fatherhood, and to His daughters He gave the responsibilities of motherhood, each with its attendant functions.

claim: Relief Society address on covenants; names exaltation as the sought-after goal but gives it no doctrinal content.
quote: As women of covenant we seek exaltation and the peace that attends eternal life in the kingdom of heaven.

claim: Sermon on illness, accident, and death, with Christ as exemplar; no taxonomy-axis content.
quote: Saul, on the road to Damascus, had a vision of the risen, exalted Christ.

claim: Nelson's whole thesis lists God's unchangeableness as constant number one — 'unchanging principles are so because they come from our unchanging Heavenly Father' — an apostolic immutability affirmation (weak-form 'God always God', not an explicit denial of progression in dominions); he also closes by applying D&C 132:19's 'continuation of the seeds forever and ever' to sealed couples.
quote: Unchanging principles are so because they come from our unchanging Heavenly Father.

claim: Opens with the standard 'spirit children of heavenly parents' formulation and premortal gender, but the plural-parents language is bare boilerplate with no Heavenly Mother content, no spirit-offspring claim, and no divine-ancestry or progression claim.
quote: The gospel teaches us that we are the spirit children of heavenly parents.

claim: Closing two-keys parable promises that the treasure only a man and woman together can unlock — plainly the joint procreative power, given the talk's frame — is replenished and never diminished in all eternity; force depends on that identification, so a reviewer may downgrade to REDUNDANT.
quote: He was promised that if he used the treasure worthily, it would be replenished and never be diminished, not in all eternity.

claim: Sermon on the mechanics of repentance and divine forgiveness; only bare references to divine potential and exalting ordinances.
quote: One who assumes that he can or must pay the price for his sins and thereby earn divine forgiveness will not feel free to continue progress toward realizing his divine potential, that is, eternal life.

claim: Quotes D&C 132:19 in full — passing by the gods to exaltation and 'a continuation of the seeds forever and ever' — but supplies no exposition of the increase language beyond calling it the blessings of exaltation.
quote: and they shall pass by the angels, and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever

claim: Father-son analogy sermon affirming that we are God's offspring and quoting D&C 130:2 on eternal sociality; no claim beyond generic divine sonship.
quote: We are in truth his offspring, and he is “not far from every one of us”

claim: Address on family breakdown and fathers' duties; eternal sealing and exaltation appear only as bare endpoints, with no axis content.
quote: The ultimate purpose of every teaching, every activity in the Church is that parents and their children are happy at home, sealed in an eternal marriage, and linked to their generations.

claim: Names eternal exaltation as life's destiny and highest goal, but supplies no content about what it consists of.
quote: We are here today because we believe that our destiny in life is to gain eternal exaltation.

claim: Family history and temple sermon quoting Howard W. Hunter that sealing can continue 'until the family of God is made perfect'; eternal family linkage only, no spirit-offspring, ancestry, or progression claim.
quote: The sealing of family units can be continued until the family of God is made perfect.

claim: First address after his call, on always remembering the Savior; exaltation named once as an atonement consequence with no content.
quote: Because of his atonement we may be exalted.

claim: Solemn-assembly address on sustaining and obeying living prophets; only bare references to exalting temple blessings.
quote: They have pleaded with us to live more Christlike lives, to emulate the Savior in all we do, and to qualify ourselves to be worthy of the saving and exalting blessings available only in the holy temples of the Lord.

claim: Home-teaching sermon; the word exalt appears once inside a Benson quotation about the program's effect on members.
quote: [Home teaching is] a program so vital that, if faithfully followed, it will help to spiritually renew the Church and exalt its individual members and families

claim: Lists 'eternal increase' as an Abrahamic-covenant entitlement and quotes D&C 132:19's thrones-and-dominions promise, but neither is expounded into a claim about spirit offspring or divine ancestry.
quote: Abraham’s posterity would be numerous, entitled to eternal increase and to bear the priesthood;

claim: Oaks makes the plural heavenly parents the foundational premise of LDS theology and deification the highest aspiration, and explicitly ties LDS exaltation to the patristic doctrine of deification/apotheosis — a specific, quotable Heavenly-Mother-plus-theosis claim from the pulpit six months before the Family Proclamation.
quote: Our theology begins with heavenly parents. Our highest aspiration is to be like them.

claim: Quotes D&C 131:1-4 verbatim including the 'cannot have an increase' penalty and glosses the highest degree as requiring the new and everlasting covenant, but the increase language is left unexpounded and pivots to mortal childbearing.
quote: He may enter into the other, but that is the end of his kingdom; he cannot have an increase

claim: Historical tribute to Hyrum Smith; exaltation appears once as a bare phrase describing the Father's plan.
quote: Visiting those inspirational sites and immersing ourselves as a family in the events of the Restoration reminded me again of the marvelous privilege we have to live in a day when we have such clear doctrinal understanding of our Heavenly Father’s plan for the salvation and exaltation of His children.

claim: Sermon on the law of witnesses and special witnesses of Christ; exaltation appears once inside a quoted Hinckley testimony.
quote: each of us, if we will walk in obedience to His truths, may go on to exaltation and an eternal life beyond our ability at this stage to understand or comprehend

claim: Sermon on patriarchal and priesthood blessings and lineage declaration; exaltation named once as the Savior's aim, with no axis content.
quote: These individualized priesthood blessings are a powerful witness of the love of the Lord Jesus Christ in seeking to bring exaltation to each of us.

claim: Survey of priesthood blessings across a lifetime; exaltation and eternal family union named only as bare endpoints.
quote: In the temple, they see themselves as the offspring of royalty—as a son or a daughter of God.

claim: Priesthood-session report on missionary work, temple building, and Church finances; exaltation named once as a bare promise to prospective missionaries.
quote: You will realize that through His atoning sacrifice He has opened the way for eternal life and an exaltation above and beyond your greatest dreams.

claim: Restates the 'spirit lineage to heavenly parents' formula as the answer to 'Who am I?' and calls eternal progress a central idea, but the plural-parents phrase is used only for self-worth and the progression in view is human, not divine.
quote: I am a child of God with a spirit lineage to heavenly parents. That parentage defines our eternal potential.

claim: Sermon on repentance, restitution, and forgiveness; exaltation appears only in an endnote distinguishing forgiveness from exaltation in David's case.
quote: Forgiveness does not, however, necessarily assure exaltation, as is the case with David

claim: Closes with a blunt apostolic deification statement — 'He is preparing you to be a god' — but it is bare theosis with no spirit-offspring, ancestry, or divine-progression content, and Scott explicitly declines to unpack it.
quote: He is preparing you to be a god. You cannot understand fully what that means, yet He knows.

claim: Sermon on moral warfare and symptoms of spiritual decline; 'exalting' appears once as an adjective about wasted effort.
quote: I have observed that the great majority of people the world over waste and wear out their lives making major commitments of time and effort toward projects that have absolutely no exalting benefits yet have eternal consequences.

claim: Defines eternal life as being exalted and living with the Father and Son, and insists commandments cannot be softened, but the exaltation content is generic and the immutability point is about commandments, not God.
quote: Eternal life, “the greatest of all the gifts of God” , is to be exalted and to live with Heavenly Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, in all the eternities to come.

claim: Priesthood-session sermon on personal cleanliness built around Joseph F. Smith's dream; 'the exalted' appears only inside the quoted dream narrative.
quote: and I could name over as many as I remember of their names, who sat there, who seemed to be among the chosen, among the exalted

claim: Sermon on finding joy amid adversity; exaltation named once as the destination of the journey.
quote: Remember you are on a journey to exaltation.

claim: Hales opens by repeating Oaks's formula that the doctrine of the family begins with heavenly parents, then defines eternal life itself as including 'eternal increase for all the eternities to come' — an apostolic gloss that makes generative exaltation part of the definition, not just a quoted scripture.
quote: each mortal can have the blessing of attaining eternal life; that is, returning to live in the presence of their Heavenly Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, having eternal increase for all the eternities to come

claim: Conference-closing sermon on peace, repentance, and forgiveness; 'exalted' appears only in the quoted Isaiah 2:2 imagery about the mountain of the Lord's house.
quote: the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills

claim: Quotes Joseph Fielding Smith that priesthood exists so we may receive exaltation and speaks of 'the gifts of exaltation' deepening the male-female partnership, but never specifies what those gifts are.
quote: The gifts of exaltation deepen the partnership of men and women as they commit to covenants and share the blessings of the temple.

claim: Young Women address on modern pioneers; exaltation appears once inside a quoted handbook phrase about temple blessings.
quote: make and keep sacred covenants, receive the ordinances of the temple, and enjoy the blessings of exaltation

claim: Brief conference-closing remarks; the Atonement is said to open the way to exaltation, with no further content.
quote: That act brought assurance of universal resurrection and opened the way to exaltation in our Father’s kingdom.

claim: Says temple ordinances qualify us for D&C 132:19's thrones and dominions, but stops short of the verse's increase language and adds no exposition.
quote: The supreme benefits of membership in the Church can be realized only through the exalting ordinances of the temple. These blessings qualify us for “thrones, kingdoms, principalities, and powers” in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Insists temple ordinances beyond baptism are required for exaltation and eternal life, but treats exaltation as an unanalyzed endpoint with no spirit-offspring, ancestry, or progression content.
quote: The Lord has decreed that the additional ordinances and covenants that I have mentioned must be received for exaltation and eternal life.

claim: Sermon on spiritual hunger and coming to Christ; exaltation is a bare closing promise, and the one immutability line sits inside a quoted George Q. Cannon passage about God never deserting us.
quote: Christ has overcome the world—our world—and His gift to us is peace now and exaltation in the world to come.

claim: Relief Society counsel on study, home, and service; no content on any axis.
On teaching by the Spirit; no content on any axis.
Defines six senses of salvation, the last being exaltation/eternal life, but says nothing specific about godhood, divine ancestry, or spirit offspring.
quote: Finally, in another usage familiar and unique to Latter-day Saints, the words *saved* and *salvation* are also used to denote exaltation or eternal life

claim: Says the fulness of the priesthood requires a wife at the man's side in the temple, gesturing at exaltation as a couple but with no claim about godhood or eternal increase.
quote: No man achieves the supernal exalting status of worthy fatherhood except as a gift from his wife.

claim: On pain, pondering, and repentance; no axis content.
Names exaltation only as the Relief Society's preparatory aim, with no claim about godhood, divine parentage, or eternal increase.
quote: I pray we will realize the vital role of our Relief Society organization, under the direction of and in harmony with the priesthood, in preparing women and families for exaltation.

claim: Names exaltation once as a fruit of the Atonement; otherwise a Christ-centered Easter message with no axis content.
quote: Our only chance to obtain redemption and exaltation.

claim: On technology, moral integrity, and the coming century; no axis content.
Eternal marriage keeps a family together beyond the veil and the temple provides exalting ordinances, but nothing is said about godhood, divine ancestry, or eternal increase.
quote: It will permit you to provide deceased ancestors the exalting ordinances you have received.

claim: Names exaltation as the goal of bringing families to the temple; no specific claim on any axis.
quote: How else will we or they receive exaltation or cope with the challenges that lie ahead?

claim: Church welfare program and self-reliance; no axis content.
Promises priesthood bearers glory, eternal life, exaltation, and 'even all He has', with JST Hebrews 7:3 that the ordained are made like unto the Son of God; bare theosis.
quote: He has promised us glory, eternal life, exaltation, even all He has, if we faithfully bear His priesthood and magnify all of our callings.

claim: Restates the standard literal spirit-daughter formula and affirms unmarried women may be exalted through sealing in the next life, but adds no claim about godhood, Heavenly Mother, or eternal increase.
quote: To be a daughter of God means that you are the offspring of Deity, literal descendants of a Divine Father, inheriting godly attributes and potential.

claim: Presents the Relief Society declaration, which affirms women are spirit daughters of God who strive for exaltation and have a divine destiny, but with no specific claim on any axis.
quote: Rejoice in the blessings of the temple, understand our divine destiny, and strive for exaltation.

claim: A single generic reference to walking the path to exaltation with new converts; otherwise a missionary-work message.
quote: And after their baptism, we need to walk the path to exaltation with them, steadying them until they have a solid foundation and testimony to carry them on through time and into life eternal.

claim: Speaks of women's exalting roles as wives and mothers and their divine destiny, but only as a call to honor womanhood, with no claim on any axis.
quote: He would focus their interests solely on their physical attributes and rob them of their exalting roles as wives and mothers.

claim: On adversity and finding peace in Christ; 'divine potential' and a D&C 121 quotation only, no axis content.
On baptismal covenants and the gift of the Holy Ghost; no axis content.
Priesthood duty and three 'lighthouse' principles; one bare use of the word exaltation, no axis content.

A wealthy-father parable of inheriting the fulness of the Father by becoming as He is, plus the line that exaltation is an eternal family experience; explicit theosis but nothing on godhood mechanics, ancestry, progression, or increase.
quote: Follow my example, mastering as I have mastered, and you will become as I am, and all that I have will be yours.

claim: Quotes the 1995 Proclamation's heavenly-parents language and says parenthood exalts a man or woman, but only in a chastity sermon with no axis-specific claim.
quote: You will not experience the combination of love and struggle, the pain and pleasure, the disappointment and sacrifice, that love which, blended together in parenthood, exalts a man or a woman and leads to that fulness of joy spoken of in the scriptures

claim: Defines eternal life as exaltation in the highest heaven and the kind of life God lives, but stops at that formula with no claim about godhood mechanics, ancestry, or increase.
quote: Eternal life is exaltation in the highest heaven—the kind of life that God lives.

claim: Recalls premortal life and names exaltation as becoming a glorified celestial being with one's own eternal family, but generically and with no axis-specific claim.
quote: You knew you could learn through personal experience the lessons that would bring happiness on earth—lessons that would eventually lead you to exaltation and eternal life as a glorified, celestial being in the presence of your Holy Father and His Beloved Son.

claim: On courage, modesty, language, and neighborliness; no axis content.

Argues exaltation is available only to a man and woman jointly, quoting Harold B. Lee that womanhood without priesthood or priesthood without womanhood does not spell exaltation, and that the fulness of the priesthood can be received only by a couple together.
quote: Pure womanhood plus priesthood means exaltation. But womanhood without priesthood, or priesthood without pure womanhood doesn’t spell exaltation.

claim: On the Atonement, forgiveness, and grace; 'exalted enough to stand before Him' is used non-technically, no axis content.
Priesthood duty and rescue stories; a single figurative reference to a 'journey to exaltation', no axis content.
Says the Church exists to exalt the family and quotes D&C 132:19 on inheriting thrones and exaltation, but with the 'continuation of the seeds' clause elided and no axis-specific claim.
quote: Our family is the focus of our greatest work and joy in this life; so will it be throughout all eternity, when we can “inherit thrones, kingdoms, principalities, … powers, dominions, … exaltation and glory.”

claim: Quotes Joseph Smith's ladder passage on learning the principles of exaltation step by step and continuing to learn long after death, but frames it only as encouragement to persevere.
quote: you must begin with the first, and go on until you learn all the principles of exaltation. But it will be a great while after you have passed through the veil before you will have learned them.

claim: Five principles drawn from Joseph Smith's history; only incidental phrases about ordinances of exaltation and divine potential.

Defines eternal life as living forever as families in God's presence and quotes D&C 132:22 on 'the exaltation and continuation of the lives', but offers no exposition of increase, godhood, or ancestry.
quote: Strait is the gate, and narrow the way that leadeth unto the exaltation and continuation of the lives, and few there be that find it, because ye receive me not in the world neither do ye know me.

claim: Describes eternal life as living forever in exalted spheres with loved ones; generic only.
quote: But eternal life means to live forever in exalted spheres in companionship with those we cherish, encompassed about by profound love, exquisite joy, and glory.

claim: On seeking and finding Christ; only an incidental phrase about His message of salvation and exaltation.
Distinguishes salvation from exaltation for wayward children claimed by sealing power, but treats exaltation only as a higher earned reward with no axis-specific content.
quote: Repentant wayward children will enjoy salvation and all the blessings that go with it, but exaltation is much more.

claim: On war, citizenship, and peace in Christ; only an incidental phrase about the exaltation of the obedient.
Names eternal increase and a continuation of lives as explicit promises to couples sealed in the temple, tying the marriage covenant to the fulness of God's glory and eternal lives.
quote: To those who keep the covenant of marriage, God promises the fulness of His glory, eternal lives, eternal increase, exaltation in the celestial kingdom, and a fulness of joy.

claim: Says the sealing authority binds families forever, making exaltations in the world to come possible; generic only.
quote: The sealing authority may bind a man, a woman, and their children together forever, making possible exaltations in the world to come—again, a blessing from the Savior.

claim: Quotes D&C 131 that the highest degree of celestial glory requires the new and everlasting covenant of marriage, and says a sealed wife increases a man's power and potential; generic.
quote: In order to obtain [it], a man must enter into this order of the priesthood [meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage]; And if he does not, he cannot obtain it.

claim: Quotes the Proclamation on spirit sons and daughters of heavenly parents and promises that those who miss marriage in mortality will not be denied blessings necessary for their exaltation, but adds nothing axis-specific.
quote: They can claim their inheritance as children of heavenly parents and, despite the tortured, agonizing test of mortal life, know that they are not lost.

claim: Insists God's fatherhood of human spirits is literal rather than allegorical and names exaltation as the added promise to the faithful, but makes no claim about godhood, ancestry, progression, or increase.
quote: He is not a father in some allegorical or poetic sense. He is literally the Father of our spirits.

claim: Maiden apostolic address on grace as enabling power; only an incidental Bible Dictionary phrase about laying hold on eternal life and exaltation.

Frames life as a three-act play (premortal, mortal, postmortal) and quotes Kimball listing godhood among the ends foreclosed by instant justice, plus Brigham Young on ordeals required for exaltation; all generic plan-of-salvation framing.
quote: There would also be an absence of joy, success, resurrection, eternal life, and godhood.

claim: Names qualifying for exaltation in the celestial kingdom as the goal of covenant keeping; generic only.
quote: In order to qualify for exaltation in the celestial kingdom, we must gain the trust of the Lord here on earth.

claim: Quotes Brigham Young that agency must be used to gain exaltation and states our goal is celestial glory; generic.
quote: All must use [this agency] in order to gain exaltation in [God’s] kingdom; inasmuch as [we] have the power of choice [we] must exercise that power.

claim: Affirms divine parentage and joint-heirship with Christ and speaks of progress toward exaltation; generic only.
quote: We are sons and daughters of the Eternal God, with the potential to be joint-heirs with Christ.

claim: Says God's work and glory can become ours and quotes D&C 132:19 on inheriting thrones, kingdoms, and exaltation, but with no elaboration touching increase, ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: Now is the time to align our goals with God’s goals. His work and His glory—“to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man”—can become ours.

claim: Closes by affirming literal divine spirit parentage of humans; otherwise a survey of prophetic last testimonies with no axis content.
quote: I know that our Heavenly Father is literally the Father of our spirits and that Jesus Christ is our Savior, our Redeemer, our Lord, and, as we obey His commandments, our friend

claim: Describes the Father and Son as separate, exalted, embodied beings and speaks of divine potential in each person, and notes Jesus inherited infinite life from an immortal Father, but makes no claim about God's own ancestry, progression, or increase.
quote: In vision, Joseph learned of God’s personal nature—that the Father and the Son are separate, exalted beings with bodies of flesh and bone.

claim: A sermon on forgiveness; only a closing phrase naming exaltation and eternal life as the Atonement's offer.
Teaches that embodiment makes us more like Heavenly Father and that we have the potential to become like Him, but this is bare theosis with no claim on any other axis.
quote: We are not less but *more* like Heavenly Father because we are embodied. I testify that we are His children, made in His image, with the potential to become like Him.

claim: Says a sealed couple are together promised power and exaltation (citing D&C 132:19-20) and that temple marriage enters the same order of the priesthood instituted with Adam; generic.
quote: The Lord has said that their covenant will be in force after this life, and together they are promised power and exaltation.

claim: Tells young women they are literally spirit daughters of Deity and 'offspring of exalted parents' (quoting McConkie), taught by heavenly parents in the premortal spirit world — an explicit plural-heavenly-parents assertion that also characterizes those parents as exalted.
quote: You have light because you are literally spirit daughters of Deity, “offspring of exalted parents” with a divine nature and an eternal destiny. You received your first lessons in the world of spirits from your heavenly parents.

claim: Approvingly relays a quorum president's answer that the worth of a soul is its capacity to become as God, alongside the D&C 84 oath-and-covenant promise that all the Father hath shall be given; striking but still bare theosis.
quote: The worth of a soul is its capacity to become as God.

claim: Says the plan offers eternal perpetuation of the family and that families may become as eternal as the kingdom of God itself, citing D&C 132:19-20, but without specifying increase or offspring.
quote: Marriage was intended by the Lord to endure beyond physical death. His plan offers eternal perpetuation of the family in the kingdom of God.

claim: On suffering as a way to know the Savior; joint-heirship quoted from Romans 8 only, no axis content.
Ensign Peak sermon on stakes as defense and refuge; 'exaltation' appears twice only as the destination the ordinances make available.
quote: A stake is self-contained with all that is needed for the salvation and exaltation of those who would come within its influence, and temples are ever closer.

claim: Standard plan-of-salvation recital: we lived as spirit children of Heavenly Father and mortality prepares us to 'become more like Him' — premortal spirit birth and theosis stated only generically, with no claim about new spirit children, God's own origin, or His progression.
quote: God is the Father of our spirits. We are literally His children, and He loves us. We lived as spirit children of our Father in Heaven before we were born on this earth.

claim: Exaltation appears only as the reward the Atonement makes available; no content on divine ancestry, divine progression, or eternal increase.
quote: It opens the gates to exaltation for all who qualify for forgiveness through repentance and obedience.

claim: Virtue framed as a prerequisite for exaltation and for young women's 'potential as daughters of God'; bare theosis with no axis-specific claim.
quote: It is clear that virtue is a requirement for exaltation.

claim: Priesthood-session sermon on personal cleanliness built around Joseph F. Smith's Hawaii dream; the only near-miss is a passing reference to seeing people 'among the exalted' in the dream.
quote: My mother was there, and she sat with a child in her lap; and I could name over as many as I remember of their names, who sat there, who seemed to be among the chosen, among the exalted.

claim: Quotes the Young Women theme's 'blessings of exaltation' and closes on assisting 'in the exaltation of your eternal family'; generic exaltation-of-families language only.
quote: The Lord is depending on you to assist in the exaltation of your eternal family.

claim: Gospel-basics and endure-to-the-end sermon; 'exalting' is used adjectivally of enduring, with no doctrinal claim on any axis.
quote: Viewed from this perspective, enduring to the end is exalting and glorious, not grim and gloomy.

claim: Eyring ties the oath and covenant of the priesthood to gaining 'the fulness of His glory,' living 'as He lives,' and 'the promise of eternal increase,' then quotes Parley P. Pratt at length that the endless union of husband and wife yields offspring as numerous as the stars — post-mortal procreation stated, not merely eternal companionship.
quote: It was from him that I learned that we might cultivate these affections, and grow and increase in the same to all eternity; while the result of our endless union would be an offspring as numerous as the stars of heaven, or the sands of the sea shore.

claim: A whole talk defining exaltation, but the definition is confined to 'the highest state of happiness and glory in the celestial realm' and families sealed forever 'as exalted beings' — deification, eternal increase, divine ancestry, and Heavenly Mother are all absent; worth flagging as a datum for the softening axis, but Nelson never reframes an earlier teaching explicitly.
quote: To be exalted—or to gain exaltation—refers to the highest state of happiness and glory in the celestial realm.
