claim: Talk on prayer; quotes the King Follett Discourse's opening line about knowing God's character and conversing with Him as one man with another, then draws only the generic inference that we are literal spirit children — the once-a-man sequel is not invoked.
quote: With the knowledge that we can converse with God as one man converses with another, we also understand that we not only have a divine spark within us, but that we are actually spirit children of our Father in heaven.

claim: Kimball reuses his vine-and-branches image (as in his 1857 chain sermon) but runs it only forward: Christ 'sprang from his Father' and was trained by Him, and disciples partake of the Father's attributes through Christ — no backward chain of Gods is drawn here.
quote: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman:” that is, he sprang from his Father, and was trained and nursed by him.

claim: Fast-day discourse on the original purity of the human spirit entering its tabernacle; the striking phrase 'spirit begets spirit—likeness, likeness' is NOT a spirit-birth statement here — in context it is a proverb about the social contagion of moods, paired with 'feelings beget their likeness; and custom, custom.' Flagging this as a conflation trap, since the 1859 conference minutes file quotes the fragment stripped of that context.
quote: Let that be the determination of every individual, for spirit begets spirit—likeness, likeness; feelings beget their likeness; and custom, custom.

claim: Article-of-Faith-13 talk on seeking the good; asserts spirit childhood and divine potential in one summary sentence and quotes Nibley that the temple extends to other worlds.
quote: As spirit children of our Heavenly Father, we should seek always to recognize the divine potential within us and never restrict our perspective to the limited scope of mortal life.

claim: The original of the procreation argument Packer reuses in 2010: the power to beget life is denied to Satan and is the ground of our differing from all other creation as offspring of God — specific about mortal procreation, silent on eternal increase or divine ancestry.
quote: The adversary is jealous toward all who have the power to beget life. He cannot beget life; he is impotent.

claim: Bare assertion that humans are the literal spirit offspring of God the Father, with no development of parenthood, mechanism, or regress.
quote: We are the literal spirit offspring of God the Father.

claim: Sermon on avoiding verbal 'bashing' and cultivating charity; no theology-proper content.
Generic reference to premortal existence as spirit children; no claim about divine parenthood, progression, or regress.
quote: In view of our existence as spirit children before we came to earth and immortality in the life hereafter, this earth life is indeed but a very short moment.

claim: Three-step self-improvement parable (repent now, choose priorities, choose the right); no axis content.
On being spiritually whole in Christ while awaiting physical healing; no theology-proper or exaltation-mechanics content.
Quotes D&C 76:22-24 (worlds created by Christ, inhabitants 'begotten sons and daughters unto God') as a closing testimony, without developing plurality of worlds or divine parentage.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Media-and-family warning; refers generically to children as 'God's spirit children' and to parenthood as an eternal calling, without asserting postmortal spirit offspring.
quote: Father and mother are callings from which we will never be released, and there is no more important stewardship than the responsibility we have for God's spirit children who come into our families.

claim: In the 2017 general women's session Jones quotes Spencer W. Kimball naming a Mother in Heaven alongside the Father and framing the gospel plan as aimed at 'eternal progression and the possibility of godhood' — a heavenly-parents-plus-deification statement delivered as current teaching (note: the load-bearing sentences are a Kimball 1978 quotation, not Jones's own formulation).
quote: God is your Father. He loves you. He and your Mother in heaven value you beyond any measure. … Let there be no question in your mind about your value as an individual. The whole intent of the gospel plan is to provide an opportunity for each of you to reach your fullest potential, which is eternal progression and the possibility of godhood.

claim: Report on area conferences in Asia and a lesson on giving; no axis content.

Standard statement that the Father is the literal parent of Christ and of His other spirit children, plus Christ's creation of 'worlds without number'; no postmortal parenthood, mechanism, or regress.
quote: God the Eternal Father is the literal parent of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and of His other spirit children.

claim: Bare theosis plus literal spirit sonship: we are God's literal spirit children and will inherit 'everything your Father has'; no new spirit children, mechanism, or regress.
quote: And in the process, as you “lose [your] life” in the service of others, you will grow and develop until you reach “the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.” Then you will be prepared to inherit, with Christ, everything your Father has.

claim: Christ-centered Easter-style sermon on why Latter-day Saints do not use the cross; quotes D&C 76:22-24 without developing plurality of worlds or divine parentage.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Premortal spirit childhood and literal divine fatherhood plus generic 'become like Him' theosis, framed around family history work; families called the basic unit of the eternal realms but no postmortal spirit offspring asserted.
quote: God is the literal Father of all mankind; we are each part of His eternal family. Because He loves us with the love of a perfect Father, He wants us to progress and advance and become like Him.

claim: Counsel on family happiness; generic references to God's spirit children and premortal instruction in the spirit world.
quote: We know that Heavenly Father has spirit children in this world who sometimes choose sin and great unhappiness.

claim: Easter/Joseph Smith sesquicentennial address; closes with D&C 76:22-24 but develops nothing about worlds, divine parentage, or progression.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Counsel to those newly called to Church service; only generic references to those served as the Father's spirit children.
quote: His work is to bless His Father's spirit children with the opportunity to choose eternal life.

claim: Ballard asserts that procreative power, like priesthood power, is shared eternally by husband and wife, and that sealed families dwell with 'our heavenly parents' while participating in the forever-expanding light and glory of God and Christ — an eternal-procreation plus expanding-divine-glory claim made in 2013 general conference.
quote: And the primary purpose of this priesthood power is to bless, sanctify, and purify us so we can live together with our families in the presence of our heavenly parents, bound by priesthood sealings, participating in the marvelous work of God and Jesus Christ in forever expanding *Their* light and glory.

claim: Thirtieth-anniversary apostolic defense of the family proclamation: Rasband repeats its 'beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents' clause as current teaching and explicitly refuses calls to revise or retire the document, calling it doctrine — a 2025 re-entrenchment (not softening) of heavenly-parents language (the clause itself is quoted from proclamation-1995).
quote: Some suggest the Church pull it back, revise, or even set the proclamation aside. The proclamation on the family is, as President Hinckley stated, doctrine, my dear brothers and sisters.

claim: Sao Paulo Temple travelogue; generic language about endless development and reaching one's highest potential through temple ordinances, with no exaltation mechanics.
quote: In addition, worthy members will receive the ordinances relating to mankind's eternal journey and to the endless potential and development of each human soul.

claim: Catechetical list of what the scriptures say about Christ; includes premortal spirit childhood and bare theosis ('progress and be like him'), with Christ explicitly a son of the Father but no regress.
quote: He taught us the physical characteristics of a resurrected being and told us that we could follow his example and that we would be able to progress and be like him.

claim: Argues Mormonism's vitality is theological, not programmatic; states the parental-likeness argument for deification and distinguishes Christ as a God who is a son of the Father, not His own Father — but asserts no regress or postmortal spirit offspring.
quote: In other words, those who know that God is our Father know that we are begotten sons and daughters made eternally in his image, and also know that because he is our Father, we not only call him Father but we expect him to help us to become as he is, realizing that children become like their parents.

claim: Bare, one-sentence assertion of premortal spirit childhood to 'heavenly parents'; no development of maternal deity, mechanism, or regress.
quote: We know that we are spirit children of heavenly parents, here on earth to receive our mortal bodies and to be tested.

claim: Premortal spirit childhood and progression toward the celestial kingdom, but the destiny is described only as 'the kind of life of those who reside in that celestial glory' — no godhood, parenthood, or regress language.
quote: Our Heavenly Father desires all of His children to return to the celestial kingdom, where God and our Savior reside, and to have the kind of life of those who reside in that celestial glory.

claim: Sermon on humble service; a single generic reference to hearers as spirit children of Heavenly Father.
quote: We are also to understand and remember that we too, like the lad in the New Testament account, are the spirit children of our Heavenly Father and that Jesus is the Christ, our Savior, and the Redeemer of the world.

claim: Armor-of-God priesthood address; quotes the oath and covenant ('all that my Father hath shall be given unto him') and calls hearers God's spirit children, without unpacking either.
quote: Brethren, we are greatly blessed to know that God lives and we are his spirit children; that his son, Jesus Christ, gave his life so that we might be resurrected and enjoy eternal life.

claim: American Bicentennial patriotic address on the divine preparation of America for the Restoration; no theology-proper content.

Abortion/sanctity-of-life address; quotes Oaks that all God's spirit children must come to earth and that individual identity predates conception, and the proclamation on 'sacred powers of procreation,' but develops no exaltation mechanics.
quote: Our attitude toward abortion is not based on revealed knowledge of when mortal life begins. … It is fixed by our knowledge that … all of the spirit children of God must come to this earth for a glorious purpose, and that individual identity began long before conception and will continue for all the eternities to come.

claim: Five-point missionary 'success formula' talk; no theology-proper or exaltation content.

Maxwell names as one of the Restoration's three 'stunners' that man was in the beginning with God — personal identity uncreated and eternal, explicitly set against creation ex nihilo — alongside a cosmos of 'worlds without number' whose inhabitants are begotten sons and daughters of God; a compact 2003 apostolic statement of the eternal-man metaphysics that underwrites the regress question, though it stops short of asserting regress itself.
quote: Revelations likewise came about our longevity as God's spirit children, since “man was also in the beginning with God”—a declaration accompanied by even further glimmers about man's eternal nature (D&C 93:29). These enunciations with their profound implications are major—challenging, for instance, the teaching that man was created in an instant “out of nothing.”

claim: Closing conference exhortation to member missionary work and family effort; recites D&C 76:22-24 with no development.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Address on moral agency and the Final Judgment; states the plan's purpose for God's spirit children is to gain bodies and 'progress eternally,' without specifying the terminus.
quote: The overarching purposes of the Father's plan are to provide His spirit children with opportunities to receive a physical body, learn “good from evil” through mortal experience, grow spiritually, and progress eternally.

claim: On calamities, adversity, and temporal/spiritual preparedness; no axis content.
Address to converts on temple and family history work; generic references to Heavenly Father's spirit children and to living 'in glory in families forever,' with no exaltation mechanics.
quote: We promise to obey His commandments. And He promises us, if we are faithful, that we may live with Him in glory in families forever in the world to come.

claim: Exposition of faith in Christ as first principle; recites Abraham 3:22-28 on the organized intelligences and premortal council and speaks of going 'on in eternal progress to perfection,' but develops neither the staging nor the terminus.
quote: It provided for them to receive physical bodies in a mortal experience where, endowed with free agency and being acted upon by good and evil, they would prove themselves worthy or unworthy to return to the society of God and go on in eternal progress to perfection.

claim: Plea to protect children from abuse, neglect, and out-of-wedlock birth; only the honorific 'sons and daughters of God,' no axis content.
Easter sermon on literal resurrection; asserts premortal existence as spirit children of the Father and recites D&C 76:22-24, without developing worlds, parenthood, or godhood.
quote: The restored gospel of Jesus Christ explains that we existed as spirit entities before being born into this sphere of activity—yes, spirit children of our Father in heaven.

claim: Chains together D&C 131:7 (spirit is matter), Abraham 3 (organized intelligences), and D&C 76:24 with Romney's own bracketed gloss extending begotten divine sonship to the inhabitants of all worlds — suggestive of plurality-of-worlds spirit parentage, but asserted only by interpolation into the scriptural text, with no postmortal parenthood or regress.
quote: Man himself is naturally spiritual. His spirit is a child of God. The spirits of “the inhabitants [of all worlds] are begotten sons and daughters unto God” (D&C 76:24).

claim: Apostolic acceptance testimony reprising his 1979 catechetical list; premortal spirit childhood plus bare 'progress and be like him' theosis.
quote: He taught us the physical characteristics of a resurrected being and told us that we could follow his example and that we would be able to progress and be like him.

claim: Conference remarks on Utah economics, debt, the sugar works, home industry, and the patience of Joseph in Egypt and Job; no theology-proper or exaltation content whatever.

Short testimony on prayer and God's reality; calls mothers 'co-partner with God' in bringing a spirit child into mortality and asks whether we know we are spirit children of God, without developing either.
quote: I am sure that my mother, being the kind of woman she was, thanked God when I was born for the blessing of being a co-partner with God in bringing this spirit child into the mortal world.

claim: Church-growth and gift-of-faith address including a radio message and a recitation of the Articles of Faith; insists God is a personal individuality rather than diffuse law, and quotes D&C 76:22-24, but asserts nothing about divine progression, parentage, or regress.
quote: When we say that we believe in God we mean that we believe in him as an individuality, as actually the Father of Jesus Christ— not a congeries of laws floating through the universe without form and void, but we believe him to be the Father of Jesus Christ.

claim: Priesthood-session charge to treat women as equals; a single generic reference to women as spirit children of Heavenly Father, no maternal deity or exaltation mechanics.
quote: Our wives, mothers, daughters, sisters, and friends are all the spirit children of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Sermon on love as the defining discipleship attribute; one bare 'heavenly parents' clause plus the standard promise of progressing in knowledge and glory and receiving all God has.
quote: He offers to His children the promise of a glorious and infinite existence and has provided a way for us to progress in knowledge and glory until we receive a fulness of joy. He has promised us all that He has.

claim: General women's meeting address; presses that righteous women equally will receive all the Father has, and calls bearing and rearing God's spirit children an eternal assignment — but the parenthood in view is mortal, and the deification claim is bare D&C 84 theosis.
quote: Sometimes to be tested and proved requires that we be temporarily deprived—but righteous women and men will one day receive *all*—think of it, sisters—*all* that our Father has!

claim: Obedience-and-duty sermon (tithing, quorum attendance, Nephi's example); quotes D&C 76:20-24 only to make a point about Sidney Rigdon's later apostasy.
quote: That by Him and through Him, and of Him the worlds are and were created and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God

claim: Address on moral decline and parental responsibility; only the bare honorific that a child is also a child of Heavenly Father.

Cannon publicly reframes the Nauvoo-era law of adoption on the day Woodruff announced the 1894 revelation: he names the old practice of men having others adopted to them in order to build up kingdoms and glory to themselves, says he has feared it ever since, and redirects the sealing chain to strict lineal descent back to Adam and to Joseph Smith as dispensation head — a documented retraction of dynastic kingdom-building, though the chain in view is one of generations, not of Gods.
quote: I well remember myself in my boyhood days that which President Woodruff has referred to—the spirit that was manifested by many at the dedication of the temple in Nauvoo when the ordinances were administered there. some men thought to build up kingdoms to themselves; and they appeared to think that by inducing men and women to be adopted into their families they were adding to their own glory. From that day until the present, I have never thought of this subject of adoption without having a certain amount of fear concerning it.

claim: Practical parenting counsel (start early, communicate, discipline with love); only a bare 'we lived before we came here' in a quoted testimony list.

Preaching chastity in April 1929 general conference, Melvin J. Ballard states the reward of temple marriage in D&C 132 terms — the worthy pass by the angels and the Gods to their glory and inheritance and 'attain unto the power of endless increase' — and grounds the duty to bear children in a premortal promise made to the Father's waiting spirit children; same speaker and doctrine as the dataset's ballard-increase (1922-09-22) but a distinct, later, official-conference instance.
quote: When you contrast that condition with the glorious privilege God has offered to the sons and daughters of Zion who keep themselves clean and pure and undefiled, to go into the temples of God to receive a companion for time and eternity, that they may be worthy to pass on by the angels and the Gods, to their glory and inheritance and attain unto the power of endless increase, is it not inducement enough to call for sacrifices, for cleanliness of life, for purity, so that we may reap these glorious blessings and holy privileges?

claim: History of Bible translation, the Book of Mormon as a parallel record, and Moroni's promise; no theology-proper content beyond 'Our Father in heaven.'
Primary-presidency address on teaching respect and reverence; only the bare 'child of God' honorific.
Spiritual-preparedness address; premortal spirit childhood plus the Father's premortal promise to 'give us all that He had,' left undeveloped.
quote: We are the spirit children of a Heavenly Father. He loved us and He taught us before we were born into this world. He told us that He wished to give us all that He had.

claim: Narrative of the premortal council through the Restoration; recites Abraham 3:24-26 with bracketed glosses and refers to the Father's 'vast creations,' but the promised terminus is only celestial glory in the Father's presence, with no godhood, parenthood, or regress.
quote: Our benevolent Father came from His vast creations to this earth to clarify truth, to disperse the intense clouds of spiritual darkness, to establish His true identity, to restore a fulness of truth, and to provide the only way to obtain secure, spiritual guidance.

claim: On core doctrine over programs; grounds the capacity for Christlike attributes in our being spirit children of God — bare theosis, no exaltation mechanics.
quote: As spirit children of our Heavenly Father, we do have the potential to incorporate Christlike attributes into our life and character.

claim: Address on accountability and stewardship; frames chastity as protecting the means by which God's spirit children come to earth, without developing eternal procreation.
quote: A loving Father in Heaven has provided us with the means to bring His spirit children into this world to fulfill the full measure of their creation.

claim: Relief Society address on service and conversion; touches divine parentage only in the vocative sense of women as daughters of God and premortal assignments, with no claim about becoming gods, heavenly parenthood, or God's own nature.
quote: Our privilege and our responsibility as daughters of God and as sisters of Relief Society, then, is to become the most effective instruments *we* can be.

claim: Church President Kimball affirms a Heavenly Mother by name, endorsing 'O My Father' as a doctrinal hymn and describing her queenly character and continuing influence on her children.
quote: Finally, when we sing that doctrinal hymn and anthem of affection, “O My Father,” we get a sense of the ultimate in maternal modesty, of the restrained, queenly elegance of our Heavenly Mother, and knowing how profoundly our mortal mothers have shaped us here, do we suppose her influence on us as individuals to be less if we live so as to return there?

claim: Caussé frames mortal parenthood as cocreation with God in providing bodies for His spirit children and promises faithful stewards 'additional creative power in the life to come,' but never specifies new spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or God's own progression.
quote: There is no stewardship more sacred, more fulfilling, and also more demanding than that of partnering with our Creator in providing physical bodies for His spirit children and then helping them reach their divine potential.

claim: Nelson closes by quoting D&C 132:19 to faithful sealed couples, promising thrones and a continuation of the seeds forever, but adds no elaboration on spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: To those couples who bear and share that priesthood worthily and remain faithful to the law of the everlasting covenant of eternal marriage, enduring the congested years and trials of diapers and dishes, crowded kitchen and thin pocketbook, service in the Church, education and the burning of the midnight oil, the Lord makes this promise: “Ye shall come forth in the first resurrection; … and shall inherit thrones, kingdoms, principalities, and *powers,* dominions, … [and there] shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.”

claim: Standard eternal-marriage sermon: sealed families endure forever and lead to an 'eternal stewardship like that of God himself,' but no new-spirit-children, mechanism, ancestry, or divine-progression claim.
quote: His way of everlasting marriage is filled with hope and promise, and is designed to lead to happiness here and to an eternal stewardship like that of God himself.

claim: Talk on certitude and testimony; the only axis-adjacent content is the generic universal-fatherhood claim that all people are sons and daughters of God, with no exaltation, ancestry, or divine-progression content.
quote: They are all sons and daughters of God.

claim: Quotes Kimball on mothers 'giving birth to and rearing the spirit children of our Father in Heaven' — generic premortal spirit-parenthood language about mortal childbearing, with no claim about new spirit children, mechanism, or divine ancestry.
quote: Do not, however, make the mistake of being drawn off into secondary tasks which will cause the neglect of your eternal assignments such as giving birth to and rearing the spirit children of our Father in Heaven.

claim: A missionary-style plea to inactive members about preparing for the Second Coming and the 'long hereafter'; no godhood, ancestry, spirit-birth, or divine-progression content.
A Word of Wisdom talk to youth about health, obedience, and the Passover symbolism of the Atonement; no content on any axis.
Parenting/media-pollution talk whose only axis contact is a boilerplate closing line that we are God's spirit children.
quote: We are his spirit children, and he loves his family.

claim: Youth exhortation that asserts bare theosis (obedient youth may become gods and goddesses, kings and queens) plus premortal valiance, but with no mechanism, no spirit offspring, and nothing about God's own past or progression.
quote: Scriptures, more than anything else, will assist you to overcome the world and enable you to become gods and goddesses, kings and queens in the celestial world.

claim: Generic 'we are spirit children of God / He is the Father of our spirit' identity exhortation with no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit-birth mechanism.
quote: We say, “We believe in God, the Eternal Father.” Do we really believe that he is the Father of our spirit, and act accordingly?

claim: Tanner argues for knowing God's character against the creeds (three separate personages, a personal God, premortal existence, humans as God's spirit children) but makes no claim about God's own origin, progression, ancestry, or post-mortal spirit offspring.
quote: As a special witness for Christ, I bear my solemn testimony that God lives; that we are his spirit children; that Jesus Christ is his Only Begotten Son in the flesh, and is the Savior of us all.

claim: A discourse on prayer that rests on the generic premises that God is our Father, that we are his spirit children, and that we had a premortal existence, with no claim about divine ancestry, divine progression, or heavenly parenthood.
quote: I pray that those who doubt might be helped to see and understand that God is our Father, that we are his spirit children, and that he is really there

claim: Entirely a sermon on honesty (13th Article of Faith), debt, promises, and public integrity; no theosis, ancestry, progression, or spirit-parenthood content whatsoever.

Covenant/heritage talk that speaks generically of humans as Heavenly Father's spirit children and of eternal life in eternal families, with no claim about becoming gods, heavenly parenthood, or God's own nature or past.
quote: We can depend on that unfailing desire of the Savior to bring all of Heavenly Father's spirit children back to their home with Him.

claim: Packer defends Godhood as mankind's destiny by arguing from literal 'after their own kind' parentage that God's offspring are not a different species than He is, affirms that anyone teaching Father/Son/Holy Ghost teaches a plurality of Gods, and then explicitly caps the hierarchy: the Father is the one true God whom no one will ever surpass or replace.
quote: The Father *is* the one true God. *This* thing is certain: no one will ever ascend above Him; no one will ever replace Him.

claim: An address entirely on Sabbath observance and the Lord's day; contains no theosis, ancestry, spirit-birth, or divine-progression content.

Joseph Fielding Smith teaches that the faithful will become gods and go on to a fullness and continuation of the seeds forever, with the prospect of building worlds and peopling them — a forward-chain claim beyond bare theosis.
quote: We are in school, the mortal school, to gain the experiences, the training, the joys, and the sufferings that we partake of, that we might be educated in all these things and be prepared, if we are faithful and true to the commandments of the Lord, to become sons and daughters of God, joint heirs with Jesus Christ; and in his presence to go on to a fullness and a continuation of the seeds forever, and perhaps through our faithfulness to have the opportunity of building worlds and peopling them.

claim: Parliament-of-World's-Religions overview of LDS belief: premortal spirit childhood and 'heir to all that He has' potential stated generically, with no ancestry, regress, divine progression, or generative-exaltation claim.
quote: These scriptures teach that all of us lived as spirit children of God before we came into this life.

claim: Sermon on the everlasting covenant that glosses never-ending celestial glory as 'the power of eternal increase' and calls Christ 'the First Born in the spirit,' but names no spirit offspring, no mechanism, no couples, and nothing about God's own origin or progression.
quote: This means a never ending glory in the Celestial Kingdom— the power of eternal increase — to become the sons and daughters of God, and heirs of God, even joint heirs with Jesus Christ, and with him to inherit all things that the Father hath.

claim: Uses spirit-birth and plural 'heavenly parents' language about our own premortal origin ('a living spirit born to our loving, eternal heavenly parents'), but asserts no mechanism, no new spirit children, no Heavenly Mother by name, and nothing about God's ancestry or progression.
quote: Just think of it! Within every human body dwells a living spirit born to our loving, eternal heavenly parents.

claim: Coleman states the standard premortal-parentage formula ('literal spirit offspring') and premortal schooling, but asserts nothing about new spirit children after this life, God's ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: The scriptures testify that we are the children of God, His literal spirit offspring.

claim: A jeremiad on America's moral decline and the need to return to Christ; no content on any axis.

Welfare-administration talk that opens with a D&C 132:19 'continuation of the seeds forever and ever' preamble plus a body/intelligence/spirit indestructibility line, but never specifies new spirit children, a mechanism, ancestry, or divine progression (borderline B1).
quote: Man and woman have the possibility of a “continuation of the seeds forever and ever” and will never have an end (see D&C 132:19).

claim: Easter resurrection sermon; the sole axis contact is a block quotation of D&C 76:22-24 in which the inhabitants of the worlds 'are begotten sons and daughters unto God,' with no comment on exaltation, heavenly parenthood, or God's nature.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God

claim: Sermon on love of God and neighbor, missionary work, and the Atonement; no content on any axis.

Ballard's missionary-preparation address invokes the fatherhood of God and premortal spirit childhood only as a conversational entry point, with no claim about divine ancestry, spirit-birth mechanism, or divine progression.
quote: Our understanding and knowledge of this basic truth should compel us to love all of God’s children as our brothers and sisters and to explain to them that we all lived premortally as spirit children of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Wells argues at length that we were literally born of God in the spirit before this earth and may be given power to become sons and daughters of God in body and spirit, but asserts no mechanism, no Heavenly Mother, no divine ancestry, and no forward chain of new spirit children.
quote: Here we have it plainly stated that they were not born and begotten of God in the flesh, not by the will of man, but of God, clearly pointing to the fact that we were the children of God born of him in the spirit before the foundations of this earth were laid.

claim: Teaching-children-to-pray talk; premortal spirit childhood and family reunion asserted only in the generic devotional register, with no ancestry, progression, or generative-exaltation content.
quote: When we teach those we love that we are spirit children temporarily away from a loving Heavenly Father, we open the door of prayer to them.

claim: Maxwell closes by affirming a Heavenly Mother as an active participant preparing the heavenly homecoming, and earlier states that God entrusts mortal women with bearing His spirit children.
quote: Could such a regal homecoming be possible without the anticipatory arrangements of a Heavenly Mother?

claim: Mission-travel report and good-vs-evil sermon that touches premortal existence and a generic 'spark of divinity / we inherit divine attributes' theosis theme, plus a bare D&C 76:24 quotation about worlds whose inhabitants are begotten sons and daughters unto God; no claim about divine ancestry, God's progression, or spirit-birth mechanism.
quote: Every one of us inherits something of the characteristics of our earthly parents. At the same time we inherit something of the divine attributes.

claim: Ellsworth asserts a Heavenly Mother as revealed doctrine ('associated with our Father in Heaven we have a Mother there'), grounds it in 'O My Father,' and then endorses Ella Wheeler Wilcox's poem — retitled by him 'Eternal Motherhood' — whose speaker claims post-mortal 'spirit children who will claim me here' waiting in 'God's great nursery,' as being 'in harmony with the idea of our having a mother in heaven.'
quote: It has also been revealed and taught to the Latter-day Saints that, associated with our Father in Heaven we have a Mother there.

claim: A Relief Society address on charity, kindness, and the goodness of the women of the Church; no content on any axis.

Plan-of-salvation overview: premortal 'second estate,' bare spirit-childhood rhetorical question, and the 'even as I am' invitation, all generic; no ancestry, regress, divine progression, or generative-exaltation claim.
quote: This should not surprise us. After all, whose spirit children are we? (See Heb. 12:9.)

claim: Sermon on agency, unrighteous dominion, and the speaker's own weakness; it treats deification only as a slow personal prospect ('I do not expect to become a god, right away'), a gradualist statement of bare theosis with no claim about God's origin, ancestry, or heavenly parenthood.
quote: I do not expect to become a god, right away.

claim: Instruction on worthiness interviews; the only axis-adjacent content is a single bare reference to members as spirit children of God.
quote: It is important that those we interview realize that they are spirit children of God and that we love them, and let them know that we love them and are interested in their welfare and in helping them succeed in life.

claim: Ballard's parenting address uses generic premortal spirit-childhood and 'glorious destiny' language, with no claim about new spirit offspring, divine ancestry, or God's progression.
quote: Every human being is a spirit child of God and lived with Heavenly Father before coming to earth.

claim: Hunter presses the universal fatherhood of God — a divine pedigree and common genealogy leading back to God, quoting the 1978 First Presidency on all people as literal spirit children of an Eternal Father — but the chain runs only up to God, with nothing on God's own ancestry, progression, or heavenly parenthood by exalted couples.
quote: All men and women have not only a physical lineage leading back to Adam and Eve, their first earthly parents, but also a spiritual heritage leading back to God the Eternal Father.

claim: Sermon on love and kindness whose only axis contact is the standard universal-siblinghood premise that we are all spirit children of Heavenly Father.
quote: We are all spirit children of our Heavenly Father and, as such, are brothers and sisters.

claim: Talk on drug addiction and agency; the only axis content is generic - humans were spirit children of the Creator before the world and are invited to become more like Him - with no exaltation mechanism, offspring, or claim about God Himself.
quote: He loves you and wants you to be happy. He wants you to grow through life's choices and become more like Him.

claim: Packer labels as doctrinal 'Truth' that we are spirit children of a Father God whose premortal existence could not have had a beginning — a specific apostolic claim on the origin-of-spirits question that bounds any account of spirit birth as an absolute beginning.
quote: Truth: We are spirit children of a Father God. We lived with him in our premortal existence, of which it must be said that there was not, neither could there have been, a beginning.

claim: An address on the Aaronic Priesthood as preparation and on mentoring young men; the only heaven-related language is generic 'children of God' and eternal families, with no axis content.
An address on delinquency, parental authority, working mothers, and family budgeting; no content on any axis.

Atonement/agency/Fall sermon; premortal spirit childhood and man's body made 'in the image of God in a separate creation' stated generically, with no ancestry, regress, divine progression, or generative-exaltation claim.
quote: The plan provided that each spirit child of God would receive a mortal body and each would be tested.

claim: Talk on worthiness and self-judgment that quotes Joseph Fielding Smith on perfection requiring ages and continued progress beyond the grave until the faithful 'shall be like God' - bare theosis about human progression, with nothing about God's own progression, ancestry, or heavenly parenthood.
quote: I believe the Lord meant just what he said: that we should be perfect, as our Father in heaven is perfect. That will not come all at once, but line upon line, and precept upon precept, example upon example, and even then not as long as we live in this mortal life, for we will have to go even beyond the grave before we reach that perfection and shall be like God.

claim: Easter resurrection sermon; the only axis-adjacent content is the standard designation of Christ as the Father's Firstborn of spirit children, with no mechanism, ancestry, or progression claim.
quote: We have a Father in Heaven, who sent his Firstborn of spirit children, his Only Begotten in the flesh, to be an earthly example for us, to take upon himself the sins of the world, and subsequently to be crucified for the sins of the world and be resurrected.

claim: Grant's remarks answer New Era attacks on Church banking and post-Manifesto plural marriage; the only axis-adjacent material is an unglossed recitation of D&C 76's 'begotten sons and daughters unto God,' quoted solely as a testimony of Christ.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: A priesthood-session talk on controlling anger and avoiding grudges and divorce; no content on any axis.

Resurrection talk that recites the Family Proclamation's 'spirit children of heavenly parents' formula once and otherwise concerns spirit/body reunion; no Heavenly Mother named, no mechanism, no ancestry or progression claim.
quote: We are spirit children of heavenly parents.

claim: Sermon on gaining and keeping a testimony via the parable of the sower; contains no content on any axis - no theosis, no exaltation, no divine parenthood, nothing about God's nature or origin.

Priesthood-leadership sermon with an 'Eternal Progression' section that argues 'like begets like' from divine childhood to human divine attributes and cites only the forward half of the Snow couplet ('as God now is man may become'); bare theosis, with the 'As man now is, God once was' half conspicuously omitted and no claim about God's ancestry or ongoing progression.
quote: And a characteristic teaching of the Church is that "as God now is man may become" -- a statement in poetic language of our magnificent doctrine of eternal progression.

claim: Petersen marshals Columbus, Washington, Lincoln, Book of Mormon traditions, and Joseph Smith's visions solely to prove that God lives and Jesus is the Christ; the only axis-adjacent line is an unglossed quotation of D&C 76:22-24 about inhabitants of worlds being 'begotten sons and daughters unto God.'
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were cre ated, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Condie lists gospel promises, including becoming partakers of the divine nature and, for the temple-sealed, God's glory as a fulness and continuation of the seeds forever, but never specifies spirit offspring, mechanism, divine ancestry, or divine progression.
quote: Those who are sealed in holy temples and who faithfully keep their covenants will receive God’s glory, which “shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever”

claim: Practical talk on four types of family council; the premortal 'heavenly parents / their spirit children' line is the standard Proclamation formula used as an analogy, with no Heavenly Mother asserted, no new-spirit-children claim, and no regress.
quote: We belonged to a family council in the premortal existence, when we lived with our heavenly parents as their spirit children.

claim: Leadership-development talk that mentions in passing that we are spirit children of God the Eternal Father; no claim about God's own nature, ancestry, or progression.
quote: Let us develop faith in ourselves; we are spirit children of God the Eternal Father, and as we magnify our callings, by doing our part, God will make us equal to every task.

claim: Youth talk asserting literal spirit parentage of God ('the pedigree of your spirit can be written on a single line') but nothing about God's own ancestry, progression, or new spirit children.
quote: You are a child of God. He is the father of your spirit. Spiritually you are of noble birth, the offspring of the King of Heaven.

claim: Counsel to parents of wayward children; refers generically to God's spirit children and to God having 'lost' some of them, with no doctrinal claim on any axis.
quote: Our Father in Heaven has also lost many of his spirit children to the world; he knows the feelings of your heart.

claim: Priesthood-session encouragement talk; generic premortal spirit-children framing plus an Abraham 3 quotation, no specific axis claim.
quote: All of us, before the period known as mortality, lived as spirit children of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Eulogistic remarks on George Albert Smith and George F. Richards and on love among the Twelve; no content on any axis.

Celestial-marriage talk affirming that mortals are literally the spiritual offspring of Heavenly Father and are copartners with God in providing bodies for waiting spirits, but it stops at mortal procreation and never asserts new spirit children begotten by exalted couples.
quote: When parents understand the purpose of their existence, that they are literally the spiritual offspring of their Father in Heaven and that they have a responsibility to provide mortal bodies for others, then they rejoice in the miracle of birth as they realize they are copartners with God in the creation of each child who comes into that home.

claim: Relief Society General President Barbara B. Smith affirms in general conference that 'O My Father' gives poetic statement to a revealed truth -- a coming reunion with our heavenly parents (plural), i.e. Mother in Heaven as revealed doctrine rather than sentiment.
quote: In the beloved Latter-day Saint hymn “O My Father,” Eliza R. Snow celebrates in words the continuity of family relationships beyond death and reminds us of a glorious reunion with our heavenly parents. Written as solace to a dear friend, Zina Huntington, who had lost her mother and father in tragic deaths, the well-known lines of this hymn give poetic statement to a great truth revealed through the Prophet Joseph Smith.

claim: McKay on inward spiritual growth, the Church as a body, and pure homes; no content on any axis (only the stock 'perfect stature of Christ' phrase).
Teaching-children talk; refers generically to God sending 'one of his spirit children' into a home, with no claim about God's nature, ancestry, or eternal increase.
quote: When our Heavenly Father sends one of his spirit children into a home, it is as if he says to the parents: “John, Mary, here is my most priceless possession—the soul of a little child.”

claim: McConkie, cataloguing the restored keys, states that the Elias restoration brings the Abrahamic promise of eternal increase -- that through celestial marriage the faithful receive an eternal posterity numberless as the sands or the stars.
quote: The man Elias brings back “the gospel of Abraham,” the great Abrahamic covenant whereby the faithful receive promises of eternal increase, promises that through celestial marriage their eternal posterity shall be as numerous as the sands upon the seashore or as the stars in heaven for multitude.

claim: Sabbath observance talk (with a prefixed Kimball condolence letter); no axis content beyond the phrase 'the offspring of God' in the letter.
Relief Society talk on strengthening families; one generic reference to children as spirit children of God.
quote: Remember, children are precious. They are spirit children of God.

claim: Sesquicentennial address on Joseph Smith as witness of the risen Christ; the only axis-adjacent material is a quotation of D&C 76:22-24 (worlds created, inhabitants begotten sons and daughters unto God), left undeveloped.
quote: “That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God”

claim: Relief Society talk on motherhood; contains the striking line that LDS mothers are 'called to mother gods,' but this is bare theosis applied to one's children -- no new spirit children, no claim about God's own past or progression.
quote: We stand in awe at Mary’s assignment to be the mother of the Lord, but we, too, have been called to mother gods.

claim: Wartime prohibition/temperance jeremiad; no content on any axis.

Whitney answers Bishop Spalding by arguing from the earthly-parent analogy that men and women may become like their Father AND their Mother in heaven, that man is 'divinity in embryo,' and that God instituted laws so the rest of the spirits might advance like Himself.
quote: Why, then, should it be deemed unphilosophic for man, the child of God, — man and woman, male and female, — to become like their Father and their Mother in heaven ?

claim: Uchtdorf, in the First Presidency, declares in general conference that we are eternal beings who have always existed and simultaneously the literal spirit children of divine, immortal, omnipotent Heavenly Parents (plural), to whom we return after this life.
quote: Brothers and sisters, we are eternal beings, without beginning and without end. We have always existed. We are the literal spirit children of divine, immortal, and omnipotent Heavenly Parents!

claim: Lost-sheep sermon on rescue and obedience; asserts literal spirit childhood and 'the substance of divinity' within us -- bare theosis with no claim about God's own nature, ancestry, progression, or eternal increase.
quote: We are created by the Almighty God. He is our Heavenly Father. We are literally His spirit children. We are made of supernal material most precious and highly refined, and thus we carry within ourselves the substance of divinity.

claim: Brief impromptu testimony; single generic reference to being spirit children of God present at the council.
quote: We know we are spirit children of God, and we were present when it was decided to form an earth here where we could come and dwell and prove ourselves worthy, by keeping the commandments, to go back into the presence of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Sill's 'three-act play' framing of premortality, mortality, and immortality; premortal spirit childhood of God is asserted generically, and he notes procreative power begins in mortality, but no claim on divine ancestry, God's progression, or eternal increase.
quote: First there was a long pre-mortal existence when we lived as the spirit children of God. This is followed by a brief mortality. Then comes an everlasting immortality.

claim: Hinckley affirms Mother in Heaven as doctrine that 'rests well' with him while ruling prayer to her out of order, and adds that we have no revealed knowledge of her -- the canonical simultaneous affirmation-and-restriction.
quote: “Logic and reason would certainly suggest that if we have a Father in Heaven, we have a Mother in Heaven. That doctrine rests well with me.”

claim: Talk on Christian love, family teaching, and caregiving; generic references to Heavenly Father's spirit children and premortal choice.
quote: Remember, our children and family members already chose to follow the Savior in their premortal realm.

claim: Monson reasons carefully from Acts 17, Hebrews 12:9, and D&C 76:24 that our spirits (not bodies) are literally God's begotten sons and daughters -- an unusually explicit statement of literal spirit birth by a Church President, but it asserts nothing about God's own ancestry, progression, eternal increase, or Heavenly Mother.
quote: Thus it is the spirit which is the offspring of God. The writer of Hebrews refers to Him as “the Father of spirits.” The spirits of all men are literally His “begotten sons and daughters.”

claim: Extended treatment of light versus darkness and the Restoration; one generic assertion that children are actually spirit children of God.
quote: Our sons and daughters should know that they are actually spirit children of God and that he loves them and wants them to succeed and be happy.

claim: Stephen L Richards, in a nationally broadcast conference address, argues that God can only be 'Our Father' as the literal progenitor and begetter of our spirits, and explicitly defends this 'procreation of spirits' against the objection that it is 'too realistic' for a Deity of ethereal nature.
quote: Some may say this procreation of spirits is too realistic, involving an assumption of personality in the Father inconsonant with the ethereal nature sometimes ascribed to Him.

claim: Talk on inner peace after the Gulf War; single generic reference to our power as spirit children of Heavenly Father.
quote: The power is in us as spirit children of our Heavenly Father.

claim: 'Be' versus 'do' parenting talk built on 3 Nephi 27:27; bare theosis (progressing to become as He is), no claim on any axis.
quote: His very plan is to help His children overcome mistakes and misdeeds and to progress to become as He *is.*

claim: Gospel-versus-Church talk; calls Elohim 'the Eternal God and Father of all our spirits' and says Christ was 'Born of a Heavenly Father, both spiritually and physically,' but develops none of the axes.
quote: Born of a Heavenly Father, both spiritually and physically, He possessed the omnipotence to overcome the world.

claim: Faith, hope, and charity talk pegged to the approaching millennium year; only 'divine potential ... as children of our Heavenly Father' in passing, no axis content.

McConkie's 'Gods of heaven' catechism states that the Father possesses all power and that there is no truth He does not know (his standing denial of continuing divine progression), while simultaneously describing Elohim as a resurrected and glorified Person and 'an Immortal Man,' and defining eternal life as life in an eternal family unit with the fulness of the Father's glory and power.
quote: He has all power, all might, and all dominion. There is no power he does not possess and no truth he does not know. Every good thing dwells in him independently in its eternal fulness. He is the Creator, Upholder, and Preserver of all things. His name is Elohim, and he is our Father in heaven, the literal Father of the spirits of all men. He has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man’s, and is in fact a resurrected and glorified Person.

claim: Priesthood-brotherhood talk; asserts generically that all human beings are literally spirit children of God and that the family unit is eternal and can enjoy eternal progression, without specifying what that progression consists of.
quote: The members of the Church are in a very unique position because they know and understand that all human beings are literally the spirit children of God, and that the family unit is eternal and can enjoy eternal progression, which should be the goal of all.

claim: Packer on Tyndale, the Church's proper name, revelation, and forgiving offense; no content on any axis.
Primary presidency talk on childlike qualities; generic references to God sending His spirit sons and daughters and to children as spirit children with divine attributes.
quote: Our Father in Heaven, in His great wisdom and love, sends His spirit sons and daughters to this earth as children.

claim: Talk urging Saints to have children; frames mortal parenthood as providing bodies for God's waiting spirit children, but makes no claim about eternal increase, God's nature, or Heavenly Mother.
quote: It is a crowning privilege of a husband and wife who are able to bear children to provide mortal bodies for these spirit children of God.

claim: Ivins rebuts a local minister by arguing from Revelation 22 that angels are resurrected men and fellow servants rather than a separate created order -- man/angel ontological continuity, but nothing about God's own ancestry, progression, or eternal increase.
quote: So, it seems that Moroni was not the first angel whom God had sent with a message to the inhabitants of the earth. It seems that he was not the first angel who had had a similar commission, and who had been a prophet, for this messenger bears witness to John that he himself was his fellow servant of the prophets and of those who keep the sayings of this book.

claim: Hanks lists the Restoration's answers to 'whence, why, whither,' including literal spirit childhood, attributes held 'in an embryonic sense,' and eventual participation with God in His creative work -- bare theosis, no eternal increase or claim about God's own past.
quote: We have assurance through the restored gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ that we are literal children of God, that we can become like him, that the ultimate of our possibility is that someday under his guidance we may even participate with him in his great creative work.

claim: Hinckley on the nature and power of personal testimony; the only axis-adjacent material is a quotation of D&C 76:22-24 and the phrase 'children with a divine birthright.'
quote: They all become our Father’s sons and daughters, children with a divine birthright.

claim: Maxwell's litany of testimony about Christ; places Jesus among the Father's premortal spirit children and affirms His superior intelligence, but makes no claim about the Father's own progression, ancestry, or eternal increase.
quote: I testify that in our first estate Jesus was the incomparable individual among all our Father’s spirit children.

claim: Report on the Vatican marriage colloquium; asserts premortal literal spirit childhood and that families are the basic units of eternity and of the government of God, but stops short of any claim about eternal increase or new spirit children.
quote: We believe that the organization and government of heaven will be built around families and extended families.

claim: In the middle of a foreordination sermon McConkie states as settled knowledge that the Eternal Father possesses all power, might, dominion, and all truth -- his standing denial of continuing divine progression -- and that God 'lives in the family unit,' with mortals endowed with power to become like Him.
quote: But we do know that our Eternal Father has all power, all might, all dominion, and all truth and that he lives in the family unit. We do know that we are his children, created in his image, endowed with power and ability to become like him.

claim: Tribute to LDS women; one generic reference to raising future generations of God's spirit children and to women as daughters of Heavenly Father.
quote: God placed within women divine qualities of strength, virtue, love, and the willingness to sacrifice to raise future generations of His spirit children.

claim: Tanner answers 'Who am I / where did I come from' from scripture; asserts premortal spirit childhood and that we 'may continue on in eternal progression,' but leaves the content of that progression unspecified and says nothing about God's own nature.
quote: Therefore, it is not commonly believed or understood that we had a premortal existence, that we are the spirit children of God, the Eternal Father, and that when we have finished our life here upon the earth we will enjoy a literal resurrection and may continue on in eternal progression.

claim: Holland closes his general conference tribute to mothers by directly addressing and thanking a Mother in Heaven alongside Eve, Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, and Mary -- an apostolic acknowledgment of her existence and 'crucial role in fulfilling the purposes of eternity,' delivered the same month as the Church's Mother in Heaven essay.
quote: To Mother Eve, to Sarah, Rebekah, and Rachel, to Mary of Nazareth, and to a Mother in Heaven, I say, “Thank you for your crucial role in fulfilling the purposes of eternity.”

claim: Report on area conferences; women are told they can be 'copartners with God' in bringing His spirit children into mortal existence, the only axis-adjacent line.
quote: They are reminded that they could have no greater responsibility or satisfying experience than to be copartners with God in the divine plan of bringing his spirit children into mortal existence, to teach them the gospel, and to help prepare them to go back into the presence of our Heavenly Father.

claim: Chastity and sex-education sermon; frames mortal procreation as making us co-creators with God and calls us His offspring learning to become like Him -- bare theosis plus mortal procreation, nothing on the eternal-increase or divine-ancestry axes.
quote: We are not animals, to dwell only in a physical world. We are the offspring of God, learning in this life to become like him.

claim: Religious-freedom address; mentions premortal spirit children and receiving 'all of the blessings our Heavenly Father has' without unpacking what those blessings are.
quote: Similarly, our exercise of agency to keep the commandments enables us to fully understand who we are and receive all of the blessings our Heavenly Father has—including the opportunity to have a body, to progress, to experience joy, to have a family, and to inherit eternal life.

claim: Priesthood-session warning about Sabbath breaking, the Word of Wisdom, and unchastity; generic assertions that we are spirit children of God and that God is a personal being in whose image we were formed.
quote: I know, as I know I stand here, that God is a personal, living God in whose image we were formed.

claim: Rulon S. Wells, arguing that eternal life is a gift no one could earn, defines that gift as 'the power of endless increase and a never ending dominion' flowing to the exalted forever -- the eternal-increase claim stated as the very content of eternal life.
quote: Oh, how idle it would be for any man to think that he can earn so great a reward as eternal life in the presence of God, which means the power of endless increase and a never ending dominion that shall flow unto us forever and forever !

claim: Dew teaches that righteous women were 'endowed premortally with the privilege of motherhood,' that motherhood is doctrine and eternal identity rather than only maternity, and that 'mother' is the word defining a woman perfected in the highest degree of the celestial kingdom who has qualified for eternal increase in posterity.
quote: For *mother* is the word that will define a righteous woman made perfect in the highest degree of the celestial kingdom, a woman who has qualified for eternal increase in posterity, wisdom, joy, and influence.

claim: Checklist talk on making a house a spiritual home; asserts in passing that the family unit continues for time and all eternity and that the home should be worthy of God's spirit children.
quote: We know that the family unit will continue for time and all eternity, but he uttered a great truth.

claim: Short message from the European Mission warning against internal contention among Saints; no content on any axis.
Voice-of-warning talk on covenants; opens with the generic affirmation that mortals are God's spirit offspring.
quote: God is in His heavens. We mortals are His spirit offspring.

claim: Kimball's iceberg-and-currents talk on family influence contains one doctrinal aside pairing the potential to become a God with our uncreated eternal existence (Abr. 3:22), but it is bare theosis plus a proof-text and develops neither.
quote: In each of us is the potentiality to become a God—pure, holy, true, influential, powerful, independent of earthly forces. We learn from the scriptures that we each have eternal existence, that we were in the beginning with God.

claim: Home teaching and family home evening address; one generic reference to generative powers being God-given for bringing God's spirit children into mortality.
quote: his generative powers are not sacred and God-given for the purpose of bringing God's spirit children into mortality, and therefore to be exercised within the limits divinely prescribed, as the gospel teaches, but they are playthings to be exploited and prostituted for the gratification of sensual and lustful desires

claim: Invitation to the less-active framed as a homeward journey; affirms premortal life in God's presence and quotes Brigham Young on God as Father of our spirits, and closes with an adaptation of 'O My Father' that keeps only the Father verses.
quote: Life is more than biology. Before we came to this earth, we lived in the presence of God. His heaven was our home. Each of us is His spirit offspring, and He is our Heavenly Father

claim: Benson argues against birth control on the ground that couples deprive waiting spirit children of bodies and that God is glorified by numerous children, but asserts no exalted-parenthood or regress claim.
quote: We believe God is glorified by having numerous children and a program of perfection for them.

claim: A priesthood-session talk on gratitude with no content on any axis.

Temple-marriage talk describing mortal parents receiving premortal spirits from Eternal Father and the celestial world as a 'kingdom of families,' but never asserts new spirit offspring for exalted couples.
quote: We must realize that marriage is designed by the Lord for a divine purpose, whereby a servant and handmaiden of the Lord may prepare themselves in righteousness to receive chosen spirits coming from our Eternal Father, and give them bodies of flesh for their mortal probation.

claim: Habit/character talk that invokes generic spirit-childhood of God and eternal life as goal; no axis-specific claim.
quote: We are spirit children of God and have born within us the power to overcome all evil practices.

claim: Eyring defines eternal life, the greatest gift of God, as living in families forever with the Father and Christ and having eternal increase.
quote: It is to live in families forever with our Heavenly Father and with Jesus Christ and to have eternal increase.

claim: James G. Duffin (Apr 1909) speaks matter-of-factly of parents rendering an account to 'our Father and Mother in heaven,' an explicit assertion of a Heavenly Mother.
quote: so that when we, as parents, give an account to our Father and Mother in heaven of the manner in which we have conducted ourselves toward the precious souls entrusted to us, how we have dealt with them, that we might bring them all with us

claim: Relief Society General President Mary Ellen Smoot names eternal increase, alongside eternal glory and continued family relationships, as one of the celestial promises motivating faithfulness.
quote: We choose to be steadfast and immovable in our faith because of the promises of eternal glory, eternal increase, and continued family relationships in the celestial kingdom.

claim: Grant quotes D&C 76:22-24 (inhabitants of the worlds are begotten sons and daughters unto God) as a testimony proof-text without developing any parentage or progression claim.
quote: that by him and through him and of him the worlds were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Sterling W. Sill closes a talk of inspirational 'transfusions' with bare theosis - that we may eventually become even as Christ is - with no exaltation mechanism or regress claim.
quote: We can follow him in his faith, we can follow him in his doctrines, we can follow him in his godliness. And we may eventually become even as he is.

claim: ElRay L. Christiansen affirms premortal spirit existence and God as literal Father of our spirits as background to a talk on Satan; no exalted-parenthood, regress, or divine-progression claim.
quote: That is, we lived in the presence of God who is literally the Father of our spirits.

claim: Eldred G. Smith describes Jehovah as the oldest spirit and creator of worlds without number, quoting J. Reuben Clark that the Lord 'has been over this course time and time again,' but the plurality-of-worlds framing carries no divine-ancestry or divine-progression claim.
quote: I repeat, our Lord is not a novice, he is not an amateur; he has been over this course time and time and time again.

claim: Temple-site narrative and a call to sustain the living prophet; no axis content.
N. Eldon Tanner invokes literal spirit-childhood of God in passing while urging leaders to discipline transgressors; no axis-specific claim.
quote: that every soul is great in the sight of God, that we are spirit children of our Heavenly Father, and he stands ready to bless us.

claim: Priesthood-worthiness talk with a single generic reference to being spirit children of God.
quote: We are the spirit children of God, holding the priesthood, in which we must honor and magnify our callings.

claim: Heber J. Grant reads his funeral remarks for Charles H. Hart; no axis content beyond a generic promise of celestial glory.

Milton R. Hunter surveys the afterlife and quotes D&C 131:1-4 on the three heavens and the loss of increase without celestial marriage, glossing 'this order of the priesthood' as the new and everlasting covenant of marriage, but adds no claim of his own about increase or spirit offspring.
quote: He may enter into the other, but that is the end of his kingdom; he cannot have an increase.

claim: Marion G. Romney on honesty; the only God-nature statement is that God cannot lie, which is off-axis.
Eyring grounds our God-given desire for independence in being spirit children of a loving Heavenly Father; generic divine-parentage framing only.
quote: We are spirit children of a loving Heavenly Father, who placed us in mortality to see if we would choose—freely choose—to keep His commandments and come unto His Beloved Son.

claim: Patriarch Eldred G. Smith opens by stating we were spirit offspring of a Father AND Mother in heaven, and that mortality lets us go through the same type of experiences our heavenly parents went through so as to become as they are - asserting the parents' own prior course, not merely theosis.
quote: We were then but spirit offspring of our Father and Mother in heaven. We all learned then that through this earth life experience we would have the opportunity of going through the same type of experiences they had done and so become as they are.

claim: Mark E. Petersen catalogs early Christian splinter sects and lists the Archontics as teaching a supreme mother in heaven, but makes no assertion or denial about a Latter-day Saint Heavenly Mother.
quote: The Archontics, who taught the existence of a supreme mother in heaven.

claim: Joseph L. Wirthlin on the sources of thought and good reading in the home; no axis content.
Primary presidency talk on kindness; no axis content.

Uchtdorf calls women spirit daughters whose spirits were fashioned by a creative God and invites them to emulate His creative work, but the creation language is rhetorical and asserts no spirit-birth mechanism or heavenly-parent chain.
quote: If you still feel incapable of creating, start small... remember that you are spirit daughters of the most creative Being in the universe. Isn't it remarkable to think that your very spirits are fashioned by an endlessly creative and eternally compassionate God?

claim: Talk on trusting Christ and staying with His Church; the only begetting language is Mosiah 5:7 spiritual rebirth in Christ, which is off-axis.
Richard G. Scott's talk on healing from abuse refers only generically to God's spirit children and the plan of happiness.
quote: He understood that some of His spirit children would use that agency improperly, causing serious problems to others.

claim: Mark E. Petersen affirms we are God's literal spirit offspring and are commanded to become like Christ, but this is bare theosis plus standard divine-parentage language with no exaltation mechanism or regress.
quote: We know that we are his children, his literal spirit offspring. We have no other source of life.

claim: Eyring appeals to our premortal life as spirit children of Heavenly Father and quotes 3 Nephi 28:10 on becoming as Christ is; bare theosis plus generic premortality.
quote: We yearn, as spirit children of our Heavenly Father, for that joy which we once had with Him in the life before this one.

claim: Uchtdorf on hope; the only progression language is human post-resurrection progress in knowledge and happiness, which is off-axis.
Lynn A. Mickelsen closes a talk on discerning truth by quoting D&C 76:22-24 as testimony; the 'begotten sons and daughters unto God' line is quoted without comment.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Hinckley on tithing, Church callings, good reading, and missionary preparation; no axis content.
Eyring frames mortality as the test by which spirit children become more like Heavenly Father and Christ; bare theosis only.
quote: Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ know and love you. They want you to return to Them and become like Them.

claim: Joseph L. Wirthlin on obedience and the Saints' example to the world; no axis content.

William K. Jackson states we are literally spirit children of heavenly parents as grounds for equal worth; this is the standard post-1995 proclamation formula with no elaboration on heavenly parenthood.
quote: We are, after all, brothers and sisters, spirit children of our heavenly parents—literally.

claim: Derek A. Cuthbert's ten aspects of maturity include a generic reference to children as God's spirit children entrusted to parents.
quote: Our sons, our daughters, are his spirit children whom he expects us to love and cherish, teach and lead.

claim: Marion G. Romney argues from the universal law that reproducing offspring reach the likeness of their parents that God's literal spirit offspring will reach the status of their heavenly parents - man is 'a God in embryo' - and states that God fathers man's spirit exactly as an earthly father fathers the body.
quote: This is so because they know that it is the universal law of nature in the plant, animal, and human worlds for reproducing offspring to reach in final maturity the likeness of their parents. They reason that the same law is in force with respect to the offspring of God. Their objective is, therefore, to someday be like their heavenly parents.

claim: Widtsoe on tolerance, allegiance to truth, and no compromise with error; no axis content despite Widtsoe being a key figure elsewhere.
Oaks grounds the command to love enemies in the reality that all mortals are children of God; generic divine-parentage only.
quote: The Savior's teaching to love our enemies is based on the reality that all mortals are beloved children of God.

claim: Charles H. Hart testifies of the resurrection and quotes D&C 76:22-24 in full, including the begotten sons and daughters line, without comment on it.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Relief Society General President Barbara B. Smith states that men and women alone among God's creations are to become as He is, and quotes Kimball on rearing the spirit children of our Father in Heaven; bare theosis.
quote: Of all the creations of God, men and women are the ones that are to become as he is. We are his children.

claim: Delbert L. Stapley teaches that sealed children become the parents' very own throughout eternity, framed as joint-heirship with Christ in all the Father possesses including His own spirit children - eternal parenthood of existing children, not new spirit offspring or increase.
quote: This knowledge adds joy, happiness, and glory to joint-heirship with Christ in all that the Father possesses, even the gift of his own spirit children.

claim: Christofferson expounds the three degrees of glory from D&C 76 and quotes verse 24, but says nothing about increase, celestial marriage, or heavenly parenthood in the celestial kingdom.
quote: It is the 'testimony, last of all,' given by the Prophet Joseph Smith, 'that he lives! ... That he is the Only Begotten of the Father—that by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.'

claim: Hinckley's Easter testimony of the Resurrection plus a report on African famine relief; D&C 76:22-24 is quoted as testimony without comment on its parentage clause.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Howard W. Hunter on agency, morality, fear, duty, and love; refers generically to premortal spirit children of the Father.
quote: Even in the preexistence the spirit children of the father had their choice.

claim: David O. McKay's Easter discourse on the literal Resurrection; quotes D&C 76:22-24 as the latter-day witness without commenting on divine parentage.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Joseph F. Merrill names eternal progression as a basic doctrine but develops only that we are spirit children who possess our Father's attributes in embryo; no claim about God's own progression or ancestry.
quote: I wish to give emphasis to the fact that since we are spirit children of our Father in heaven it is perfectly natural that we should possess at least in embryo and microscopic quantities the attributes of our Father.

claim: Steven D. Bangerter teaches premortal foreordination and quotes President Nelson that we are literally spirit children of God with divine potential; standard divine-nature language only.
quote: My dear friends, you are literally spirit children of God. ... Make no mistake about it: Your potential is divine.

claim: Joseph F. Merrill on Sabbath observance, quoting D&C 59, Joseph F. Smith, and the 1928 First Presidency editorial; no axis content.
Ezra Taft Benson on free agency, the Constitution, and Communism; premortal spirit children and 'Godlike men' appear only as framing.
quote: This master plan, if lived, will build men of character, men of strength, men of deep spirituality, Godlike men.

claim: Benson's missionary-work talk refers only generically to all people as our Heavenly Father's children.
quote: Hearts of leaders of nations must be softened, doors of nations opened, false ideologies overcome, and the gospel presented to all our Heavenly Father's children.

claim: Faust on judgment, mercy, and faith; quotes Moses 1:39 but makes no claim on any axis.
Eyring on building faith in the home and eternal sealing; refers generically to Heavenly Father's love for us, His spirit children.
quote: I know that Heavenly Father loves us, His spirit children, with a perfect love.

claim: David B. Haight's Easter narrative of the Resurrection appearances, closing with D&C 76:19-24 quoted without comment on divine parentage.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: L. Tom Perry quotes Spencer W. Kimball in general conference teaching that Peter and John's righteous lives opened the door to godhood, creation of worlds, and eternal increase - and that for that work they would eventually need a total knowledge of the sciences, implying continued acquisition of knowledge after deification.
quote: Their righteous lives opened the door to godhood for them and creation of worlds with eternal increase. For this they would probably need, eventually, a total knowledge of the sciences.

claim: Hinckley's closing conference remarks on obedience, tithing, fasting, and service; no axis content.
Derek A. Cuthbert's ten investigator questions include the purpose of life, answered with generic premortal spirit-childhood and eternal families; no exaltation mechanism or regress.
quote: In that period of time, which we call the premortal existence, we lived with God as his spirit children.

claim: Joseph Fielding Smith reads Orson Pratt's Millennial Star warning into general conference, framing the celestial stakes as an 'endless increase of immortal lives' versus being left a servant-angel with 'no means of enlarging yourselves.'
quote: You forfeit your right to an endless increase of immortal lives.

claim: Easter sermon on the reality and universality of the Resurrection; no material on divine ancestry, divine progression, or eternal increase.
Generic spirit-child parentage plus bare theosis (God will 'share all He has and all He is' and we 'ultimately become like Him'), with no mechanism, no new spirit children, and no backward chain.
quote: The relationship God seeks with each spirit child is one so close and personal that He will be able to share all He has and all He is.

claim: Defense of two Book of Mormon passages (Alma 7:10 'at Jerusalem'; Mosiah 15 Christ as Father and Son); the fatherhood discussed is Christ's spiritual begetting of the redeemed, not divine ancestry.
