Priesthood address on standing against crime and gangs; only incidental reference to God's 'strongest spirit children.'
Bare theosis in a devotional frame ('become like Them'), plus the standard premortal-spirit-children reference with Christ as firstborn; nothing on mechanism or regress.
quote: Jesus volunteered to be our Savior and Redeemer so that we could become like Them and return to Their presence.

claim: Crisply worded but bare theosis ('become all that He is') tied to covenant birthright; no new spirit children, no progression of God, no backward chain.
quote: It would be easy for Heavenly Father to simply give you all that He has. His desire is to help you become all that He is.

claim: Address on worldly sin, labor strikes, and a re-reading of the 1936 First Presidency warning against communism; no axis content.
Wartime address on liberty as a spiritual quality and the internal decay of nations; no axis content.
History of the laws of war from Grotius forward and a protest against the atomic bomb and biological weapons; no axis content.
Youth address on premortal faith and gathering Israel; premortal spirit sonship is invoked only as identity motivation, with no theosis or increase claim.

Reports that outside thinkers now sense man 'may become like his Father in Heaven' and that 'within man is an embryotic Deity' — vivid theosis phrasing, but it stays on the A axis with no offspring, mechanism, or backward chain.
quote: Many understand the fact that like begets like, and that within man is an embryotic Deity.

claim: Address on faith, works, and progress (a smoking-cessation interview anecdote); 'we are his spirit children' is the only incidental touch.

Penrose defines 'eternal lives' as 'perpetual increase of posterity, worlds without end,' and separately describes the Father as understanding our emotions 'having passed through the experiences that we are now passing through' — i.e. God's own past mortal experience.
quote: That means more than life, more than mere existence, it means perpetual increase of posterity, worlds without end, and these blessings shall be ours if we will prove faithful to that which we have received of the Lord, and this is what we are for in the Church, every one of us, that is our duty, that is what we are on the earth for, to build up this Latter-day kingdom, to lead the inhabitants of the earth up to God, to bring them nearer to him so that they will be obedient in their hearts and be willing to obey his commandments and walk in his ways and be prepared for the glorious future that lies before them.

claim: Bare theosis in the 'eternal parents' idiom — God's offspring may hope to become like them — with no offspring mechanism, no Heavenly Mother named, and no backward chain.
quote: I know that God lives, that we were created in his image, and that by obeying the principles of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the offspring of God may eventually hope to become like their eternal parents.

claim: Seven-pillars self-improvement sermon; touches theosis only in the generic claim that we are endowed with God's attributes for development.
quote: For we are not only created in the image of God, but we have been endowed with a set of his attributes, the development of which is one of the purposes for which we live.

claim: Address on love in the home, parental responsibility, and modest dress; only a quoted mother's letter mentions 'You are the spirit children of God.'
Stewardship-of-wealth and tithing address; the Brigham Young 'eternal increase' quotation is explicitly about talent, strength, intellect, and earthly wealth, not posterity.
Second-person narrative retelling of Joseph Smith's life and martyrdom, closing with D&C 76:22-24; no axis content.
Cites D&C 76:58-59 ('they are gods') and Abraham 3:26 in a catena on LDS education; bare theosis with no mechanism, offspring, or regress.
quote: “Wherefore, as it is written, they are gods, even the sons of God—Wherefore, all things are theirs. …”

claim: Missionary-work and Book of Mormon testimony address; no axis content.
Closing remarks summarize conference as focused on 'His Father's plan for our eternal increase and joy' — the euphemism only, with no content behind it.
quote: The Spirit of the Lord has inspired all of us to concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies on the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ and His Father’s plan for our eternal increase and joy.

claim: Brief remarks on radio reception of conference plus a recitation of D&C 76:22-24; no axis content.

Long statistical/testimony address; the only axis contact is the anthropomorphic premise that the First Vision showed 'God himself, a glorified man' — corporeality asserted, but no past mortality, Father-of-the-Father, or progression claim.
quote: The very foundation of the Church rests upon the fact that a boy not yet 15 years of age saw God himself, a glorified man, beyond the power of any individual to describe, and that God introduced Jesus Christ to this boy.

claim: Missionary-work and material-prudence address with a warning about immorality; no axis content.
Address on adult example, pornography, and eroding moral standards; only the incidental 'we are his spirit children.'
Faith-without-works exhortation plus a recitation of D&C 76:22-24; no axis content.
Polemic for a corporeal, personal God against creedal abstraction — including the striking insistence that God is not 'sexless' — but no claim about God's own past, progression, or parentage.
quote: There are those who through their teachings would deprive God of his body, deny his personality, take away his senses, faculties, and feelings. They would leave him sexless, thoughtless, and helpless, without boundaries, shape, identity, or location.

claim: Apologetic on a personal God, the dual nature of man, and the eternal home; closes with the 'endless increase … worlds without end' formula but supplies no content behind it.
quote: This gospel is the power of God unto salvation, the means for salvation, endless joy, endless increase, happiness and progress forever, worlds without end.

claim: Fundamentalist-vs-modernist defense of miracles plus Abraham 3 premortality; asserts a plurality of worlds created and redeemed by the same God and man's capacity for 'endless increase,' but no chain of Gods and no offspring mechanism.
quote: This earth was created, not out of nothing, as antiquated theology asserts; but out of eternal spirit and eternal element; and it is but one of millions like it that have been created, peopled and redeemed by the same All-wise God, who has placed his children here, primarily to give their spirits bodies, that they might become souls, capable of endless increase and advancement; also that it might be seen whether they would do all that the Lord requires at their hands.

claim: Historical survey of Church service — Missouri expulsions, the 1849 missions, the down-and-back ox trains, the Black Hawk War; no axis content.
Missionary work, the Word of Wisdom, and the Josiah Quincy tribute to Joseph Smith; no axis content.

Defines the celestial reward as 'the power of endless increase, worlds without end' and glosses 'eternal lives' as 'endless increase,' with humans 'born' of God in a 'spirit birth' and destined 'to be made exactly like the Father.' (Note: filename says Lund but the vault frontmatter credits Charles W. Penrose, 1914-10-04.)
quote: ...then we can draw from the highest heights and from the lowest depths of all parts of God's great universe everything that will contribute to joy, to pleasure, to progress and development, to knowledge, to wisdom, to power, and to dominion above all, if we have that glorious gift of celestial glory, the power of endless increase, worlds without end. And this is what we Latter-day Saints are after, what we are trying to get, this fulness of glory and joy and power and dominion ; in other words, to be made exactly like the Father.

claim: Plan-of-salvation address (Apollo 13 framing) that quotes 1 Cor 8:5 'there be gods many, and lords many' and refers to 'the council meeting of Gods,' but only to distinguish the Father's and Son's roles — no backward chain and no progression claim.
quote: Understanding this principle in the plan of the government of God, we are given a glimpse of the council meeting of Gods, as briefly recorded in revelations to ancient prophets.

claim: Crisp but bare theosis — the gospel is 'destined to make … of man, a god,' with God's spirit children advancing to 'become like him'; no offspring mechanism, no divine ancestry, no progression of God.
quote: And it is destined to make of this earth, a heaven; and of man, a god.

claim: Reconciles God's personal corporeality with divine immanence via the light-of-Christ doctrine; the corporeality premise only, with nothing on ancestry, progression, or increase.
Aaronic Priesthood address to his grandsons about resisting temptation; only the incidental 'all of us are spirit children of God.'

Oath-and-covenant sermon citing D&C 84:38 ('all that my Father hath'), 2 Peter 1:4 ('partakers of the divine nature'), and 3 Nephi 27:27 ('even as I am') — bare theosis throughout, and rebirth into God's family is by baptism, not spirit begetting.
quote: Now brethren, I have spoken only of the first step along the path of progression which will yield eventually a fullness of the blessings which God the Father has in store for us if we are willing to pay the price attached to those blessings.

claim: Eldred G. Smith argues from the resurrection that God the Father must Himself have passed through mortality and been resurrected — explicitly on 'some previous earth in the long distant past' — reasoning that man could not otherwise accomplish what God has not.
quote: I worship my God who is my Father in heaven, the Father of my spirit, a resurrected, glorified, perfected man, not resurrected from this earth, no, but from some previous earth in the long distant past.

claim: Gratitude and moral-decline address; touches theosis only in the family-home-evening line that children are taught they have 'that spark of divinity' enabling them 'to reach immortal heights.'
quote: They are taught that we are the children of God and that as his children we have that spark of divinity in us which makes it possible for us to reach immortal heights by living according to the teachings of the gospel of his Son Jesus Christ.

claim: Restoration apologetics (the Catholic-or-Mormon dilemma, apostasy proof-texts) closing with D&C 76:19-24; no axis content.
Gratitude for work and Church organization statistics, with the 'boost spirit' and old-frog anecdotes; no axis content.
Anti-divorce sermon on eternal marriage; uses the 'eternal increase and build a kingdom' formula for temple-sealed couples but supplies no content behind it — no new spirit children, no mechanism.
quote: ...because it means that those who enter into such a covenant shall continue after death and have eternal increase and build a kingdom.

claim: Defense of Mormonism as an educational institution (Relief Society, Sunday School, MIA, Religion Class); no axis content.
Church of the Air radio address on the reality of a personal God against modern false gods; 'Man is the offspring of God' is the only incidental touch.

Argues against pre-Adamite language in Church curriculum and for Adam as the first man and literal son of God who 'fell' rather than evolved; nothing on divine ancestry, God's progression, or increase.
Testimony-by-the-Holy-Ghost epistemology and a warning about Satan's influence in postwar politics; the Godhead-in-whose-image-man-is-made premise only.
Priesthood-session anecdotes on standing for the right, closing with bare theosis — spirit children with 'the potential to make it possible to be like him.'
quote: May we as individuals have the determination, the courage, the ability to stand up and do those things which we know are right, realizing that we are the spirit children of God, with the potential to make it possible to be like him if we will follow his teachings and keep his commandments.

claim: Address on self-control and 'school thy feelings,' using Lindbergh's character checklist and Christ as ideal; no axis content.

'Divine spark' address: God is the literal Father of our spirits, we inherit divine attributes, and eternal progression continues through all eternity — but the progression in view is man's, not God's, and there is no offspring or ancestry claim.
quote: This Church teaches the value and necessity of eternal progression. We progressed in the preexistence, and it is our responsibility and opportunity to progress in this estate and throughout all eternity.

claim: Lists Joseph Smith's achievements, including the sealing covenant that secures couples 'the power of eternal increase and the blessing of endless lives' — the formula only, with no explanation of what increase consists of.
quote: ...thus securing to them the power of eternal increase and the blessing of endless lives, and emphasizing, as no earthly covenant alone could do, the sanctity of the marriage bond...

claim: Annual statistics, then an address on Elijah, the Kirtland restoration of the sealing keys, and genealogical work for the dead; no axis content.
Foreordination of prophets in the grand council and Joseph Smith as a seer 'great like unto Moses'; premortal spirit sonship is background only, with no theosis, increase, or ancestry claim.

Argues from 'like begets like' that humans are 'of the race of the Gods' and that inherited divine attributes may reach 'God-like proportions' hereafter — vivid, but still theosis-by-inheritance with no backward chain, no offspring, and no progression of God.
quote: Since in the world of life, like begets like, it must follow that in bodily form we are like our Father in heaven. Hence, it cannot be true that we are brutes or descendants of beasts; we are of the race of the Gods.

claim: Easter address on the resurrection as the foundation of five gospel principles (Fatherhood of God, sonship of Christ, immortality, brotherhood, standards); the Fatherhood section argues only for a personal God.

Grant's farewell counsel on virtue, prayer, and the Constitution; only axis brush is a quotation of D&C 76:22-24 on worlds created by Christ whose inhabitants are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Short testimony built entirely of D&C 76 quotations; the only axis-adjacent line is the same 'worlds are and were created' verse, with no commentary.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Brown closes an anti-divorce address by promising the temple-sealed that beyond mortal posterity they receive 'eternal increase' hereafter, distinguishing posterity here from increase in the celestial glory.
quote: You shall have joy in your posterity here, eternal family union and association hereafter, immortality, eternal life, and eternal increase.

claim: Penrose says the inhabitants of the created worlds are begotten sons and daughters unto God whatever their 'immediate progenitors' may have been (all centering up to the one Eternal Father), and closes by promising the faithful endless increase of dominions and posterity.
quote: And of the increase of our glory and our happiness and our peace and our dominions and our posterity, there will be no end.

claim: Travelogue and testimony address; the only axis contact is another recitation of D&C 76:22-24 and repeated insistence on the individuality and personality of God, with no progression, ancestry, or spirit-offspring claim.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Knight reads an anti-Mormon tract's list of 'awful doctrines' -- that God once was as we are, that we may become what God now is, and that we have a Heavenly Mother -- and endorses the whole list ironically from the conference pulpit.
quote: They teach that God once was as we are now. and that we may become what God is now. They teach that we have a heavenly Father and a heavenly Mother.

claim: Radio, semiannual Church statistics, and D&C 121 counsel; the only axis contact is another reading of D&C 76:22-24 with no doctrinal elaboration.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds. are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: The Presiding Patriarch states as settled knowledge that Latter-day Saints have a Mother in heaven as well as a Father, tied to sealing power binding families eternally.
quote: We: do not wander in our minds, but we know, like little children, that we have a father, and a mother in heaven, and that we have our loved ones there.

claim: Home industry, Church birth/death statistics, and Word of Wisdom counsel; procreation is discussed only as a mortal commandment, with no eternal-increase or divine-parentage content.
quote: To beget children, and rear them in the fear and admonition of the Lord, is one of the chief purposes of our being.

claim: Gratitude address affirming premortal existence and eternal family sealing, closing with a bare benedictory triad of 'eternal life, eternal progress, eternal increase' that is never unpacked.
quote: and who offers us the blessings of eternal life, eternal progress, eternal increase in his celestial kingdom.

claim: Purely administrative Sunday School instruction on grading pupils by age and ability; no doctrinal content of any kind.
quote: The ages assigned are only suggestive.

claim: Brief closing testimony resting on D&C 76's witness of the risen Christ; only axis contact is the created-worlds verse, quoted without comment.
quote: that by Him and through Him and of Him the worlds are and were created and the inhabitants thereof, and begotten sons and daughters of God.

claim: Priesthood-session address against divorce; frames the home as the institution that receives the Father's spirit children into mortality, but says nothing about exalted couples begetting new spirit offspring.
quote: this sacred institution, ordained of the Lord, is charged with the primary responsibility for receiving the spirit children of the Father, tabernacled in the flesh, and then to nurture, train and develop these children in mortality, and then return them to the Celestial presence whence they came.

claim: Kimball's 'platform of faith' and jeremiad against 'half-way men'; the only axis brush is a bare statement of human likeness to a perfect God.
quote: God rises above men. We are like Him, but He is perfect and that is why I have faith in Him, knowing that I will be rewarded for all of my faithful labors, and for all of my mistakes I will have to be resposible.

claim: Counsel on moderation, thrift, debt, automobiles, and the principle of consecration; no theological content on any axis.
quote: Moderation begets tolerance, and tolerance lies at the foundation of sympathy and charity.

claim: Rich teaches man is a 'trinity' -- an everlasting intelligence placed inside a spirit body that was literally born to a Father AND a Mother in heaven, which was then placed in a mortal tabernacle.
quote: The spirit that God places within this tabernacle was not created in this sphere, it was created yonder, in the presence of our Father and our Mother in heaven. When that spirit tabernacle was born unto them, there was a light, there was an intelligence placed within it that existed from everlasting.

claim: Mission-president report on anti-Mormon prejudice, missionary sacrifice, tithing, and fast offerings; the nearest doctrinal statement is that the Father is a tangible being, which touches no axis.
quote: The world needs the testimony that Jesus is in very deed the Christ, and that our Father in heaven is a reality, a tangible being and not a myth.

claim: Centennial publicity report and testimony; affirms God is the Father of our spirits and again quotes D&C 76:22-24, with no elaboration on ancestry, progression, or increase.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Robinson quotes the Snow couplet from the conference pulpit -- attributing it to Joseph Smith -- and grounds it in a 'like begets like' argument from God's literal fatherhood.
quote: So the Prophet Joseph Smith, in this age, has added to this truth by the assertion that "As man is God once was, and that as He is man may become," because He is our Father, and like begets like, and inherent within us are the attributes of divinity that shall lead us into perfection, which Christ intended His Saints to attain unto.

claim: McKay on individual testimony as the source of the Church's vitality, plus a plea for charity during election season; no axis content.
quote: The secret lies in the testimony possessed by each individual who is faithful in the membership of the Church of Christ, that the gospel consists of correct principles.

claim: Argument against 'spiritualizing' the Bible and for literal bodily resurrection and scripture study; no divine-ancestry, progression, or increase content.
quote: He will accept the declaration of the Holy Scriptures that the Lord Jesus Christ was born of a woman, literally and naturally, like all other men have been born, and will not attempt, as some do, to spiritualize the birth of the Lord Jesus Christ.

claim: Roberts on conference overflow, revelation-by-inquiry, and the mental laziness of the Seventies; eternal marriage appears only as an example of revelation given in answer to a question.
quote: The great law of marriage, the system which includes the eternity of the marriage covenant, one of the most splendid principles ever revealed unto the children of men -- the fact that the union between husband and wife, the holy family relations of children and parents, this great central, primary truth concerning these relationships and their continuance in time and in eternity, came in response to earnest inquiry on the part of the Prophet.

claim: Restoration apologetic and a train-conversation anecdote; the doctrinal payload is bare theosis -- attributes of Deity inherent in man, needing only time to develop -- with no ancestry, increase, or progression claim.
quote: telling her that inherent within us are the attributes of Deity, and that we only lack the time and opportunity to develop these things to become like the Father.

claim: Penrose on parental duty and spiritual warfare; corrects the folk notion that Lucifer was the Firstborn, affirms universal premortal divine sonship, and closes with the formulaic promise of 'endless increase' with dominions and kingdoms, but never unpacks increase into spirit offspring.
quote: and He has sent us down here on the earth for a time and a season, that we may be proven, tested and tried, to see what we are worthy of, so that in the future we may be placed where we belong, and have glory, immortality and endless increase, with dominions, and kingdoms, and principalities and powers forever, if we are fit to have them

claim: Defense of Christ's literal divinity and the continuity of individual identity past death; quotes D&C 76:24 and D&C 93 on Christ as Firstborn, but makes no claim about divine ancestry, progression, or eternal increase.
quote: and they learned that "By Him and through Him, and of Him the worlds were made, and the inhabitants thereof were begotten sons and daughters unto God."

claim: Woodruff frames mortality as self-exile from a premortal home shared with a Father AND a Mother in heaven.
quote: We have left our Father and Mother in heaven, become self-exiled from the associations of our primeval existence, and have come down here on earth in obedience to the will of God, for a wise purpose He has in view.

claim: Reading of the D&C 135 martyrdom account plus the standard D&C 76 testimony passage; no axis claim beyond the created-worlds verse.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Talmage argues from Christ's 'what I have seen my Father do' that the Eternal Father was once a Man who progressed by conquest over sin and death to Godship, quotes the Snow couplet, and says we may become like our Eternal Father AND Eternal Mother.
quote: the Father of His spirit and the Father of His body, was once a Man, and has progressed, not by any favor but by the right of conquest over sin, and over death, to His present position of priesthood and power, of Godship and Godliness, as the Supreme Being whom we all profess to worship.

claim: Penrose says Christ was the Father's literal first-born in the spirit and that the rest of us 'were born afterwards in the spirit,' with the Father's attributes transmitted to us by generation; he also reads D&C 76:24 as a revelation that other worlds are inhabited.
quote: How was He brought forth -- as an individual, conscious, thinking, intelligent spirit with agency? Why, He was begotten of the Father, and therefore the attributes of the Father came to Him by generation, and so to us, measurably, every one of us

claim: Conversion narrative and praise of the Wesleys; ends with the stock formula 'glory, immortality and eternal increase' as a reward for obedience, with no elaboration.
quote: he will be blessed and have joy in this life, and glory, immortality and eternal increase will be added to him in the world to come.

claim: Practical stake-president counsel on reverence in chapels; the doctrinal frame is the oath-and-covenant promise that 'all that our Father has may be ours' plus the priesthood creating worlds without number -- bare theosis.
quote: Lastly, if we are faithful to our Priesthood and magnify our callings, we may be sanctified, so we are told, by the spirit unto the renewing of our bodies, and all that our Father has may be ours.

claim: Polemic against the Reorganized Church and testimony of fulfilled prophecy; closes with the same D&C 76 passage, unelaborated.
quote: That by him and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Meditation on learning, ancient religions, and the Prophet's Hebrew school; God appears only as Creator and Father of mankind, with no axis content.
quote: We all agreed that nothing surpasses the first chapter of Genesis in sheer beauty, for it is the divine truth that God lives and is the Creator of heaven and earth and is the Father of mankind.

claim: Sill's 'We believe in God' success sermon; states God is literally the Father of our spirits and that offspring may become like the parent, which is bare theosis with no further specification.
quote: We mean that we understand something about the kind of being he is, that he is literally the Father of our spirits, and, according to the great law of the universe, the offspring may sometime become like the parent.

claim: Ivins says the sealed couple -- not the individually endowed man -- receives 'the power of eternal increase,' which he identifies explicitly as an attribute of Godhood.
quote: The greatest result of such living is the union of a man and a woman for time and eternity, sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise, with the power of eternal increase, an attribute of Godhood.

claim: Defines spirituality as beginning with the recognition of divine sonship; asserts we are spiritually born of God and Christ is our Elder Brother, but goes no further.
quote: The recognition that we are the sons and daughters of God, spiritually born of him, it seems to me, is a starting place if you are going to try to define spirituality.

claim: Counsel to students on keeping faith against scientific skepticism; entirely epistemological, with no claim about God's nature, ancestry, progression, or eternal increase.
quote: One may secure faith by doing the things that he would do and being the kind of a person that he would be if he had faith.

claim: Merrill grounds deification in literal spirit parentage plus the biological law that like begets like -- we hold the Father's attributes 'in embryo' -- and cites only the forward half of the Snow couplet, calling it the law of eternal progression.
quote: We are his children, literally his spirit children, and in the great law of the universe, in the biological field, at any rate, we have found -- this has been revealed to us by scientific research -- that like begets like. As children of our Father in Heaven we possess, in embryo, at least, his attributes.

claim: Almost entirely administrative minutes (sustainings, tithing, adobes, canyon timber), but Brigham Young's Oct 8 priesthood address -- preserved here in both Bullock's minutes and a revised fair copy -- asserts that the Father literally begat Christ's mortal body himself, without the aid of any man; note this is divine physical siring, not the B4 spirit-birth mechanism, so grade with care.
quote: Paul [struck: knew that God Almighty] had all the qualifications [struck: of a man ... he had power to bring forth his only begotten Son] to beget his Son in the Flesh & [struck: had the power to beget the body without asking aid of any man to do it for him, he had the qualification in him], he had an eternity of qualifications far beyond [struck: your] ^[their] conceptions or imagination.

claim: Church-wide anti-liquor and anti-tobacco campaign report; repeats Merrill's 'spirit children ... in embryo his attributes' formula in a single incidental sentence with none of the 1937 argument behind it.
quote: We are spirit children of the Father and possess in embryo his attributes.

claim: Conference-attendance anecdotes, welfare report, and long readings from D&C 76 and 121; no axis claim beyond the created-worlds verse.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Radio address on the foundations of peace; asserts man's 'divine pedigree' -- begotten of God, with the Father in the beginning -- and eternal progress toward God's likeness, but keeps it at the level of generic divine sonship.
quote: Man is a very son of God, begotten of God; he was with the Father in the beginning. Since he is of a divine pedigree, with a spark of divinity within him, he rises immeasurably in the world of things.

claim: Call for the world to acknowledge God, stressing the first commandment that 'there is one God,' and rehearsing the First Vision, Kirtland, and D&C 76 appearances; monotheistic emphasis is exhortative, not a denial of plurality.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: Premortal council, the war in heaven, and a racial explanation of the priesthood restriction; the only axis contact is the oath-and-covenant promise that all the Father has shall be given to the faithful -- bare theosis.
quote: He has promised the male membership of his Church who shall receive the Priesthood, that if we will magnify that Priesthood -- and that means live righteous lives, lives of service to God and to our fellow men -- all that he has shall be given unto us, and the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof.

claim: Argument that Christianity failed only because Christians did, tracing apostasy to the Greek philosophizing of plain apostolic testimony; quotes D&C 76:19-24 as the modern witness, with no axis elaboration.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.

claim: An 'invitation to the kingdom' addressed to common men, women, and youth; describes sealed parents as priest and priestess receiving the Father's spirit children into mortality and projecting the home into eternity, but claims no eternal increase or divine parenthood for them.
quote: As a priest and priestess in the temple of the home, it is their high privilege to receive the spirit children of our Eternal Father into mortality; then to nurture, train, and lead these chosen ones coming to their home back into the eternal presence whence they came.

claim: Counsel to youth on gaining, keeping, and reinforcing a personal testimony, plus a plea to the inactive to return; no axis content.
quote: Testimony inspires testimony; conviction begets conviction.

claim: Romney's 'The Living and True God' argues from 'like begets like' that spirit sons will grow up to be like their Father, and states outright that God himself attained perfection through that same process, quoting the Snow couplet as the Church's peculiar teaching.
quote: As a matter of fact, he taught that through this process God himself attained perfection.

claim: Sill's 'greatest days' sermon on premortality, resurrection, and judgment; affirms that our spirits were begotten of God and argues hard that the Father must have a body, but stops short of saying He was once mortal.
quote: Our spirits were begotten of God in heaven, and one of the most important purposes of our mortal lives is to be "added upon" with a body of flesh and bones.

claim: Catalogue of scriptural witnesses that Jesus is the Christ, addressed to doubting youth; ends with D&C 76:22-24 quoted as testimony only.
quote: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
